1.62.s:
sumanturuvāca
athānyaṃ sarahasyaṃ tu saṃvādaṃ vacmi te'khilam .
sūryasya diṇḍinā sārdhaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam . . 1
1.62.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
अथान्यं सरहस्यं तु संवादं वच्मि तेऽखिलम् ।
सूर्यस्य दिण्डिना सार्धं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥ 1
1.62.m:
Sumantu said:
Now I shall tell you another entire esoteric dialogue,
between the Sun and Diṇḍi, which destroys all sins.

1.62.s:
brahmahatyābhibhūtastu parā diṃḍirmahātapāḥ .
ārādhanāya devasya stotraṃ cakre mahātmanaḥ . . 2
1.62.d:
ब्रह्महत्याभिभूतस्तु परा दिंडिर्महातपाः ।
आराधनाय देवस्य स्तोत्रं चक्रे महात्मनः ॥ 2
1.62.m:
Diṇḍi of great austerities, having been overcome by the sin of killing a brāhmaṇa,
composed a hymn of praise for the worship of the noble god.

1.62.s:
śrutvā tasyārthataḥ stotraṃ tutoṣa bhagavānraviḥ .
uvāca devadevastaṃ diṇḍinaṃ gaṇanāyakam . . 3
1.62.d:
श्रुत्वा तस्यार्थतः स्तोत्रं तुतोष भगवान्रविः ।
उवाच देवदेवस्तं दिण्डिनं गणनायकम् ॥ 3
1.62.m:
Having heard his hymn full of meaning, the blessed Sun was pleased;
the god of gods said to Diṇḍi, the leader of the gaṇas:

1.62.s:
āditya uvāca
haṃta diṇḍe prasanno'smi bhaktyā stotreṇa te'nagha1 .
varaṃ vṛṇīṣva dharmajña yatte manasi vartate . . 4
1.62.d:
आदित्य उवाच
हंत दिण्डे प्रसन्नोऽस्मि भक्त्या स्तोत्रेण तेऽनघ1 ।
वरं वृणीष्व धर्मज्ञ यत्ते मनसि वर्तते ॥ 4
1.62.m:
The Sun said:
'Well, Diṇḍi, I am pleased with your devotion and hymn, O sinless one!
Choose a boon, O knower of righteousness, whatever is in your mind.'

1.62.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
eṣa eva varaḥ ślāghyo yatprāpto'si mamāntikam .
tvaddarśanamapuṇyānāṃ svapneṣvapi ca durlabham . . 5
1.62.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
एष एव वरः श्लाघ्यो यत्प्राप्तोऽसि ममान्तिकम् ।
त्वद्दर्शनमपुण्यानां स्वप्नेष्वपि च दुर्लभम् ॥ 5
1.62.m:
Diṇḍi said:
'This alone is a praiseworthy boon, that you have come into my presence.
The sight of you is difficult to obtain even in dreams for the unvirtuous.

1.62.s:
yathaiṣā brahmahatyā me āgatā lokagarhitā .
bhavāñjānāti sarveśo hadisthaḥ sarvadehinām . . 6
1.62.d:
यथैषा ब्रह्महत्या मे आगता लोकगर्हिता ।
भवाञ्जानाति सर्वेशो हदिस्थः सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥ 6
1.62.m:
How this killing of a brāhmaṇa, condemned by the world, came upon me,
you know, O lord of all, residing in the heart of all embodied beings.

1.62.s:
tvatprasādānmameśāna3 nāśamāśu prayātu vai .
tathā ca duritaṃ sarvaṃ yaccānyallokagarhitam . . 7
1.62.d:
त्वत्प्रसादान्ममेशान3 नाशमाशु प्रयातु वै ।
तथा च दुरितं सर्वं यच्चान्यल्लोकगर्हितम् ॥ 7
1.62.m:
By your grace, O Lord, let it indeed swiftly go to destruction,
and likewise all wickedness and whatever else is condemned by the world.

1.62.s:
yadyadicchāmyahaṃ tattatsarvamastu divaspate .
etenaivānumānena prasanno bhagavanniti . . 8
1.62.d:
यद्यदिच्छाम्यहं तत्तत्सर्वमस्तु दिवस्पते ।
एतेनैवानुमानेन प्रसन्नो भगवन्निति ॥ 8
1.62.m:
Whatever I desire, let all that come to pass, O Lord of the sky!
By this very inference, [I know] the Lord is pleased with me.

1.62.s:
jñātaṃ mayā hi mārtaṇḍe nāprasanne vibhūtayaḥ .
evaṃ sarvasukhāhlādamadhyastho'pi hi bhānumān . . 9
1.62.d:
ज्ञातं मया हि मार्तण्डे नाप्रसन्ने विभूतयः ।
एवं सर्वसुखाह्लादमध्यस्थोऽपि हि भानुमान् ॥ 9
1.62.m:
For it is known by me that when Mārtaṇḍa is not pleased, there are no prosperities.
Though standing in the midst of joy from all pleasures, the Sun,

1.62.s:
tvaṃ māmagādhe saṃsāre magnamuddhartumarhasi .
sukhāni tāni caivānte teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na tatsukham . . 1.62.10
1.62.d:
त्वं मामगाधे संसारे मग्नमुद्धर्तुमर्हसि ।
सुखानि तानि चैवान्ते तेषां दुःखं न तत्सुखम् ॥ 1.62.10
1.62.m:
you ought to lift me up, sunken in the bottomless worldly existence.
Those pleasures end in suffering; their [result] is not happiness.

1.62.s:
yadā tu duḥkhamāgāmi kiṃ4 vā kasyaiva bhakṣaṇāt .
tatprasādaṃ kuru vibho jagatāṃ tvaṃ jagatpate . . 11
1.62.d:
यदा तु दुःखमागामि किं4 वा कस्यैव भक्षणात् ।
तत्प्रसादं कुरु विभो जगतां त्वं जगत्पते ॥ 11
1.62.m:
When suffering is impending, what is the use of consuming anything?
Therefore grant your grace, O all-pervading Lord of the worlds, O master of the universe,

1.62.s:
jñānadānena yenaivamuttareyaṃ bhavārṇavam .
ityuktastena mārtaṇḍaḥ kathayāmāsa yogavit . . 12
1.62.d:
ज्ञानदानेन येनैवमुत्तरेयं भवार्णवम् ।
इत्युक्तस्तेन मार्तण्डः कथयामास योगवित् ॥ 12
1.62.m:
by granting knowledge through which I may cross the ocean of existence.'
Addressed thus by him, Mārtaṇḍa, who knows yoga, spoke.

1.62.s:
yogaṃ nirbījamatyantaṃ duḥkhasaṃyogabheṣajam .
śrutvā yogaṃ tu taṃ diṇḍirnirbījaṃ niṣkalaṃ babhau . . 13
1.62.d:
योगं निर्बीजमत्यन्तं दुःखसंयोगभेषजम् ।
श्रुत्वा योगं तु तं दिण्डिर्निर्बीजं निष्कलं बभौ ॥ 13
1.62.m: [Mārtaṇḍa taught] seedless yoga, which is the ultimate remedy for connection with suffering. / Having heard that seedless, partless yoga, Diṇḍi, however, shone.

1.62.s:
praṇipatya mahātejā idaṃ vacanamabravīt .
devadeva tvayā yogo yaḥ prokto dhvāntanāśana . .
naiṣa prāpyo mayā nānyairmānavairajitendriyaiḥ . . 14
1.62.d:
प्रणिपत्य महातेजा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
देवदेव त्वया योगो यः प्रोक्तो ध्वान्तनाशन ॥
नैष प्राप्यो मया नान्यैर्मानवैरजितेन्द्रियैः ॥ 14
1.62.m: Bowing low, he of great splendour spoke these words: / "O God of gods, O dispeller of darkness, this yoga which has been declared by you / cannot be attained by me, nor by other men whose senses are unsubdued.

1.62.s:
viṣayā durjayāḥ puṃbhirindriyākarṣiṇaḥ sadā .
indriyāṇāṃ jayo yuktaḥ kaḥ śaktānāṃ kariṣyati . . 15
1.62.d:
विषया दुर्जयाः पुंभिरिन्द्रियाकर्षिणः सदा ।
इन्द्रियाणां जयो युक्तः कः शक्तानां करिष्यति ॥ 15
1.62.m: Sense objects are difficult for men to conquer; they continually draw away the senses. / When the senses are powerful, who can accomplish their proper conquest?

1.62.s:
ahaṃmametivikhyātirdurjayaṃ cañcalaṃ manaḥ .
rāgādayastathā tyaktuṃ śakyā janmāntarairyadi2 . . 16
1.62.d:
अहंममेतिविख्यातिर्दुर्जयं चञ्चलं मनः ।
रागादयस्तथा त्यक्तुं शक्या जन्मान्तरैर्यदि2 ॥ 16
1.62.m: The notion of 'I' and 'mine' is renowned; the restless mind is hard to conquer. / Passion and the like can only be abandoned through other lifetimes, if at all.

1.62.s:
so'hamicchāmi deveśa tvatprasādādanirjitaiḥ .
rāgādibhiramartyatvaṃ prāpuḥ prakṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ . . 17
1.62.d:
सोऽहमिच्छामि देवेश त्वत्प्रसादादनिर्जितैः ।
रागादिभिरमर्त्यत्वं प्रापुः प्रक्षीणकल्मषाः ॥ 17
1.62.m: Therefore, O Lord of gods, by your grace I wish that [even] with passion and the like unconquered, / they whose blemishes have wasted away may attain immortality."

1.62.s:
āditya uvāca
yadyevaṃ muktikāmastvaṃ gaṇanātha śṛṇuṣva tam .
kriyāyogaṃ samastānāṃ kleśānāṃ hānikārakam3 .. 18.
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru .
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ . . 19
1.62.d:
आदित्य उवाच
यद्येवं मुक्तिकामस्त्वं गणनाथ शृणुष्व तम् ।
क्रियायोगं समस्तानां क्लेशानां हानिकारकम्3 ॥ 18.
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥ 19
1.62.m: Āditya said: / "If you desire liberation in this way, O lord of the retinue, listen to that / yoga of action which brings about the destruction of all afflictions: / Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow down to me; / having thus disciplined yourself with me as your ultimate goal, you shall come to me alone.

1.62.s:
madbhāvanā madyajanā madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ .
mama pūjākarāścaiva mayi yānti layaṃ narāḥ . . 1.62.20
1.62.d:
मद्भावना मद्यजना मद्भक्ता मत्परायणाः ।
मम पूजाकराश्चैव मयि यान्ति लयं नराः ॥ 1.62.20
1.62.m: Those whose contemplation is on me, whose worship is of me, who are devoted to me, who have me as their ultimate goal, / and who perform my worship—such men attain dissolution in me.

1.62.s:
sarvabhūteṣu māṃ paśyanmamavasthitamīśvaram4 .
karttāsi kena caiva tvamevaṃ doṣānprahāsyasi5 . . 21
1.62.d:
सर्वभूतेषु मां पश्यन्ममवस्थितमीश्वरम्4 ।
कर्त्तासि केन चैव त्वमेवं दोषान्प्रहास्यसि5 ॥ 21
1.62.m: Seeing me, the Lord, abiding within all beings, / and [thinking] 'Through whom are you the agent?', you will thus cast off all faults.

1.62.s:
jaṅgamājaṅgame jñāte mayyāsakte samantataḥ .
rāgalobhādināśena bhavitrī kṛtakṛtyatā . . 22
1.62.d:
जङ्गमाजङ्गमे ज्ञाते मय्यासक्ते समन्ततः ।
रागलोभादिनाशेन भवित्री कृतकृत्यता ॥ 22
1.62.m: When the moving and the unmoving are known [as me] and attached to me on all sides, / fulfillment will arise through the destruction of passion, greed, and the rest.

1.62.s:
bhaktyātipraṇayasyāpi cañcalatvānmano yadi .
mayyāveśaṃ dadhad bhūyaḥ kuru madrūpiṇīṃ tanum . . 23
1.62.d:
भक्त्यातिप्रणयस्यापि चञ्चलत्वान्मनो यदि ।
मय्यावेशं दधद् भूयः कुरु मद्रूपिणीं तनुम् ॥ 23
1.62.m: Even if, out of great affection through devotion, your mind is restless, / then, directing your absorption towards me, make again a physical image that has my form.

1.62.s:
suvarṇarajatādyaistvaṃ śailamṛddārulekhanam .
pūjopahārairvividhaiḥ sampūjaya trilocanam . . 24
1.62.d:
सुवर्णरजताद्यैस्त्वं शैलमृद्दारुलेखनम् ।
पूजोपहारैर्विविधैः सम्पूजय त्रिलोचनम् ॥ 24
1.62.m: With gold, silver, and other materials, worship the three-eyed one, / fashioned from stone, clay, or wood, or in a painting, with various offerings of worship.

1.62.s:
tasyāśritaṃ samāviśya sarvabhāvena sarvadā .
pūjitā saiva te bhaktyā dhyātā caivopakāriṇī . . 25
1.62.d:
तस्याश्रितं समाविश्य सर्वभावेन सर्वदा ।
पूजिता सैव ते भक्त्या ध्याता चैवोपकारिणी ॥ 25
1.62.m: Having resorted to that [form] and absorbed yourself [in it] with your whole being at all times, / worshipped with devotion and meditated upon, that very [image] will be beneficial to you.

1.62.s:
gacchaṃstiṣṭhansvapanbhuñjastāmevāgre ca pṛṣṭhataḥ .
uparyadhastathā pārśve cintayaṃstanmayaśca vai . . 26
1.62.d:
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन्स्वपन्भुञ्जस्तामेवाग्रे च पृष्ठतः ।
उपर्यधस्तथा पार्श्वे चिन्तयंस्तन्मयश्च वै ॥ 26
1.62.m: Walking, standing, sleeping, eating, thinking on that very [form] / in front, behind, above, below, and at your side, become indeed absorbed in it.

1.62.s:
snānaistīrthodakairhadyaiḥ 1puṣpairgandhānulepanaiḥ .
vāsobhirbhūṣaṇairbhakṣyairgītavādyairmanoramaiḥ . . 27
1.62.d:
स्नानैस्तीर्थोदकैर्हद्यैः 1पुष्पैर्गन्धानुलेपनैः ।
वासोभिर्भूषणैर्भक्ष्यैर्गीतवाद्यैर्मनोरमैः ॥ 27
1.62.m: With baths of water from sacred fords, with delightful flowers and fragrant ointments, / with garments, ornaments, foods, and charming songs and instrumental music,

1.62.s:
yacca yacca taveṣṭaṃ vai kiñcidbhojyādikaṃ tava .
bhaktinamro gaṇaśreṣṭha prīṇayasva kṛtiṃ2 mama . . 28
1.62.d:
यच्च यच्च तवेष्टं वै किञ्चिद्भोज्यादिकं तव ।
भक्तिनम्रो गणश्रेष्ठ प्रीणयस्व कृतिं2 मम ॥ 28
1.62.m: and whatever is pleasing to you, whatever food and the like you have, / bow low in devotion, O best of the retinue, and propitiate my image.

1.62.s:
rāgeṇākṛṣyate tāta gandharvābhimukhaṃ yadi .
mayi buddhiṃ samāveśya gāyethā yāḥ kathā mama . . 29
1.62.d:
रागेणाकृष्यते तात गन्धर्वाभिमुखं यदि ।
मयि बुद्धिं समावेश्य गायेथा याः कथा मम ॥ 29
1.62.m: If, dear one, [your mind] is drawn by passion toward Gandharva music, / absorb your intellect in me and sing the stories that pertain to me.

1.62.s:
kathayā ramate ceto yadi tadbhavato mama .
śrotavyāḥ prītiyogena matsvarūpodayāḥ kathāḥ . . 1.62.30
1.62.d:
कथया रमते चेतो यदि तद्भवतो मम ।
श्रोतव्याः प्रीतियोगेन मत्स्वरूपोदयाः कथाः ॥ 1.62.30
1.62.m: If your mind delights in stories, then, / stories about the arising of my true nature must be heard by you with loving devotion.

1.62.s:
evaṃ samarpitamanāścetaso ye'tha āśrayāḥ .
heyāstānnikhilāndiṇḍe parityajya sukhī bhava . . 31
1.62.d:
एवं समर्पितमनाश्चेतसो येऽथ आश्रयाः ।
हेयास्तान्निखिलान्दिण्डे परित्यज्य सुखी भव ॥ 31
1.62.m: With your mind thus surrendered, whatever supports of the mind / are to be rejected, abandon all of them, O Diṇḍi, and be happy.

1.62.s:
akṣīṇarāgadveṣo'pi matpriyaḥ paramaḥ param .
padamāpnoṣi mā bhaiṣīrmayyarpitamanā bhava . . 32
1.62.d:
अक्षीणरागद्वेषोऽपि मत्प्रियः परमः परम् ।
पदमाप्नोषि मा भैषीर्मय्यर्पितमना भव ॥ 32
1.62.m: Even if your passion and hatred are not exhausted, as my supreme beloved you will attain the highest / abode; do not fear, surrender your mind to me.

1.62.s:
mayi saṃnyasya sarvaṃ tvamātmānaṃ yatnavānbhava .
madarthaṃ kuru karmāṇi mā ca dharmavyatikramam . . 33
1.62.d:
मयि संन्यस्य सर्वं त्वमात्मानं यत्नवान्भव ।
मदर्थं कुरु कर्माणि मा च धर्मव्यतिक्रमम् ॥ 33
1.62.m: Having renounced everything unto me, exert yourself; / perform actions for my sake and do not transgress righteousness.

1.62.s:
evaṃ vyapohya hatyāstvaṃ brahmaṇa mokṣyase bhavāt .
etenaivopadeśena vyākhyātamakhilaṃ tava . . 34
1.62.d:
एवं व्यपोह्य हत्यास्त्वं ब्रह्मण मोक्ष्यसे भवात् ।
एतेनैवोपदेशेन व्याख्यातमखिलं तव ॥ 34
1.62.m: Having thus dispelled the killings of brahmins, you will be freed from worldly existence; / through this very instruction everything has been explained to you.

1.62.s: kriyāyogaṃ samāsthāya madarpitamanā bhava . . 35
1.62.d: क्रियायोगं समास्थाय मदर्पितमना भव ॥ 35
1.62.m: Relying on the yoga of action, surrender your mind to me."

1.62.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
maddhitāya jagannātha kriyāyogāmṛtaṃ mama .
vistareṇa samākhyāhi prasannastvaṃ hi duḥkhahā . . 36
1.62.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
मद्धिताय जगन्नाथ क्रियायोगामृतं मम ।
विस्तरेण समाख्याहि प्रसन्नस्त्वं हि दुःखहा ॥ 36
1.62.m: Diṇḍi said: / "For my benefit, O Lord of the universe, explain to me in detail / the nectar of the yoga of action; for, being pleased, you remove suffering.

1.62.s:
tvāmṛte na hi tadvaktuṃ samartho'nyo1 jagadguro .
guhyametatpavitraṃ ca tadācakṣva prasīda me . . 37
1.62.d:
त्वामृते न हि तद्वक्तुं समर्थोऽन्यो1 जगद्गुरो ।
गुह्यमेतत्पवित्रं च तदाचक्ष्व प्रसीद मे ॥ 37
1.62.m: Except for you, indeed no other is able to speak of that, O teacher of the world; / this is secret and purifying; therefore declare it, be gracious to me."

1.62.s:
āditya uvāca
ākhyāsyate tadakhilaṃ nirvikalpaṃ gaṇādhipa .
ityuktvāntardadhe devaḥ sarvalokapradīpakaḥ . . 38
1.62.d:
आदित्य उवाच
आख्यास्यते तदखिलं निर्विकल्पं गणाधिप ।
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे देवः सर्वलोकप्रदीपकः ॥ 38
1.62.m: Āditya said: / "All of that will be declared free of conceptual construction, O lord of the retinue." / Having spoken thus, the god, the illuminator of all the worlds, disappeared.

1.62.s: sa ca diṇḍirmahātejā jagāmāśu nabhogatim . . 39
1.62.d: स च दिण्डिर्महातेजा जगामाशु नभोगतिम् ॥ 39
1.62.m: And Diṇḍi, of great splendour, swiftly went along his sky-bound course.

1.62.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
diṇḍyādityasaṃvādavarṇanaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāya . 62 .
ādityamahimāvarṇanam
1.62.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
दिण्ड्यादित्यसंवादवर्णनं नाम द्विषष्टितमोऽध्याय । 62 ।
आदित्यमहिमावर्णनम्
1.62.m:
Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, named 'The Description of the Dialogue between Diṇḍi and Āditya', in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Greatness of Āditya

1.63.s:
sumanturuvāca
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ surajyeṣṭhaṃ caturmukham .
uvāca sa mahātejā diṇḍirlokeśamādarāt . . 1
1.63.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं सुरज्येष्ठं चतुर्मुखम् ।
उवाच स महातेजा दिण्डिर्लोकेशमादरात् ॥ 1
1.63.m: Sumantu said: / Having bowed with his head to the god, the eldest of the deities, the four-faced one, / Diṇḍi of great splendour respectfully addressed the Lord of the world:

1.63.s:
devadevena bhavatādiṣṭo'smi ca mahātmanā .
kriyāyogāmṛtaṃ2 sarvamākhyāsyati bhavānkila . . 2
1.63.d:
देवदेवेन भवतादिष्टोऽस्मि च महात्मना ।
क्रियायोगामृतं2 सर्वमाख्यास्यति भवान्किल ॥ 2
1.63.m: "I have been directed by you, the God of gods, the great-souled one; / you will indeed explain all the nectar of the yoga of action.

1.63.s:
sa tvāṃ pṛcchāmyahaṃ brahmankriyāyogaṃ nirantaram .
santoṣayitumīśehaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi . . 3
1.63.d:
स त्वां पृच्छाम्यहं ब्रह्मन्क्रियायोगं निरन्तरम् ।
सन्तोषयितुमीशेहं यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 3
1.63.m: Therefore I ask you, O Brahmā, about the uninterrupted yoga of action; / I am here to please the Lord; you ought to speak properly."

1.63.s:
brahmovāca
ehyehi matsakāśaṃ ca matsamīpe gaṇādhipa .
brahmahatyā praṇaṣṭā te darśanādeva tasya tu . . 4
1.63.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एह्येहि मत्सकाशं च मत्समीपे गणाधिप ।
ब्रह्महत्या प्रणष्टा ते दर्शनादेव तस्य तु ॥ 4
1.63.m: Brahmā said: / "Come, come into my presence and near me, O lord of the retinue; / your killing of a brahmin was destroyed merely by the sight of him.

1.63.s:
anugrāhyo'si bhūteśa bhāskarasyāmitaujasaḥ .
ārādhanāya bhūteśa yadīśe pravaṇaṃ manaḥ . . 5
1.63.d:
अनुग्राह्योऽसि भूतेश भास्करस्यामितौजसः ।
आराधनाय भूतेश यदीशे प्रवणं मनः ॥ 5
1.63.m: You are worthy of the grace of the Sun of boundless splendour, O lord of beings, / if your mind is inclined toward the Lord for his worship, O lord of beings.

1.63.s:
yadi devapatiṃ bhānumārādhayitumicchasi .
bhagavantamanādyantaṃ bhava dīkṣāguṇānvitaḥ . . 6
1.63.d:
यदि देवपतिं भानुमाराधयितुमिच्छसि ।
भगवन्तमनाद्यन्तं भव दीक्षागुणान्वितः ॥ 6
1.63.m: If you wish to worship the Sun, the lord of gods, / the Lord without beginning or end, be endowed with the qualities of initiation.

1.63.s:
na hyadīkṣānvitairbhānurjñātu stotuṃ ca tattvataḥ .
draṣṭuṃ vā śakyate mūḍhaiḥ praveṣṭuṃ kuta eva hi . . 7
1.63.d:
न ह्यदीक्षान्वितैर्भानुर्ज्ञातु स्तोतुं च तत्त्वतः ।
द्रष्टुं वा शक्यते मूढैः प्रवेष्टुं कुत एव हि ॥ 7
1.63.m: For by those who are uninitiated, the Sun cannot truly be known or praised, / or even seen by the foolish; how much less could he be entered into?

1.63.s:
janmabhirbahubhiḥ pūtā narāstadgatacetasaḥ .
bhavanti bhagavansaurāstadā dīkṣāguṇānvitāḥ . . 8
1.63.d:
जन्मभिर्बहुभिः पूता नरास्तद्गतचेतसः ।
भवन्ति भगवन्सौरास्तदा दीक्षागुणान्विताः ॥ 8
1.63.m: Purified through many births, their minds fixed on him, / men then become, O blessed one, Saura worshippers endowed with the qualities of initiation.

1.63.s:
anekajanmasaṃsāracite pāpasamuccaye .
nākṣīṇe jāyate puṃsāṃ mārtaṇḍābhimukhī matiḥ . . 9
1.63.d:
अनेकजन्मसंसारचिते पापसमुच्चये ।
नाक्षीणे जायते पुंसां मार्तण्डाभिमुखी मतिः ॥ 9
1.63.m: When the accumulation of sins gathered through worldly existence over many births / is not exhausted, the intellect of men does not turn towards Mārtaṇḍa.

1.63.s:
pradveṣaṃ yāti mārtaṇḍe dvijānvedāṃśca nindati .
yo narastaṃ vijānīyātpāpabījasamudbhavam 1 . . 1.63.10
1.63.d:
प्रद्वेषं याति मार्तण्डे द्विजान्वेदांश्च निन्दति ।
यो नरस्तं विजानीयात्पापबीजसमुद्भवम् 1 ॥ 1.63.10
1.63.m: That man who feels hatred towards Mārtaṇḍa and reviles the twice-born and the Vedas, / one should know him to have arisen from a seed of sin.

1.63.s:
pākhaṇḍeṣu ratiḥ puṃsāṃ hetuvādānukūlatā .
jāyate viṣṇumāyāmbhaḥ patitānāṃ durātmanām . . 11
1.63.d:
पाखण्डेषु रतिः पुंसां हेतुवादानुकूलता ।
जायते विष्णुमायाम्भः पतितानां दुरात्मनाम् ॥ 11
1.63.m: Delight in heterodox views and an inclination toward dialectics / arise in those wicked men who have fallen into the waters of Viṣṇu's Māyā.

1.63.s:
yadā pāpakṣayaḥ puṃsāṃ tadā vedadvijādiṣu .
ravau ca devadeveśe śraddhāṃ bhavati niścalā . . 12
1.63.d:
यदा पापक्षयः पुंसां तदा वेदद्विजादिषु ।
रवौ च देवदेवेशे श्रद्धां भवति निश्चला ॥ 12
1.63.m: When the destruction of sins occurs for men, then unwavering faith / arises in the Vedas, the twice-born, and the like, and in the Sun, the God of gods.

1.63.s:
yadā svalpāvaśeṣastu narāṇāṃ pāpasañcayaḥ .
tadā dīkṣāguṇānsarve bhajante nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 13
1.63.d:
यदा स्वल्पावशेषस्तु नराणां पापसञ्चयः ।
तदा दीक्षागुणान्सर्वे भजन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥ 13
1.63.m: When only a small remainder of men's accumulation of sins is left, / then all resort to the qualities of initiation; there is no doubt about this.

1.63.s:
bhramatāmatra saṃsāre narāṇāṃ pāpadurgame .
hastāvalambadopyeko bhaktiprīto divākaraḥ . . 14
1.63.d:
भ्रमतामत्र संसारे नराणां पापदुर्गमे ।
हस्तावलम्बदोप्येको भक्तिप्रीतो दिवाकरः ॥ 14
1.63.m: For men wandering here in worldly existence, which is hard to traverse because of sin, / the Day-Maker alone, pleased by devotion, gives a supporting hand.

1.63.s:
sarvabhāgavato bhūtvā sarvapāpaharaṃ ravim .
ārādhayeha taṃ bhaktyā prītimeṣyati bhāskaraḥ . . 15
1.63.d:
सर्वभागवतो भूत्वा सर्वपापहरं रविम् ।
आराधयेह तं भक्त्या प्रीतिमेष्यति भास्करः ॥ 15
1.63.m: Becoming wholly a devotee, worship with devotion here the Sun, / the destroyer of all sins; the Sun will show his favour."

1.63.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
kiṃ lakṣaṇā narā dīkṣāmarhanti padmasambhava .
yacca dīkṣānvitaiḥ kāryaṃ tanme kathaya padmaja . . 16
1.63.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
किं लक्षणा नरा दीक्षामर्हन्ति पद्मसम्भव ।
यच्च दीक्षान्वितैः कार्यं तन्मे कथय पद्मज ॥ 16
1.63.m: Diṇḍi said: / "Men of what characteristics are worthy of initiation, O lotus-born one? / And what is to be done by those endowed with initiation? Tell me that, O lotus-born one."

1.63.s:
brahmovāca
karmaṇā manasā vācā prāṇināṃ yo na hiṃsakaḥ .
bhāvabhaktaśca mārtaṇḍe tasya dīkṣā guṇānvitā . . 17
1.63.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा प्राणिनां यो न हिंसकः ।
भावभक्तश्च मार्तण्डे तस्य दीक्षा गुणान्विता ॥ 17
1.63.m: Brahmā said: / "He who does not harm living beings by action, mind, or speech, / and has heartfelt devotion to Mārtaṇḍa, his initiation is endowed with [all] qualities."

1.63.s:
brāhmaṇāṃścaiva devāṃśca nityameva namasyati .
na ca drogdhā1 paraṃ vāde sa mārtaṇḍaṃ samarcati . . 18
1.63.d:
ब्राह्मणांश्चैव देवांश्च नित्यमेव नमस्यति ।
न च द्रोग्धा1 परं वादे स मार्तण्डं समर्चति ॥ 18
1.63.m: And who always bows down to brāhmaṇas and gods, / and is not malicious toward another in debate—he truly worships Mārtaṇḍa.

1.63.s:
sarvāndevān raviṃ vetti sarvalokāṃśca bhāskaram .
tebhyaśca nānyamātmānaṃ sa naraḥ sauratāṃ vrajet . . 19
1.63.d:
सर्वान्देवान् रविं वेत्ति सर्वलोकांश्च भास्करम् ।
तेभ्यश्च नान्यमात्मानं स नरः सौरतां व्रजेत् ॥ 19
1.63.m: He who knows all gods to be the Sun, and all worlds to be the Light-maker, / and knows himself to be non-different from them—that man attains the state of a Saura.

1.63.s:
devaṃ manuṣyamanyaṃ vā paśupakṣipipīlikān .
tarupāṣāṇakāṣṭhāni bhūmyaṃbho gaganaṃ diśaḥ . . 1.63.20
1.63.d:
देवं मनुष्यमन्यं वा पशुपक्षिपिपीलिकान् ।
तरुपाषाणकाष्ठानि भूम्यंभो गगनं दिशः ॥ 1.63.20
1.63.m: God, man, or another creature, beasts, birds, ants, / trees, stones, wood, earth, water, sky, the directions,

1.63.s:
ātmānaṃ cāpi deveśādvyatiriktaṃ divākarāt .
yo na jānāti yatiṣu sa vai dīkṣāguṇānbhajet . . 21
1.63.d:
आत्मानं चापि देवेशाद्व्यतिरिक्तं दिवाकरात् ।
यो न जानाति यतिषु स वै दीक्षागुणान्भजेत् ॥ 21
1.63.m: and also himself—he who among ascetics does not know [any of these] to be distinct / from the Lord of Gods, the Sun, he indeed partakes of the virtues of initiation.

1.63.s:
bhāvaṃ na kurute yastu sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam .
karmaṇā manasā vācā sa tu dīkṣāṃ samarhati . . 22
1.63.d:
भावं न कुरुते यस्तु सर्वभूतेषु पापकम् ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा स तु दीक्षां समर्हति ॥ 22
1.63.m: Moreover, he who does not harbor an evil intention toward any being, / in deed, mind, or speech, he is truly worthy of initiation.

1.63.s:
sutapteneha tapasā yathairvā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ .
tāṃ gatiṃ na narā yānti yāṃ gatāḥ sūryamāśritāḥ . 23
1.63.d:
सुतप्तेनेह तपसा यथैर्वा बहुदक्षिणैः ।
तां गतिं न नरा यान्ति यां गताः सूर्यमाश्रिताः । 23
1.63.m: Not by intensely practiced penance here, nor by sacrifices with bountiful gifts, / do men attain that destination which those who have taken refuge in the Sun have attained.

1.63.s:
yena sarvātmanā bhānau bhaktyā bhāvo niveśitaḥ .
gaṇeśvara kṛtārthatvācchlāghyaḥ sauraḥ sa mānavaḥ . . 24
1.63.d:
येन सर्वात्मना भानौ भक्त्या भावो निवेशितः ।
गणेश्वर कृतार्थत्वाच्छ्लाघ्यः सौरः स मानवः ॥ 24
1.63.m: He by whom, with his whole soul, intent has been placed in the Sun with devotion, / O lord of gaṇas, having accomplished his aim, that Saura man is praiseworthy.

1.63.s:
api naḥ sa kule dhanyo jāyate kulapāvanaḥ .
bhagavānbhaktibhāvena yena bhānurupāsitaḥ . . 25
1.63.d:
अपि नः स कुले धन्यो जायते कुलपावनः ।
भगवान्भक्तिभावेन येन भानुरुपासितः ॥ 25
1.63.m: Indeed, fortunate is he born in our family, a purifier of his line, / by whom, through the attitude of devotion, the blessed Sun has been worshiped.

1.63.s:
yaḥ kārayati - devārcāṃ hṛdayālambanaṃ raveḥ .
sa naro bhānusālokyamāpnoti dhutakalmaṣaḥ . . 26
1.63.d:
यः कारयति - देवार्चां हृदयालम्बनं रवेः ।
स नरो भानुसालोक्यमाप्नोति धुतकल्मषः ॥ 26
1.63.m: The man who causes an image of the Sun to be made, a resting place for the heart, / attains the same world as the Sun, his impurities shaken off.

1.63.s:
yastu devālayaṃ bhānorbhaktyā kārayati dhruvam .
sa sapta puruṣām̐llokaṃ bhānornayati mānavaḥ . . 27
1.63.d:
यस्तु देवालयं भानोर्भक्त्या कारयति ध्रुवम् ।
स सप्त पुरुषाम्̐ल्लोकं भानोर्नयति मानवः ॥ 27
1.63.m: Moreover, that man who faithfully causes a temple of the Sun to be built as an enduring [work], / leads seven generations to the world of the Sun.

1.63.s:
yāvantyābdāni devārcā ravestiṣṭhati mandire .
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi sūryaloke mahīyate . . 28
1.63.d:
यावन्त्याब्दानि देवार्चा रवेस्तिष्ठति मन्दिरे ।
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 28
1.63.m: For as many years as the divine image of the Sun remains in the temple, / for that many thousands of years he is glorified in the world of the Sun.

1.63.s:
devārcā lakṣaṇopetā tadgṛhe santato vidhiḥ .
niṣkāmaṃ ca mano yasya sa yātyakṣarasāmyatām . . 29
1.63.d:
देवार्चा लक्षणोपेता तद्गृहे सन्ततो विधिः ।
निष्कामं च मनो यस्य स यात्यक्षरसाम्यताम् ॥ 29
1.63.m: The man whose house has a divine image endowed with auspicious characteristics, where the rite is continuous, / and whose mind is free of desire, he attains equality with the imperishable.

1.63.s:
puṣpāṇi ca sugandhīni manojñāni ca yaḥ pumān .
prayacchati sahasrāṃśoḥ sadā prayatamānasaḥ . . 1.63.30
1.63.d:
पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि मनोज्ञानि च यः पुमान् ।
प्रयच्छति सहस्रांशोः सदा प्रयतमानसः ॥ 1.63.30
1.63.m: The man who, with an ever-restrained mind, / offers fragrant and pleasing flowers to the Thousand-Rayed One,

1.63.s:
dhūpāṃśca tāṃstānvividhāngandhāḍhyaṃ cānulepanam .
naraḥ so'nudinaṃ yajñaṃ karotyārādhanaṃ raveḥ . . 31
1.63.d:
धूपांश्च तांस्तान्विविधान्गन्धाढ्यं चानुलेपनम् ।
नरः सोऽनुदिनं यज्ञं करोत्याराधनं रवेः ॥ 31
1.63.m: as well as various kinds of incense and ointment rich in fragrance, / that man performs daily a sacrifice, an adoration of the Sun.

1.63.s:
yajñeśo bhagavānpūṣā sadā kratubhirijyate .
bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsambhāravistarāḥ . . 32
1.63.d:
यज्ञेशो भगवान्पूषा सदा क्रतुभिरिज्यते ।
बहूपकरणा यज्ञा नानासम्भारविस्तराः ॥ 32
1.63.m: The Lord Pūṣan, the master of sacrifice, is constantly worshipped with sacrificial rites; / sacrifices require many implements and extensive assortments of provisions.

1.63.s:
na te diṇḍinnavāpyante manuṣyairalpasañcayaiḥ .
bhaktyā tu puruṣaiḥ pūjā kṛtā dūrvāṅkurairapi . .
bhānordadāti hi phalaṃ sarvayajñaiḥ sudurlabham . . 33
1.63.d:
न ते दिण्डिन्नवाप्यन्ते मनुष्यैरल्पसञ्चयैः ।
भक्त्या तु पुरुषैः पूजा कृता दूर्वाङ्कुरैरपि ॥
भानोर्ददाति हि फलं सर्वयज्ञैः सुदुर्लभम् ॥ 33
1.63.m: O Diṇḍi, they cannot be obtained by men of small means. / But worship performed by men with devotion even with sprouts of dūrvā grass / gives from the Sun a reward indeed very hard to obtain through all sacrifices.

1.63.s:
yāni puṣpāṇi hṛdyāni dhūpagandhānulepanam .
dayitaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ yacca prītaye caiva vāsasī . . 34
1.63.d:
यानि पुष्पाणि हृद्यानि धूपगन्धानुलेपनम् ।
दयितं भूषणं यच्च प्रीतये चैव वाससी ॥ 34
1.63.m: Whatever flowers are pleasing to the heart, incense, fragrances, and ointments, / whatever ornament is beloved, and two garments for [his] pleasure,

1.63.s:
yāni cābhyavahāryāṇi bhakṣāāṇi ca phalāni vai .
prayaccha tāni mārtaṇḍe bhavethāścaiva tanmanāḥ . . 35
1.63.d:
यानि चाभ्यवहार्याणि भक्षाआणि च फलानि वै ।
प्रयच्छ तानि मार्तण्डे भवेथाश्चैव तन्मनाः ॥ 35
1.63.m: and whatever eatables, delicacies, and fruits there are— / offer them to Mārtaṇḍa and keep your mind fixed on him.

1.63.s:
ādyaṃ taṃ bhuvanādhāraṃ yathāśaktyā prasādaya .
ārādhya yāti taṃ devaṃ tasminneva naro layam . . 36
1.63.d:
आद्यं तं भुवनाधारं यथाशक्त्या प्रसादय ।
आराध्य याति तं देवं तस्मिन्नेव नरो लयम् ॥ 36
1.63.m: Propitiate that primordial support of the world according to your ability; / having adored that god, a man attains dissolution in him alone.

1.63.s:
puṣpaistīrthodakairgandhairmadhunā sarpiṣā tathā .
kṣīreṇa snāpayedbhānuṃ graheśaṃ gopatiṃ khagam . . 37
1.63.d:
पुष्पैस्तीर्थोदकैर्गन्धैर्मधुना सर्पिषा तथा ।
क्षीरेण स्नापयेद्भानुं ग्रहेशं गोपतिं खगम् ॥ 37
1.63.m: One should bathe the Sun, the lord of the planets, the master of rays, the sky-goer, / with flowers, water from sacred fords, perfumes, honey, clarified butter, and milk.

1.63.s:
dadhikṣīrahradānpuṇyāṃstato lokānmadhucyutaḥ .
prayāsyati gaṇaśreṣṭha nirvṛttiṃ ca vilakṣaṇām . . 38
1.63.d:
दधिक्षीरह्रदान्पुण्यांस्ततो लोकान्मधुच्युतः ।
प्रयास्यति गणश्रेष्ठ निर्वृत्तिं च विलक्षणाम् ॥ 38
1.63.m: Then, O best of the gaṇa, he will go to sacred worlds of lakes of curd and milk, / flowing with honey, and to peerless bliss.

1.63.s:
stotrairgītaistathā vādyairbrāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ .
manasaścaiva yogena ārādhaya divākaram . . 39
1.63.d:
स्तोत्रैर्गीतैस्तथा वाद्यैर्ब्राह्मणानां च तर्पणैः ।
मनसश्चैव योगेन आराधय दिवाकरम् ॥ 39
1.63.m: With hymns of praise, songs, musical instruments, and gratifications of brāhmaṇas, / and with concentration of the mind, adore the Maker of Day.

1.63.s:
ārādhya taṃ jagannāthaṃ mayā sargaḥ pravartitaḥ .
viṣṇuśca pālayellokāṃstamārādhya divākaram . . 1.63.40
1.63.d:
आराध्य तं जगन्नाथं मया सर्गः प्रवर्तितः ।
विष्णुश्च पालयेल्लोकांस्तमाराध्य दिवाकरम् ॥ 1.63.40
1.63.m: Having adored that Lord of the Universe, creation was set in motion by me; / and Viṣṇu, having adored that Maker of Day, protects the worlds.

1.63.s:
rudraśca prāptavāndevīṃ bhavānīṃ tatprasādataḥ .
dīpyante ṛṣayaścāpi tamārādhya divākaram . . 41
1.63.d:
रुद्रश्च प्राप्तवान्देवीं भवानीं तत्प्रसादतः ।
दीप्यन्ते ऋषयश्चापि तमाराध्य दिवाकरम् ॥ 41
1.63.m: And Rudra obtained the goddess Bhavānī through his grace; / and the sages also shine, having adored that Maker of Day.

1.63.s:
sa tvamebhiḥ prakāraistamupavāsaiśca bhāskaram .
toṣayābdaṃ hi tuṣṭo'sau bhānurdvaṃdvapraśāntidaḥ . . 42
phalasaptamīvarṇanam
1.63.d:
स त्वमेभिः प्रकारैस्तमुपवासैश्च भास्करम् ।
तोषयाब्दं हि तुष्टोऽसौ भानुर्द्वंद्वप्रशान्तिदः ॥ 42
फलसप्तमीवर्णनम्
1.63.m:
Therefore, by these means and by fasts, / please that Maker of Light for a year; for when pleased, the Sun brings an end to dualities.
Description of the Phalasaptamī.

1.64.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
upavāsaiḥ suraśreṣṭha kathaṃ tuṣyati bhāskaraḥ .
parihārāṃstathācakṣva ye tyājyāścopavāsibhiḥ . . 1
1.64.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
उपवासैः सुरश्रेष्ठ कथं तुष्यति भास्करः ।
परिहारांस्तथाचक्ष्व ये त्याज्याश्चोपवासिभिः ॥ 1
1.64.m:
Diṇḍi said:
O best of gods, how is the Maker of Light pleased by fasts? / And tell [me] of the abstentions that are to be avoided by those who fast.

1.64.s:
yadyatkāryaṃ yathā caiva bhāskarārādhane narai .
tatsarvaṃ vistarādbrahmanyathāvadvaktumarhasi . . 2
1.64.d:
यद्यत्कार्यं यथा चैव भास्कराराधने नरै ।
तत्सर्वं विस्तराद्ब्रह्मन्यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 2
1.64.m: Whatever is to be done, and in what manner, by men in the worship of the Maker of Light, / all that, O Brahmā, you ought to tell me in detail, as it truly is.

1.64.s:
brahmovāca
smṛtaḥ sampūjito dhūpapuṣpānnairbhānurādarāt .
bhogināmupakārāya kiṃ punaścopavāsinām . . 3
1.64.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स्मृतः सम्पूजितो धूपपुष्पान्नैर्भानुरादरात् ।
भोगिनामुपकाराय किं पुनश्चोपवासिनाम् ॥ 3
1.64.m:
Brahmā said:
The Sun, when remembered and worshipped with devotion with incense, flowers, and food, / brings benefit to pleasure-seekers—how much more then to those who fast?

1.64.s:
upāvṛttasya pāpebhyo yastu vāso guṇaiḥ saha .
upavāsaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sarvabhogavivarjitaḥ . . 4
1.64.d:
उपावृत्तस्य पापेभ्यो यस्तु वासो गुणैः सह ।
उपवासः स विज्ञेयः सर्वभोगविवर्जितः ॥ 4
1.64.m: The residence of one who has turned away from sins along with [spiritual] virtues, / devoid of all sensual pleasures, is to be known as a fast.

1.64.s:
ekarātraṃ dvirātraṃ vā trirātraṃ naktameva ca .
upavāsī raviṃ yastu bhaktyā dhyāyati mānavaḥ . . 5
1.64.d:
एकरात्रं द्विरात्रं वा त्रिरात्रं नक्तमेव च ।
उपवासी रविं यस्तु भक्त्या ध्यायति मानवः ॥ 5
1.64.m: Fasting for one night, two nights, three nights, or taking only the nocturnal meal, / the man who meditates upon the Sun with devotion,

1.64.s:
tannāmajāpī tatkarmaratastadgatamānasaḥ .
niṣkāmaḥ puruṣo diṇḍe sa brahma paramāpnuyāt . . 6
1.64.d:
तन्नामजापी तत्कर्मरतस्तद्गतमानसः ।
निष्कामः पुरुषो दिण्डे स ब्रह्म परमाप्नुयात् ॥ 6
1.64.m: muttering his names, delighting in his works, his mind absorbed in him, / that man, free from desire, O Diṇḍi, attains the supreme Brahman.

1.64.s:
yaṃ ca kāmamabhidhyāya māskarārpitamānasaḥ .
upoṣati tamāpnoti prasanne khagame'khilam . . 7
1.64.d:
यं च काममभिध्याय मास्करार्पितमानसः ।
उपोषति तमाप्नोति प्रसन्ने खगमेऽखिलम् ॥ 7
1.64.m: And whatever desire one contemplates with one's mind offered to the Maker of Light / while fasting, he obtains it all when the Sky-Goer is pleased.

1.64.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdraiḥ strībhiśca kañjaja .
saṃsāragarte paṅkasthe sugatiḥ prāpyate katham . . 8
1.64.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैः शूद्रैः स्त्रीभिश्च कञ्जज ।
संसारगर्ते पङ्कस्थे सुगतिः प्राप्यते कथम् ॥ 8
1.64.m:
Diṇḍi said:
By brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and by women, O lotus-born one, / stuck in the mire of the pit of saṃsāra, how is a good destiny attained?

1.64.s:
brahmovāca
anārādhya jagannāthaṃ gopatiṃ dhvāntanāśanam .
nirvyalīkena cittena kaḥ prayāsyati sadgatim . . 9
1.64.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अनाराध्य जगन्नाथं गोपतिं ध्वान्तनाशनम् ।
निर्व्यलीकेन चित्तेन कः प्रयास्यति सद्गतिम् ॥ 9
1.64.m:
Brahmā said:
Without adoring the Lord of the Universe, the master of rays, the destroyer of darkness, / with a sincere heart, who will attain a good destiny?

1.64.s:
viṣayagrāhi vai yasya na cittaṃ bhāskarārpitam .
sa kathaṃ pāpapaṅkākto naro yāsyati sadgatim . . 1.64.10
1.64.d:
विषयग्राहि वै यस्य न चित्तं भास्करार्पितम् ।
स कथं पापपङ्काक्तो नरो यास्यति सद्गतिम् ॥ 1.64.10
1.64.m: He whose mind, grasping sense objects, is not offered to the Maker of Light, / how will that man, smeared with the mire of sin, attain a good destiny?

1.64.s:
yadi saṃsāraduḥkhārtaḥ sugatiṃ gantumicchasi .
tadārādhaya sarveśaṃ bhāskaraṃ jyotiṣāṃ patim . . 11
1.64.d:
यदि संसारदुःखार्तः सुगतिं गन्तुमिच्छसि ।
तदाराधय सर्वेशं भास्करं ज्योतिषां पतिम् ॥ 11
1.64.m: If, afflicted by the suffering of saṃsāra, you wish to attain a good destiny, / then adore the Lord of All, the Maker of Light, the master of luminaries,

1.64.s:
puṣpaiḥ sugandhairhadyaiśca dhūpaiḥ sāgarucandanaiḥ .
vāsobhirbhūṣaṇairbhakṣyairupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ . . 12
1.64.d:
पुष्पैः सुगन्धैर्हद्यैश्च धूपैः सागरुचन्दनैः ।
वासोभिर्भूषणैर्भक्ष्यैरुपवासपरायणः ॥ 12
1.64.m: with fragrant and delightful flowers, with incenses of agallochum and sandalwood, / with garments, ornaments, and eatables, intent on fasting.

1.64.s:
yadi saṃsāranirvedādabhivācchasi sadgatim .
tadārādhaya mārtaṇḍaṃ bhaktipravaṇacetasā . . 13
1.64.d:
यदि संसारनिर्वेदादभिवाच्छसि सद्गतिम् ।
तदाराधय मार्तण्डं भक्तिप्रवणचेतसा ॥ 13
1.64.m: If, out of disgust with saṃsāra, you long for a good destiny, / then adore Mārtaṇḍa with a mind bowed in devotion.

1.64.s:
puṣpāṇi yadi te na snuḥ śastapādapapallavaiḥ .
dūrvāṅkarairapi diṇḍe tadabhāve'rcayāryamam . . 14
1.64.d:
पुष्पाणि यदि ते न स्नुः शस्तपादपपल्लवैः ।
दूर्वाङ्करैरपि दिण्डे तदभावेऽर्चयार्यमम् ॥ 14
1.64.m: If you should not have flowers, worship Aryaman with the shoots of auspicious trees, / or even with dūrvā sprouts, O Diṇḍi, in their absence.

1.64.s:
puṣpapatrāmbubhirdhūpairyathāvibhavamātmanaḥ .
pūjitastuṣṭimatulāṃ bhaktyā yātyekacetasā . . 15
1.64.d:
पुष्पपत्राम्बुभिर्धूपैर्यथाविभवमात्मनः ।
पूजितस्तुष्टिमतुलां भक्त्या यात्येकचेतसा ॥ 15
1.64.m: Worshipped with flowers, leaves, water, and incense according to one's means, / with devotion and with single-mindedness, he reaches incomparable satisfaction.

1.64.s:
yaḥ sadāyatane bhānoḥ kurute mārjanakriyām .
sa yātyuttamake sthāne sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati . . 16
1.64.d:
यः सदायतने भानोः कुरुते मार्जनक्रियाम् ।
स यात्युत्तमके स्थाने सर्वपापं व्यपोहति ॥ 16
1.64.m: He who constantly performs the act of sweeping in the abode of the Sun / goes to the highest realm and removes all sin.

1.64.s:
yāvatyaḥ pāṃsukaṇikā mārjyante bhāskarālaye .
dināni divi tāvanti tiṣṭhatyarkasamo naraḥ . . 17
1.64.d:
यावत्यः पांसुकणिका मार्ज्यन्ते भास्करालये ।
दिनानि दिवि तावन्ति तिष्ठत्यर्कसमो नरः ॥ 17
1.64.m: For as many specks of dust as are swept away in the abode of the Maker of Light, / for that many days does a man dwell in heaven, equal to the Sun.

1.64.s:
ahanyahani yatpāpaṃ kurute gaṇanāyaka .
gocarmamātraṃ sammārjya hanti tadbhāskarālaye . . 18
1.64.d:
अहन्यहनि यत्पापं कुरुते गणनायक ।
गोचर्ममात्रं सम्मार्ज्य हन्ति तद्भास्करालये ॥ 18
1.64.m: Whatever sin one commits day by day, O leader of the gaṇa, / by sweeping an area the size of a cowhide in the abode of the Maker of Light, he destroys it.

1.64.s:
yaścānulepanaṃ kuryādbhānorāyatane naraḥ .
so'pi lokaṃ samāsādya haṃsena saha modate . . 19
1.64.d:
यश्चानुलेपनं कुर्याद्भानोरायतने नरः ।
सोऽपि लोकं समासाद्य हंसेन सह मोदते ॥ 19
1.64.m: And the man who applies an unguent in the Sun's temple, / he too, having reached [the Sun's] realm, rejoices together with the goose.

1.64.s:
mṛdā dhātuvikārairvā varṇakairgomayena vā .
upalepanakṛdyāti matpuraṃ yānamāsthitaḥ . . 1.64.20
1.64.d:
मृदा धातुविकारैर्वा वर्णकैर्गोमयेन वा ।
उपलेपनकृद्याति मत्पुरं यानमास्थितः ॥ 1.64.20
1.64.m: Whether with clay, or with mineral pigments, or with colours, or with cow dung, / one who smears [the floor] goes mounted upon a vehicle to my city.

1.64.s:
udakābhyukṣaṇaṃ bhānoryaḥ karoti sadā gṛhe .
so'pi gacchati yatrāste bhagavānyādasāṃ patiḥ . . 21
1.64.d:
उदकाभ्युक्षणं भानोर्यः करोति सदा गृहे ।
सोऽपि गच्छति यत्रास्ते भगवान्यादसां पतिः ॥ 21
1.64.m: He who always sprinkles water in the house of the Sun, / he also goes to where the blessed lord of the aquatic creatures resides.

1.64.s:
puṣpaprakaramatyarthaṃ sugandhaṃ bhāskarālaye .
anulipte naro dattvā na durgatimavāpnuyāt . . 22
1.64.d:
पुष्पप्रकरमत्यर्थं सुगन्धं भास्करालये ।
अनुलिप्ते नरो दत्त्वा न दुर्गतिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 22
1.64.m: A man who offers a profuse, highly fragrant scattering of flowers / in the Sun's temple once smeared, will not meet with an unfortunate rebirth.

1.64.s:
vimānamatiśobhāḍhyaṃ sarvartusukhabhūṣitam .
samāpnoti naro dattvā dīpakaṃ bhāskarālaye . . 23
1.64.d:
विमानमतिशोभाढ्यं सर्वर्तुसुखभूषितम् ।
समाप्नोति नरो दत्त्वा दीपकं भास्करालये ॥ 23
1.64.m: A man obtains a celestial chariot rich in splendour, / adorned with the pleasures of all seasons, having offered a lamp in the Sun's temple.

1.64.s:
yastu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ tilapātraprado naraḥ .
dhvajaṃ ca bhāskare dadyātsamamatra phalaṃ labhet . . 24
1.64.d:
यस्तु संवत्सरं पूर्णं तिलपात्रप्रदो नरः ।
ध्वजं च भास्करे दद्यात्सममत्र फलं लभेत् ॥ 24
1.64.m: The man who offers a vessel of sesame for a full year, / and offers a banner to the Sun, obtains equal fruit in this matter.

1.64.s:
vidhūto hanti vātena dāturajñānataḥ kṛtam .
pāpaṃ karturgṛhe bhānordivā rātrau narādhipa . . 25
1.64.d:
विधूतो हन्ति वातेन दातुरज्ञानतः कृतम् ।
पापं कर्तुर्गृहे भानोर्दिवा रात्रौ नराधिप ॥ 25
1.64.m: Shaken by the wind, O ruler of men, in the house of the Sun day and night / it destroys the sin committed unknowingly by the donor and the maker.

1.64.s:
gītavādyādibhirbhānuṃ ya upāste tamopaham .
gandharvairnṛtyagītaiḥ sa vimānastho niṣevyate . . 26
1.64.d:
गीतवाद्यादिभिर्भानुं य उपास्ते तमोपहम् ।
गन्धर्वैर्नृत्यगीतैः स विमानस्थो निषेव्यते ॥ 26
1.64.m: He who worships the dispeller of darkness with song, instrumental music, and other [arts], / stays in a celestial chariot and is attended by Gandharvas with dances and songs.

1.64.s:
jātismaratvaṃ medhāṃ ca tathaivoparame smṛtim .
prāpnoti gaṇāśārdūla kṛtvā pustakavācanam . . 27
1.64.d:
जातिस्मरत्वं मेधां च तथैवोपरमे स्मृतिम् ।
प्राप्नोति गणाशार्दूल कृत्वा पुस्तकवाचनम् ॥ 27
1.64.m: Recollection of past lives, intelligence, and likewise memory at the time of death / does one obtain, O tiger among the Gaṇas, by performing the recitation of a book.

1.64.s:
evaṃ khageśvaro bhaktyā yena bhānurupāsitaḥ .
sa prāpnoti gatiṃ ślādhyāṃ yāṃ yāmicchati cetasā . . 28
1.64.d:
एवं खगेश्वरो भक्त्या येन भानुरुपासितः ।
स प्राप्नोति गतिं श्लाध्यां यां यामिच्छति चेतसा ॥ 28
1.64.m: Thus, by whomsoever the Sun, the lord of birds, has been worshipped with devotion, / he attains that praiseworthy state, whatever it be, that he desires in his heart.

1.64.s:
devatvaṃ manujaiḥ kaiścidgandharvatvaṃ tathā paraiḥ .
vidyādharatvamaparaiḥ saṃrādhyeha divākaram . . 29
1.64.d:
देवत्वं मनुजैः कैश्चिद्गन्धर्वत्वं तथा परैः ।
विद्याधरत्वमपरैः संराध्येह दिवाकरम् ॥ 29
1.64.m: Godhood [has been attained] by some men, Gandharvahood likewise by others, / and Vidyādharahood by yet others, having thoroughly propitiated the Day-Maker here.

1.64.s:
śakraḥ 1 kratuśateneśamārādhya jyotiṣāṃ patim .
devendratvaṃ gatastasmānnānyaḥ2 pūjyatamaḥ kvacit . . 1.64.30
1.64.d:
शक्रः 1 क्रतुशतेनेशमाराध्य ज्योतिषां पतिम् ।
देवेन्द्रत्वं गतस्तस्मान्नान्यः2 पूज्यतमः क्वचित् ॥ 1.64.30
1.64.m: Śakra, having propitiated the lord of the luminaries with a hundred sacrifices, / attained the status of king of the gods; therefore none other anywhere is more worthy of worship.

1.64.s:
brahmacārigṛhasthānāṃ vanasthānāṃ gaṇādhipa .
nānyaḥ pūjyastathā strīṇāmṛte devaṃ divākaram . . 31
1.64.d:
ब्रह्मचारिगृहस्थानां वनस्थानां गणाधिप ।
नान्यः पूज्यस्तथा स्त्रीणामृते देवं दिवाकरम् ॥ 31
1.64.m: For celibate students, householders, and forest-dwellers, O leader of the Gaṇas, / and likewise for women, none other is to be worshipped except the divine Day-Maker.

1.64.s:
madhye parivrājakānāṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ mahātmanām .
mokṣadvāraṃ viśantīha taṃ raviṃ vijitātmanām . . 32
1.64.d:
मध्ये परिव्राजकानां सहस्रांशुं महात्मनाम् ।
मोक्षद्वारं विशन्तीह तं रविं विजितात्मनाम् ॥ 32
1.64.m: Among self-controlled ascetics of great soul, / here they enter that Thousand-Rayed Ravi, the doorway to liberation.

1.64.s:
evaṃ sarvāśramāṇāṃ hi sahasrāṃśuḥ parāyaṇam .
sarveṣāṃ caiva varṇānāṃ graheśo vai gatiḥ parā . . 33
1.64.d:
एवं सर्वाश्रमाणां हि सहस्रांशुः परायणम् ।
सर्वेषां चैव वर्णानां ग्रहेशो वै गतिः परा ॥ 33
1.64.m: Thus the Thousand-Rayed is indeed the supreme goal for all stages of life, / and the lord of the planets is truly the highest path for all classes.

1.64.s:
śṛṇuṣva gadataḥ kāmyānupavāsāṃstathāparān .
śṛṇu diṇḍe mahāpuṇyaphalakāṃ saptamīṃ parām . . 34
1.64.d:
शृणुष्व गदतः काम्यानुपवासांस्तथापरान् ।
शृणु दिण्डे महापुण्यफलकां सप्तमीं पराम् ॥ 34
1.64.m: Listen as I proclaim other wish-fulfilling fasts as well; / listen, O Diṇḍi, to the supreme Saptamī yielding great merit as its fruit.

1.64.s:
ādityārādhanāyaināṃ sarvapāpaharāṃ śivām .
yāmupoṣya naro bhaktyā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ . . 35
1.64.d:
आदित्याराधनायैनां सर्वपापहरां शिवाम् ।
यामुपोष्य नरो भक्त्या मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ॥ 35
1.64.m: This auspicious [day] for propitiating Āditya removes all sins; / fasting on it with devotion, a man is freed from all grave sins.

1.64.s:
tathā lokamavāpnoti sūryasyāmitatejasaḥ .
atha bhādrapade māsi śuklapakṣe samāgate . . 36
1.64.d:
तथा लोकमवाप्नोति सूर्यस्यामिततेजसः ।
अथ भाद्रपदे मासि शुक्लपक्षे समागते ॥ 36
1.64.m: Likewise he attains the world of the Sun of boundless radiance. / Now, when the month of Bhādrapada has arrived in the bright fortnight,

1.64.s:
sopoṣyā prathamaṃ tāta vidhānaṃ śṛṇu tatra vai .
ayācitaṃ caturthyāṃ tu pañcamyāmekabhojanam . . 37
1.64.d:
सोपोष्या प्रथमं तात विधानं शृणु तत्र वै ।
अयाचितं चतुर्थ्यां तु पञ्चम्यामेकभोजनम् ॥ 37
1.64.m: it is to be fasted on first, my dear; hear indeed the rule for it: / unasked-for food on the fourth, and a single meal on the fifth,

1.64.s:
upavāsaparaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ .
arcayitvā dinakaraṃ gandhadhūpanivedanaiḥ . . 38
1.64.d:
उपवासपरः षष्ठ्यां जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः ।
अर्चयित्वा दिनकरं गन्धधूपनिवेदनैः ॥ 38
1.64.m: intent on fasting on the sixth, having conquered anger and subdued the senses, / having worshipped the Day-Maker with offerings of scent and incense,

1.64.s:
purataḥ sthaṇḍile rātrau svapyāddevasya putraka .
pradhyāyanmanasā devaṃ sarvabhūtārtināśanam . . 39
1.64.d:
पुरतः स्थण्डिले रात्रौ स्वप्याद्देवस्य पुत्रक ।
प्रध्यायन्मनसा देवं सर्वभूतार्तिनाशनम् ॥ 39
1.64.m: he should sleep at night on bare ground in front of the god, my son, / meditating in his mind upon the god who destroys the suffering of all beings,

1.64.s:
sarvadoṣapraśamanaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam .
vibuddhastvatha saptamyāṃ kuryādbrāhmaṇabhojanam . . 1.64.40
1.64.d:
सर्वदोषप्रशमनं सर्वपातकनाशनम् ।
विबुद्धस्त्वथ सप्तम्यां कुर्याद्ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ॥ 1.64.40
1.64.m: who pacifies all defects and destroys all grave sins. / Awakened, then on the seventh, he should feed Brahmins,

1.64.s:
pūjayitvā dinakaraṃ puṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ .
naivedyaṃ tāta devasya phalāni kathayanti4 hi . .4 1
kharjūranālikerāṇi tathā āmraphalāni tu .
mātuliṅgaphalānyeva kathitāni manīṣibhiḥ . . 42
1.64.d:
पूजयित्वा दिनकरं पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ।
नैवेद्यं तात देवस्य फलानि कथयन्ति4 हि ॥4 1
खर्जूरनालिकेराणि तथा आम्रफलानि तु ।
मातुलिङ्गफलान्येव कथितानि मनीषिभिः ॥ 42
1.64.m: having worshipped the Day-Maker with flowers, incense, and unguents. / Indeed, for food-offerings to the god, my dear, fruits are stated [by the wise]: / dates and coconuts, and likewise mango fruits; / citron fruits indeed have been spoken of by the wise.

1.64.s:
etaiśca bhojayedviprānātmanā ca prabhakṣayet .
tathaiṣāṃ cāpyabhāvena śṛṇu cānyāni suvrata . .4 3
śāligodhūmapiṣṭāni kārayedgaṇanāyaka .
guḍagarbhakṛtānīha ghṛtapākena pāvayet . .44
1.64.d:
एतैश्च भोजयेद्विप्रानात्मना च प्रभक्षयेत् ।
तथैषां चाप्यभावेन शृणु चान्यानि सुव्रत ॥4 3
शालिगोधूमपिष्टानि कारयेद्गणनायक ।
गुडगर्भकृतानीह घृतपाकेन पावयेत् ॥44
1.64.m: And with these he should feed the Brahmins, and partake of [them] himself. / Likewise, in the absence of these, hear of others, O one of good vows: / he should have flours of rice and wheat prepared, O leader of the Gaṇas; / made with fillings of jaggery, he should purify them here by frying in ghee.

1.64.s:
cāturyāvakamiśrāṇi ādityāya nivedayet .
agnikāryamatho kṛtvā brāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ . .45
1.64.d:
चातुर्यावकमिश्राणि आदित्याय निवेदयेत् ।
अग्निकार्यमथो कृत्वा ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्ततः ॥45
1.64.m: Mixed with barley-meal four times over, he should offer them to Āditya. / Then, having performed the fire-rite, he should feed the Brahmins thereafter.

1.64.s:
itthaṃ dvādaśa vai māsānkāryaṃ vratamanuttamam .
māsi māsi phalāhāraḥ phaladāyī phalārcanaḥ . .46
1.64.d:
इत्थं द्वादश वै मासान्कार्यं व्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
मासि मासि फलाहारः फलदायी फलार्चनः ॥46
1.64.m: In this way, this unexcelled votive observance is to be performed for twelve months, / eating fruit, giving fruit, and worshipping with fruit month by month.

1.64.s:
varṣānte tvatha kurvīta śaktyā brāhmaṇabhojanam .
snānaprāśanayoścāpi vidhānaṃ śṛṇu suvrata . . 47
1.64.d:
वर्षान्ते त्वथ कुर्वीत शक्त्या ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
स्नानप्राशनयोश्चापि विधानं शृणु सुव्रत ॥ 47
1.64.m: At the end of the year, however, he should feed Brahmins according to his capacity. / And listen to the rule for bathing and sipping [the sanctified substances], O one of good vows:

1.64.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam .
tilasarṣapayoḥ kalkaṃ śvetā mṛccāpi suvrata . .48
1.64.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् ।
तिलसर्षपयोः कल्कं श्वेता मृच्चापि सुव्रत ॥48
1.64.m: cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, water with kuśa grass, / paste of sesame and mustard, and white clay as well, O one of good vows,

1.64.s:
dūrvākalkaṃ ghṛtaṃ cāpi gośṛṃgakṣālitaṃ jalam .
jātigulmaviniryāsaḥ praśastaḥ snānakarmaṇi . . 49
1.64.d:
दूर्वाकल्कं घृतं चापि गोशृंगक्षालितं जलम् ।
जातिगुल्मविनिर्यासः प्रशस्तः स्नानकर्मणि ॥ 49
1.64.m: paste of dūrvā grass and ghee, and water washed over a cow's horn; / the sap of a jasmine shrub is praised in the rite of bathing.

1.64.s:
prāśane cāpyathaitāni sarvapāpaharāṇi vai .
ādau kṛtvā bhādrapadaṃ yathā saṃkhyaṃ vidurbudhāḥ . . 1.64.50
1.64.d:
प्राशने चाप्यथैतानि सर्वपापहराणि वै ।
आदौ कृत्वा भाद्रपदं यथा संख्यं विदुर्बुधाः ॥ 1.64.50
1.64.m: And in sipping too, these indeed remove all sins, / beginning with Bhādrapada, according to their number, the wise know.

1.64.s:
itthaṃ varṣāntamāsādya bhojayitvā dvijottamān .
divyānbhogānmahādeva tatastebhyo nivedayet . . 51
1.64.d:
इत्थं वर्षान्तमासाद्य भोजयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ।
दिव्यान्भोगान्महादेव ततस्तेभ्यो निवेदयेत् ॥ 51
1.64.m: In this way, having reached the end of the year and fed the best of the twice-born, / O Mahādeva, he should then present heavenly enjoyments to them:

1.64.s:
phalāni tāta1 haimāni yathā śaktyā gaṇādhipa .
savatsāmatha vā dhenuṃ bhūmiṃ sasyānvitāmatha . . 52
1.64.d:
फलानि तात1 हैमानि यथा शक्त्या गणाधिप ।
सवत्सामथ वा धेनुं भूमिं सस्यान्वितामथ ॥ 52
1.64.m: golden fruits, my dear, according to his capacity, O leader of the Gaṇas, / or a cow along with her calf, or land endowed with crops,

1.64.s:
prāsādamatha vā bhaumaṃ sarvadhānyasamanvitam .
dadyātchuklāni2 vastrāṇi tāmrapātraṃ 3savidrumam . . 53
1.64.d:
प्रासादमथ वा भौमं सर्वधान्यसमन्वितम् ।
दद्यात्छुक्लानि2 वस्त्राणि ताम्रपात्रं 3सविद्रुमम् ॥ 53
1.64.m: or an earthen mansion stocked with all grains. / He should give white clothes, and a copper vessel with coral.

1.64.s:
śaktiyuktasya caitāni daridrasya tu me śṛṇu .
phalāni piṣṭakānyeṣāṃ tilacūrṇānvitāni tu . . 54
1.64.d:
शक्तियुक्तस्य चैतानि दरिद्रस्य तु मे शृणु ।
फलानि पिष्टकान्येषां तिलचूर्णान्वितानि तु ॥ 54
1.64.m: And these [are for one] possessed of capacity; but hear from me for a poor man: / cakes made of these flours, mixed with sesame powder.

1.64.s:
bhojayitvā dvijāndadyādrājatāni4 phalāni tu .
dhāturaktaṃ vastrayugamamācāryāya nivedayet . . 55
1.64.d:
भोजयित्वा द्विजान्दद्याद्राजतानि4 फलानि तु ।
धातुरक्तं वस्त्रयुगममाचार्याय निवेदयेत् ॥ 55
1.64.m: Having fed the twice-born, he should give fruits of silver; / he should present a pair of garments dyed with red mineral pigment to the teacher,

1.64.s:
sahiraṇyaṃ mahādeva pañcaratnasamanvitam .
itthaṃ samāpyate tāta pāraṇaṃ vārṣikāntikam . . 56
1.64.d:
सहिरण्यं महादेव पञ्चरत्नसमन्वितम् ।
इत्थं समाप्यते तात पारणं वार्षिकान्तिकम् ॥ 56
1.64.m: together with gold, O Mahādeva, and accompanied by the five gems. / Thus is completed, my dear, the concluding fast-breaking at the year's end.

1.64.s:
ityeṣā vai puṇyatamā saptamī duritāpahā .
yāmupoṣya narāḥ sarve yānti sūryasalokatām . . 57
1.64.d:
इत्येषा वै पुण्यतमा सप्तमी दुरितापहा ।
यामुपोष्य नराः सर्वे यान्ति सूर्यसलोकताम् ॥ 57
1.64.m: In this manner, this most holy Saptamī dispels misfortune; / fasting on which, all men attain the world of the Sun.

1.64.s:
1pūjyamānaḥ sadā devairgandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ .
anayā mānavo nityaṃ pūjayedbhāskaraṃ sadā . . 58
1.64.d:
1पूज्यमानः सदा देवैर्गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणैः ।
अनया मानवो नित्यं पूजयेद्भास्करं सदा ॥ 58
1.64.m: Continuously worshipped by the gods and hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases, / through this [votive observance] a mortal should always worship the Sun perpetually.

1.64.s:
dāridyaduḥkhaduritairmukto yāti divākaram .
brāhmaṇo mokṣamāyāti kṣatriyaścendratāṃ vrajet . . 59
1.64.d:
दारिद्यदुःखदुरितैर्मुक्तो याति दिवाकरम् ।
ब्राह्मणो मोक्षमायाति क्षत्रियश्चेन्द्रतां व्रजेत् ॥ 59
1.64.m: Freed from poverty, sorrow, and misfortune, he goes to the Day-Maker. / A Brahmin attains liberation, and a Kṣatriya attains the status of Indra;

1.64.s:
vaiśyo dhanadasālokyaṃ śūdroḥ vipratvamāpnuyāt .
aputro labhate putraṃ durbhagā subhagā bhavet . . 1.64.60
1.64.d:
वैश्यो धनदसालोक्यं शूद्रोः विप्रत्वमाप्नुयात् ।
अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रं दुर्भगा सुभगा भवेत् ॥ 1.64.60
1.64.m: a Vaiśya attains the same world as the Giver of Wealth, and a Śūdra attains the status of a Brahmin. / A childless man obtains a son, and an unfortunate woman becomes fortunate.

1.64.s:
yāmupoṣya ca nārīmāṃ saptamīṃ lokapūjitām .
vidhavā vā satī bhaktyā anayā pūjayedravim . . 61
1.64.d:
यामुपोष्य च नारीमां सप्तमीं लोकपूजिताम् ।
विधवा वा सती भक्त्या अनया पूजयेद्रविम् ॥ 61
1.64.m: And whatever woman, having fasted on this Saptamī honoured by the worlds, / whether a widow or a virtuous wife, worships Ravi with devotion through this [votive observance],

1.64.s:
nānyajanmani vaidhavyaṃ nārī prāpnoti mānada .
cintāmaṇisamā hyeṣā vijñeyā phalasaptamī . . 62
1.64.d:
नान्यजन्मनि वैधव्यं नारी प्राप्नोति मानद ।
चिन्तामणिसमा ह्येषा विज्ञेया फलसप्तमी ॥ 62
1.64.m: no woman suffers widowhood in another birth, O giver of honour. / For this Phalasaptamī is to be understood as equal to a wish-fulfilling jewel.

1.64.s: paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ diṇḍe sarvakāmapradā smṛtā . . 63
1.64.d: पठतां शृण्वतां दिण्डे सर्वकामप्रदा स्मृता ॥ 63
1.64.m: It is traditionally remembered as granting all desires to those who read and hear [it], O Diṇḍi.

1.64.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi brahmadiṇḍisaṃvāde
saptamīkalpe phalasaptamīvarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāya . 64 .
ādityamāhātmyavarṇanam
1.64.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि ब्रह्मदिण्डिसंवादे
सप्तमीकल्पे फलसप्तमीवर्णनं नाम चतुःषष्टितमोऽध्याय । 64 ।
आदित्यमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
1.64.m:
Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter, named 'The Description of the Phalasaptamī' in the Section on the Saptamī, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Diṇḍi, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Glory of Āditya

1.65.s:
brahmovāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi rahasyāṃ nāma saptamīm .
saptamī kṛtamātreyaṃ narāṃstārayate bhavāt . . 1
1.65.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि रहस्यां नाम सप्तमीम् ।
सप्तमी कृतमात्रेयं नरांस्तारयते भवात् ॥ 1
1.65.m:
Brahmā said:
Next, I shall proclaim the saptamī known as Rahasyā.
Merely by being observed, this saptamī rescues men from worldly existence,

1.65.s:
saptāparānsapta pūrvānpitṝṃścāpi na saṃśayaḥ .
rogāṃśchinatti duśchedyāndurjayāñjayate hyarīn . . 2
1.65.d:
सप्तापरान्सप्त पूर्वान्पितॄंश्चापि न संशयः ।
रोगांश्छिनत्ति दुश्छेद्यान्दुर्जयाञ्जयते ह्यरीन् ॥ 2
1.65.m:
and seven future and seven past ancestors as well, without a doubt.
It severs diseases that are hard to sever, and conquers enemies that are hard to vanquish.

1.65.s:
arthānprāpnoti duṣprāpānyaḥ kuryānnāma saptamīm .
kanyārthī labhate kanyāṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam . . 3
1.65.d:
अर्थान्प्राप्नोति दुष्प्रापान्यः कुर्यान्नाम सप्तमीम् ।
कन्यार्थी लभते कन्यां धनार्थी लभते धनम् ॥ 3
1.65.m:
Whoever performs the Nāma-saptamī attains desires difficult to attain.
One who desires a maiden gains a maiden; one who desires wealth gains wealth;

1.65.s:
putrārthī labhate putrāndharmārthī dharmamāpnuyāt .
samayānpālayansarvānkuryāccemāṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ . .4
1.65.d:
पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रान्धर्मार्थी धर्ममाप्नुयात् ।
समयान्पालयन्सर्वान्कुर्याच्चेमां विचक्षणः ॥4
1.65.m:
one who desires sons gains sons; one who desires dharma attains dharma.
Observing all the rules, a wise person should perform this [observance].

1.65.s:
samayāñchṛṇu bhūteśa śreyase gadato mama .
ādityabhaktaḥ puruṣaḥ saptamyāṃ gaṇanāyaka . . 5
1.65.d:
समयाञ्छृणु भूतेश श्रेयसे गदतो मम ।
आदित्यभक्तः पुरुषः सप्तम्यां गणनायक ॥ 5
1.65.m:
Listen to the rules, O lord of beings, as I speak them for [your] welfare.
On the saptamī, O leader of the gaṇas, a man devoted to Āditya

1.65.s:
maitrīṃ sarvatra vai kuryādbhāskaraṃ vāpi ciṃtayet .
saptamyāṃ na spṛśettailaṃ nīlaṃ vastraṃ na dhārayet . .
na cāpyāmālakaiḥ snānaṃ na kuryātkalahaṃ kvacit . . 6
1.65.d:
मैत्रीं सर्वत्र वै कुर्याद्भास्करं वापि चिंतयेत् ।
सप्तम्यां न स्पृशेत्तैलं नीलं वस्त्रं न धारयेत् ॥
न चाप्यामालकैः स्नानं न कुर्यात्कलहं क्वचित् ॥ 6
1.65.m:
should cultivate friendliness toward all, or meditate upon the Sun.
On the saptamī, he must not touch oil, nor wear blue clothing,
nor bathe with āmalaka fruits, nor ever quarrel.

1.65.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
kimarthaṃ na spaśettailaṃ saptamyāṃ padmasaṃbhava . . 7
1.65.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
किमर्थं न स्पशेत्तैलं सप्तम्यां पद्मसंभव ॥ 7
1.65.m:
Diṇḍi said:
For what reason should one not touch oil on the saptamī, O lotus-born one?

1.65.s:
kaśca doṣo bhaveddeva nīlavastrasya dhāraṇāt .
brahmovāca
śṛṇu diṇḍe mahābāho nīlavastrasya dhāraṇe . . 8
1.65.d:
कश्च दोषो भवेद्देव नीलवस्त्रस्य धारणात् ।
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृणु दिण्डे महाबाहो नीलवस्त्रस्य धारणे ॥ 8
1.65.m:
And what fault arises, O god, from wearing blue clothing?
Brahmā said:
Listen, O mighty-armed Diṇḍi, to the fault in wearing blue clothing,

1.65.s:
dūṣaṇaṃ gaṇaśārdūla gadato mama kṛtsnaśaḥ .
pālanaṃ vikrayaścaiva sadvṛttirupajīvanam . . 9
1.65.d:
दूषणं गणशार्दूल गदतो मम कृत्स्नशः ।
पालनं विक्रयश्चैव सद्वृत्तिरुपजीवनम् ॥ 9
1.65.m:
O tiger among the gaṇas, as I speak it in full.
[Its] maintenance, sale, making it a regular trade, or living by it—

1.65.s:
patitastu bhavedviprastribhiḥ kṛcchairviśuddhyati .
nīlīraktena vastreṇa yatkarma kurute dvijaḥ . . 1.65.10
1.65.d:
पतितस्तु भवेद्विप्रस्त्रिभिः कृच्छैर्विशुद्ध्यति ।
नीलीरक्तेन वस्त्रेण यत्कर्म कुरुते द्विजः ॥ 1.65.10
1.65.m:
a brahmin [who does this] becomes fallen; he is purified by three kṛcchras.
Whatever rite a twice-born performs with cloth dyed in indigo—

1.65.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam .
vṛthā tasya mahāyajñā nīlasūtrasya dhāraṇāt . . 11
1.65.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायः पितृतर्पणम् ।
वृथा तस्य महायज्ञा नीलसूत्रस्य धारणात् ॥ 11
1.65.m:
bathing, giving, recitation, fire offering, Vedic study, and offering libations to the ancestors—
his great sacrifices become useless on account of wearing blue thread.

1.65.s:
nīlīraktaṃ yadā vastraṃ viprastvaṅgeṣu dhārayet .
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā pañcagavyena śuddhyati . . 12
1.65.d:
नीलीरक्तं यदा वस्त्रं विप्रस्त्वङ्गेषु धारयेत् ।
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा पञ्चगव्येन शुद्ध्यति ॥ 12
1.65.m:
When a brahmin wears cloth dyed in indigo on his limbs,
he is purified by pañcagavya after fasting for a day and night.

1.65.s:
romakūpe yadā gacchedraktaṃ nīlasya1 kasyacit .
patitastu bhavedviprastribhiḥ kṛcchrairviśuddhyati . . 13
1.65.d:
रोमकूपे यदा गच्छेद्रक्तं नीलस्य1 कस्यचित् ।
पतितस्तु भवेद्विप्रस्त्रिभिः कृच्छ्रैर्विशुद्ध्यति ॥ 13
1.65.m:
If the dye of indigo enters anyone's hair-follicle,
a brahmin becomes fallen; he is purified by three kṛcchras.

1.65.s:
nīlīmadhyaṃ yadā gacchetpramādādbrāhmaṇaḥ kvacit .
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā pañcagavyena śuddhyati . . 14
1.65.d:
नीलीमध्यं यदा गच्छेत्प्रमादाद्ब्राह्मणः क्वचित् ।
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा पञ्चगव्येन शुद्ध्यति ॥ 14
1.65.m:
If a brahmin should ever inadvertently walk amidst indigo [plants],
he is purified by pañcagavya after fasting for a day and night.

1.65.s:
nīlīdāru yadā bhiṃdyādbrāhmaṇānāṃ śarīrake .
śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yatra dvijaścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret . . 15
1.65.d:
नीलीदारु यदा भिंद्याद्ब्राह्मणानां शरीरके ।
शोणितं दृश्यते यत्र द्विजश्चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥ 15
1.65.m:
When an indigo stem pierces the body of brahmins
so that blood is seen, the twice-born should perform a cāndrāyaṇa.

1.65.s:
kuryādajñānato yastu nīlervā dantadhāvanam .
kṛtvā kṛcchradvayaṃ diṇḍe viśuddhaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ . . 16
1.65.d:
कुर्यादज्ञानतो यस्तु नीलेर्वा दन्तधावनम् ।
कृत्वा कृच्छ्रद्वयं दिण्डे विशुद्धः स्यान्न संशयः ॥ 16
1.65.m:
And he who out of ignorance cleans his teeth with indigo,
would become purified, O Diṇḍi, after performing two kṛcchras, without a doubt.

1.65.s:
vāpayedyatra nīlīṃ tu bhavettatrāśucirmahī .
pramāṇadvādaśābdāni tata ūrdhvaṃ śucirbhavet3 . . 17
1.65.d:
वापयेद्यत्र नीलीं तु भवेत्तत्राशुचिर्मही ।
प्रमाणद्वादशाब्दानि तत ऊर्ध्वं शुचिर्भवेत्3 ॥ 17
1.65.m:
Where one sows indigo, the earth there becomes impure
for the duration of twelve years; after that, it becomes pure.

1.65.s:
saptamyāṃ spṛśatastailamiṣṭā bhāryā vinaśyati .
ityeṣa nīlītailasya doṣaste kathito mayā . . 18
1.65.d:
सप्तम्यां स्पृशतस्तैलमिष्टा भार्या विनश्यति ।
इत्येष नीलीतैलस्य दोषस्ते कथितो मया ॥ 18
1.65.m:
For one who touches oil on the saptamī, his beloved wife perishes.
Thus has this fault of indigo and oil been told to you by me.

1.65.s:
na caiva khādenmāṃsāni madyāni na pibedbudhaḥ .
na drohaṃ kasyacitkuryānna pāruṣyaṃ samācaret . . 19
1.65.d:
न चैव खादेन्मांसानि मद्यानि न पिबेद्बुधः ।
न द्रोहं कस्यचित्कुर्यान्न पारुष्यं समाचरेत् ॥ 19
1.65.m:
A wise man must not eat meat, nor drink intoxicating beverages.
He must not bear malice toward anyone, nor practice harshness.

1.65.s:
nāvabhāṣeta cāṇḍālaṃ striyaṃ naiva rajasvalām .
na vāpi saṃspṛśeddhīnaṃ mṛtakaṃ nāvalokayet . . 1.65.20
1.65.d:
नावभाषेत चाण्डालं स्त्रियं नैव रजस्वलाम् ।
न वापि संस्पृशेद्धीनं मृतकं नावलोकयेत् ॥ 1.65.20
1.65.m:
He must not converse with a cāṇḍāla, nor with a menstruating woman;
nor should he touch an outcaste, nor look upon a corpse.

1.65.s:
nāsphoṭayennātihasedgāyeccāpi na gītakam .
na nṛtyedatirāgeṇa na ca vādyāni vādayet . . 21
1.65.d:
नास्फोटयेन्नातिहसेद्गायेच्चापि न गीतकम् ।
न नृत्येदतिरागेण न च वाद्यानि वादयेत् ॥ 21
1.65.m:
He should not clap his arms, nor laugh loudly, nor sing a song;
he should not dance with excessive passion, nor play musical instruments.

1.65.s:
na śayīta striyā sārdhaṃ na seveta durodaram .
na rudyādaśrupātena na ca vācyaṃ ca śaukikam . . 22
1.65.d:
न शयीत स्त्रिया सार्धं न सेवेत दुरोदरम् ।
न रुद्यादश्रुपातेन न च वाच्यं च शौकिकम् ॥ 22
1.65.m:
He should not lie down with a woman, nor indulge in gambling;
he should not weep with shedding of tears, nor speak words relating to profit.

1.65.s:
ākṛṣenna śiroyūkā na vṛthāvādamācaret .
parasyāniṣṭakathanamatiśokaṃ ca varjayet . . 23
1.65.d:
आकृषेन्न शिरोयूका न वृथावादमाचरेत् ।
परस्यानिष्टकथनमतिशोकं च वर्जयेत् ॥ 23
1.65.m:
He should not pull lice from his head, nor engage in idle dispute;
he should avoid speaking ill of another, and excessive grief.

1.65.s:
na kañcittāḍayejjantuṃ na kuryādatibhojanam .
na caiva hi divā svapnaṃ dambhaṃ śāṭhyaṃ ca varjayet . . 24
1.65.d:
न कञ्चित्ताडयेज्जन्तुं न कुर्यादतिभोजनम् ।
न चैव हि दिवा स्वप्नं दम्भं शाठ्यं च वर्जयेत् ॥ 24
1.65.m:
He should not strike any living being, nor overeat;
he must avoid sleeping by day, hypocrisy, and deceit.

1.65.s:
rathyāyāmaṭanaṃ vāpi yatnataḥ parivarjayet .
athāparo vidhiścātra śrūyatāṃ tripurāntaka . . 25
1.65.d:
रथ्यायामटनं वापि यत्नतः परिवर्जयेत् ।
अथापरो विधिश्चात्र श्रूयतां त्रिपुरान्तक ॥ 25
1.65.m:
He should also diligently avoid wandering about in the street.
Now hear another rule in this matter, O destroyer of Tripura.

1.65.s:
caitrātprabhṛti kartavyā sarvadā nāma saptamī .
dhāteti caitramāse tu pūjanīyo divākaraḥ . . 26
1.65.d:
चैत्रात्प्रभृति कर्तव्या सर्वदा नाम सप्तमी ।
धातेति चैत्रमासे तु पूजनीयो दिवाकरः ॥ 26
1.65.m:
Beginning from Caitra, the Nāma-saptamī should always be observed.
In the month of Caitra, the sun should be worshipped as Dhātṛ;

1.65.s:
aryameti ca vaiśākhe jyeṣṭhe mitraḥ prakīrtitaḥ .
āṣāḍhe varuṇo jñeya indro nabhasi kathyate . . 27
1.65.d:
अर्यमेति च वैशाखे ज्येष्ठे मित्रः प्रकीर्तितः ।
आषाढे वरुणो ज्ञेय इन्द्रो नभसि कथ्यते ॥ 27
1.65.m:
and as Aryaman in Vaiśākha; in Jyeṣṭha, he is proclaimed as Mitra;
in Āṣāḍha, he is to be known as Varuṇa; in Śrāvaṇa, he is called Indra;

1.65.s:
vivasvāṃśca nabhasye'tha parjanyośvayuji smṛtaḥ .
pūṣā kārttikamāse tu mārgaśīrṣeṣurucyate . . 28
1.65.d:
विवस्वांश्च नभस्येऽथ पर्जन्योश्वयुजि स्मृतः ।
पूषा कार्त्तिकमासे तु मार्गशीर्षेषुरुच्यते ॥ 28
1.65.m:
and Vivasvat in Bhādrapada; in Āśvina, he is remembered as Parjanya;
Pūṣan in the month of Kārttika; in Mārgaśīrṣa, he is called Aṃśu;

1.65.s:
bhagaḥ pauṣe bhavetpūjyastvaṣṭā māghe tu śasyate .
viṣṇuśca phālgune māsi pūjyo vandyaśca bhāskaraḥ . . 29
1.65.d:
भगः पौषे भवेत्पूज्यस्त्वष्टा माघे तु शस्यते ।
विष्णुश्च फाल्गुने मासि पूज्यो वन्द्यश्च भास्करः ॥ 29
1.65.m:
in Pauṣa, Bhaga should be worshipped; Tvaṣṭṛ is praised in Māgha;
and in the month of Phālguna, the Sun is to be worshipped and revered as Viṣṇu.

1.65.s:
saptamyāṃ caiva saptamyāṃ bhojayedbhojakānbudhaḥ1 .
saghṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ deyaṃ bhojayitvā vidhānataḥ . . 1.65.30
1.65.d:
सप्तम्यां चैव सप्तम्यां भोजयेद्भोजकान्बुधः1 ।
सघृतं भोजनं देयं भोजयित्वा विधानतः ॥ 1.65.30
1.65.m:
On every saptamī, the wise man should feed Bhojakas.
Food with clarified butter should be offered after feeding them according to the injunctions.

1.65.s:
bhojakāyaiva viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ svarṇamāṣakam .
saghṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ deyaṃ raktavastrāṇi caiva hi . . 31
1.65.d:
भोजकायैव विप्राय दक्षिणां स्वर्णमाषकम् ।
सघृतं भोजनं देयं रक्तवस्त्राणि चैव हि ॥ 31
1.65.m:
A fee of a golden māṣaka should be given to the Bhojaka brahmin,
along with food accompanied by clarified butter and red garments.

1.65.s:
abhāve bhojakānāṃ tu dakṣiṇīyā dvijottamāḥ .
tathaiva bhojanīyāśca śraddhayā parayā vibho . . 32
1.65.d:
अभावे भोजकानां तु दक्षिणीया द्विजोत्तमाः ।
तथैव भोजनीयाश्च श्रद्धया परया विभो ॥ 32
1.65.m:
In the absence of Bhojakas, the best of twice-borns should receive the fees;
and they should likewise be fed with supreme faith, O mighty one.

1.65.s:
viśeṣato vācakaśca bāhmaṇaḥ kalpavitsadā .
ityeṣā kathitā tubhyaṃ saptamī gaṇanāyaka . . 33
1.65.d:
विशेषतो वाचकश्च बाह्मणः कल्पवित्सदा ।
इत्येषा कथिता तुभ्यं सप्तमी गणनायक ॥ 33
1.65.m:
Especially a reciter who is a brahmin, always knowledgeable in ritual procedure.
Thus this saptamī has been recounted to you, O leader of the gaṇas;

1.65.s:
śrutā satī pāpaharā sūryalokapradāyinī . . 34
yājñavalkyavarṇanam
1.65.d:
श्रुता सती पापहरा सूर्यलोकप्रदायिनी ॥ 34
याज्ञवल्क्यवर्णनम्
1.65.m:
when heard, it removes sin and bestows the realm of the Sun.
Description of Yājñavalkya

1.66.s:
sumanturuvāca
ityuktvā bhagavānbrahmā jagāmādarśanaṃ vibhoḥ 3 .
sūryamārādhayaddiṇḍī4 sūryasyānucaro'bhavat . . 1
1.66.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्ब्रह्मा जगामादर्शनं विभोः 3 ।
सूर्यमाराधयद्दिण्डी4 सूर्यस्यानुचरोऽभवत् ॥ 1
1.66.m:
Sumantu said:
Having spoken thus, the blessed Brahmā vanished from the sight of the lord.
Diṇḍi worshipped the Sun and became an attendant of the Sun.

1.66.s:
śatānīka uvāca
bhūyaḥ kathaya viprendra māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasya me .
śṛṇvato nāsti me tṛptiramṛtasyeva suvrata . . 2
1.66.d:
शतानीक उवाच
भूयः कथय विप्रेन्द्र माहात्म्यं भास्करस्य मे ।
शृण्वतो नास्ति मे तृप्तिरमृतस्येव सुव्रत ॥ 2
1.66.m:
Śatānīka said:
Tell me further, O best of brahmins, the majesty of the Sun.
As I listen, there is no satiety for me, as if with nectar, O one of good vows.

1.66.s:
sumanturuvāca
śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājansamvādaṃ dvijaśaṅkhayoḥ .
yaṃ śrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate mānavo1 nṛpa . . 3
1.66.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
शृणुष्वावहितो राजन्सम्वादं द्विजशङ्खयोः ।
यं श्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते मानवो1 नृप ॥ 3
1.66.m:
Sumantu said:
Listen attentively, O king, to the dialogue between the twice-born and Śaṅkha,
hearing which a mortal is freed from all sins, O king.

1.66.s:
āsīnamāśrame śaṃkhaṃ dvijo draṣṭuṃ jagāma ha .
phalabhārānatacchāye vṛkṣavṛndasamākule . . 4
1.66.d:
आसीनमाश्रमे शंखं द्विजो द्रष्टुं जगाम ह ।
फलभारानतच्छाये वृक्षवृन्दसमाकुले ॥ 4
1.66.m:
A twice-born went to see Śaṅkha seated in his hermitage,
which was crowded with groves of trees bent low under the weight of fruits and casting shade;

1.66.s:
parasparamṛgaśṛṅgakaṇḍūyitamṛgāvṛte .
barhirvanāmbarānītatīrthakandopabhogini . . 5
1.66.d:
परस्परमृगशृङ्गकण्डूयितमृगावृते ।
बर्हिर्वनाम्बरानीततीर्थकन्दोपभोगिनि ॥ 5
1.66.m:
filled with deer scratching each other with their horns;
enjoying holy roots brought from peacock-inhabited forest clearings;

1.66.s:
prabhūtakusumāmodaṣaṭpadodgītaśālinī .
siddhadevarṣigandharvatīrthasevitavāriṇi . . 6
1.66.d:
प्रभूतकुसुमामोदषट्पदोद्गीतशालिनी ।
सिद्धदेवर्षिगन्धर्वतीर्थसेवितवारिणि ॥ 6
1.66.m:
resplendent with the hum of bees drawn by the fragrance of abundant flowers;
its waters frequented by siddhas, celestial sages, gandharvas, and sacred bathing places;

1.66.s:
muṇḍaiśca jaṭilaiścaiva tāpasairupaśobhite .
āśrame taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ śaṃkhāhvaṃ sukhamāsthitam . . 7
1.66.d:
मुण्डैश्च जटिलैश्चैव तापसैरुपशोभिते ।
आश्रमे तं मुनिश्रेष्ठं शंखाह्वं सुखमास्थितम् ॥ 7
1.66.m:
adorned with ascetics, both shaven-headed and with matted hair.
[He saw] that best of sages named Śaṅkha comfortably seated in the hermitage,

1.66.s:
stotraiḥ stotuṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ tadbhaktaṃ tatparāyaṇam .
tataḥ saṃhatya sahasā taṃ bhojakakumārakāḥ . . 8
1.66.d:
स्तोत्रैः स्तोतुं सहस्रांशुं तद्भक्तं तत्परायणम् ।
ततः संहत्य सहसा तं भोजककुमारकाः ॥ 8
1.66.m:
devoted to Him and intent on Him, in order to praise the Thousand-rayed One with hymns.
Then, gathering together at once, young Bhojaka boys

1.66.s:
vinītā upasaṃgamya yathāvadabhivādya ca .
āsaneṣūpaviṣṭāsta upaviṣṭamathābruvan . . 9
1.66.d:
विनीता उपसंगम्य यथावदभिवाद्य च ।
आसनेषूपविष्टास्त उपविष्टमथाब्रुवन् ॥ 9
1.66.m:
approached humbly and greeted [him] properly.
Seated on their seats, they spoke to him who was seated.

1.66.s:
bhagavantsarvavedeṣu2 cchiṃdhi naḥ saṃśayo mahān .
vinayenopapannānāṃ kumārāṇāṃ tato muniḥ . . 1.66.10
1.66.d:
भगवन्त्सर्ववेदेषु2 च्छिंधि नः संशयो महान् ।
विनयेनोपपन्नानां कुमाराणां ततो मुनिः ॥ 1.66.10
1.66.m: "O venerable one, dispel our great doubt regarding all the Vedas!" / Then the sage, to the youths endowed with humility,

1.66.s:
anādīṃścaturo vedānuvāca prītamānasaḥ .
teṣāṃ tu paṭhatāmeva āśramaṃ tu yadṛcchayā . . 11
1.66.d:
अनादींश्चतुरो वेदानुवाच प्रीतमानसः ।
तेषां तु पठतामेव आश्रमं तु यदृच्छया ॥ 11
1.66.m: spoke the four beginningless Vedas with a joyful mind. / But while they were indeed reciting, by chance to the hermitage

1.66.s:
muniśreṣṭho'tha taṃ deśamājagāma dvijo nṛpa .
yathāvadarcitastena śaṅkhenāmitatejasā . . 12
1.66.d:
मुनिश्रेष्ठोऽथ तं देशमाजगाम द्विजो नृप ।
यथावदर्चितस्तेन शङ्खेनामिततेजसा ॥ 12
1.66.m: a best of sages, a twice-born, came to that place, O king. / Duly honoured by him, by Śaṅkha of boundless splendour,

1.66.s:
vanditaśca kumāraistairabhavatprītamānasaḥ .
athaitānabravīcchaṃkhastānbhojakakumārakān . . 13
1.66.d:
वन्दितश्च कुमारैस्तैरभवत्प्रीतमानसः ।
अथैतानब्रवीच्छंखस्तान्भोजककुमारकान् ॥ 13
1.66.m: and saluted by those youths, he became pleased in mind. / Then Śaṅkha spoke to those Bhojaka youths:

1.66.s:
śiṣṭāgamādanadhyāyaḥ sa ca jāto viramyatām .
yathājñāpayasītyāhuḥ kumārāste ṛṣiṃ tataḥ . . 14
1.66.d:
शिष्टागमादनध्यायः स च जातो विरम्यताम् ।
यथाज्ञापयसीत्याहुः कुमारास्ते ऋषिं ततः ॥ 14
1.66.m: "Because of the arrival of an honoured guest, study is suspended; that has occurred, so let it cease." / "As you command," the youths then said to the Ṛṣi.

1.66.s:
prapaccha siddhidaścaitānke hyete kiṃ paṭhanti ca .
śaṅkhovāca mahārāja kumārā bhojakātmajāḥ . . 15
1.66.d:
प्रपच्छ सिद्धिदश्चैतान्के ह्येते किं पठन्ति च ।
शङ्खोवाच महाराज कुमारा भोजकात्मजाः ॥ 15
1.66.m: The granter of perfection asked them: "Who are these, and what do they study?" / Śaṅkha said, "O great king, these youths are the sons of Bhojakas.

1.66.s:
sasūtrakalpāṃścaturo vipra vedānadhīyate .
tathaiva saptamīkalpe paricaryāṃ ca bhāsvataḥ . . 16
1.66.d:
ससूत्रकल्पांश्चतुरो विप्र वेदानधीयते ।
तथैव सप्तमीकल्पे परिचर्यां च भास्वतः ॥ 16
1.66.m: They are studying, O brāhmaṇa, the four Vedas along with their sūtras and ritual manuals, / and likewise the service to the Sun according to the manual of the seventh lunar day,

1.66.s:
agnikāryavidhānaṃ ca pratiṣṭhākalpamāditaḥ .
adhyaṅgalakṣaṇaṃ 1 brahman rathayātrāvidhiṃ tathā . . 17
1.66.d:
अग्निकार्यविधानं च प्रतिष्ठाकल्पमादितः ।
अध्यङ्गलक्षणं 1 ब्रह्मन् रथयात्राविधिं तथा ॥ 17
1.66.m: the injunction for fire-offerings, the manual for consecration from the beginning, / the characteristics of subordinate limbs, O brāhmaṇa, and the rules for chariot processions."

1.66.s:
dvija uvāca
kathaṃ kriyeta saptamyāṃ kabhrārcanavidhikramaḥ .
gandhapuṣpapradīpānāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ ravimandire . . 18
1.66.d:
द्विज उवाच
कथं क्रियेत सप्तम्यां कभ्रार्चनविधिक्रमः ।
गन्धपुष्पप्रदीपानां किं फलं रविमन्दिरे ॥ 18
1.66.m: The twice-born said: / "How should the procedure for worshipping the Sun on the seventh lunar day be performed? / What is the fruit of fragrant ointments, flowers, and lamps in the temple of the Sun?

1.66.s:
kena tuṣyati dānena vratena niyamena ca .
dhūpapuṣpopahārādi kiṃ ca deyaṃ vivasvate . . 19
1.66.d:
केन तुष्यति दानेन व्रतेन नियमेन च ।
धूपपुष्पोपहारादि किं च देयं विवस्वते ॥ 19
1.66.m: By what gift, votive observance, and restraint is he pleased? / And what incense, flowers, food-offerings, and the like should be given to Vivasvat?

1.66.s:
etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tanme brūhi tapodhana .
viśeṣatastu māhātmyaṃ brūhi māṃ bhāskarasya hi . . 1.66.20
1.66.d:
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन ।
विशेषतस्तु माहात्म्यं ब्रूहि मां भास्करस्य हि ॥ 1.66.20
1.66.m: This I wish to hear; tell me that, O you whose wealth is asceticism. / Especially, indeed, tell me the greatness of the Sun."

1.66.s:
śaṅkha uvāca
imamarthaṃ vaśiṣṭhena pṛṣṭaḥ sāmbo yathā purā .
sa covāca vaśiṣṭhāya tadahaṃ kathayāmi te . . 21
1.66.d:
शङ्ख उवाच
इममर्थं वशिष्ठेन पृष्टः साम्बो यथा पुरा ।
स चोवाच वशिष्ठाय तदहं कथयामि ते ॥ 21
1.66.m: Śaṅkha said: / "Regarding this matter, just as Sāmba was asked in ancient times by Vasiṣṭha, / and what he said to Vasiṣṭha, that I shall narrate to you.

1.66.s:
atrāśrame puṇyatame tīrthānāmuttame prabhuḥ .
vavande niyatātmānaṃ vaśiṣṭhaṃ munisattamam . . 22
1.66.d:
अत्राश्रमे पुण्यतमे तीर्थानामुत्तमे प्रभुः ।
ववन्दे नियतात्मानं वशिष्ठं मुनिसत्तमम् ॥ 22
1.66.m: In this most holy hermitage, the best among sacred places, the master / saluted the self-restrained Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages.

1.66.s:
vinayenopasaṃgamya vavande caraṇau muneḥ .
kṛtapraṇāmaṃ sāmbaṃ tu bhaktiprahvīkṛtānanam . . 23
1.66.d:
विनयेनोपसंगम्य ववन्दे चरणौ मुनेः ।
कृतप्रणामं साम्बं तु भक्तिप्रह्वीकृताननम् ॥ 23
1.66.m: Approaching with humility, he bowed to the feet of the sage. / Seeing Sāmba who had made his obeisance, his face bowed in devotion,

1.66.s:
vilokya paramaprīto muniḥ papraccha taṃ tadā .
sarvataḥ sphuṭitaṃ gātraṃ kuṣṭhena mahatā tava . . 24
1.66.d:
विलोक्य परमप्रीतो मुनिः पप्रच्छ तं तदा ।
सर्वतः स्फुटितं गात्रं कुष्ठेन महता तव ॥ 24
1.66.m: the sage, exceedingly pleased, then asked him: / 'Your body was cracked everywhere by great leprosy

1.66.s:
ghorarūpeṇa tīvreṇa kathaṃ tadvigataṃ tava1 .
kathaṃ ca lakṣmīradhikā rūpaṃ cātimanoharam . . 25
1.66.d:
घोररूपेण तीव्रेण कथं तद्विगतं तव1 ।
कथं च लक्ष्मीरधिका रूपं चातिमनोहरम् ॥ 25
1.66.m: of dreadful form and fierce; how has that departed from you? / And how is there this extraordinary splendour and most charming beauty,

1.66.s: tejasvitātimahatī tathaiva2 sukumāratā . . 26
1.66.d: तेजस्वितातिमहती तथैव2 सुकुमारता ॥ 26
1.66.m: immense radiance, and likewise such tenderness?'

1.66.s:
sāmba uvāca
stuto nāmasahasreṇa lokanātho divākaraḥ .
darśanaṃ ca gataḥ sākṣāddattavāṃśca varānmama . . 27
1.66.d:
साम्ब उवाच
स्तुतो नामसहस्रेण लोकनाथो दिवाकरः ।
दर्शनं च गतः साक्षाद्दत्तवांश्च वरान्मम ॥ 27
1.66.m: Sāmba said: / 'Praised with a thousand names, the Sun, the lord of the world, / came visibly before my eyes and granted me boons.'

1.66.s:
vaśiṣṭha uvāca
kathamārādhitaḥ sūryastvayā yādavanaṃdana .
kaiśca vratatapodānairdarśanaṃ bhagavāngataḥ . . 28
1.66.d:
वशिष्ठ उवाच
कथमाराधितः सूर्यस्त्वया यादवनंदन ।
कैश्च व्रततपोदानैर्दर्शनं भगवान्गतः ॥ 28
1.66.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / 'How was the Sun propitiated by you, O delighter of the Yādavas? / And by what votive observances, austerities, and gifts did the blessed one appear before you?'

1.66.s:
sāmba uvāca
śṛṇuṣvāvahito brahmansarvameva mayā yathā .
toṣito bhagavānsūryo vidhinā yena suvrata . . 29
1.66.d:
साम्ब उवाच
शृणुष्वावहितो ब्रह्मन्सर्वमेव मया यथा ।
तोषितो भगवान्सूर्यो विधिना येन सुव्रत ॥ 29
1.66.m: Sāmba said: / 'Listen attentively, O brāhmaṇa, O you of noble vows, to all of how / the blessed Sun was pleased by me, [and] by what procedure.

1.66.s:
mohānmayopahasito3 durvāsāḥ kopano muniḥ .
tato'haṃ tasya śāpena mahākuṣṭhamavāptavān . . 1.66.30
1.66.d:
मोहान्मयोपहसितो3 दुर्वासाः कोपनो मुनिः ।
ततोऽहं तस्य शापेन महाकुष्ठमवाप्तवान् ॥ 1.66.30
1.66.m: Out of delusion, the irascible sage Durvāsas was mocked by me; / then, by his curse, I contracted severe leprosy.

1.66.s:
tato'haṃ pitaraṃ gatvā kuṣṭhayogābhipīḍitaḥ .
lajjamāno'tigarveṇa idaṃ vākyamathābravam . . 31
1.66.d:
ततोऽहं पितरं गत्वा कुष्ठयोगाभिपीडितः ।
लज्जमानोऽतिगर्वेण इदं वाक्यमथाब्रवम् ॥ 31
1.66.m: Then, afflicted by the onset of leprosy, / feeling ashamed because of my excessive pride, I went to my father and spoke these words:

1.66.s:
tāta sīdati me gātraṃ svaraśca parihīyate .
ghorarūpo mahāvyādhirvapureṣa jighāṃsati . . 32
1.66.d:
तात सीदति मे गात्रं स्वरश्च परिहीयते ।
घोररूपो महाव्याधिर्वपुरेष जिघांसति ॥ 32
1.66.m: "Father, my body is failing, and my voice is wasting away; / this terrible, great disease wishes to destroy my form.

1.66.s:
aśeṣavyādhirājñāhaṃ pīḍitaḥ krūrakarmaṇā .
vaidyairoṣadhibhiścaiva na śāntirmama vidyate . . 33
1.66.d:
अशेषव्याधिराज्ञाहं पीडितः क्रूरकर्मणा ।
वैद्यैरोषधिभिश्चैव न शान्तिर्मम विद्यते ॥ 33
1.66.m: I am afflicted by the king of all diseases, through cruel action; / neither by physicians nor by medicines is there any relief for me.

1.66.s:
so'haṃ tvayā hyanujñātastyaktumicchāmi jīvitam .
yadi vāhamanugrāhyastato'nujñātumarhasi . . 34
1.66.d:
सोऽहं त्वया ह्यनुज्ञातस्त्यक्तुमिच्छामि जीवितम् ।
यदि वाहमनुग्राह्यस्ततोऽनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ॥ 34
1.66.m: Thus, permitted by you, I wish to abandon my life. / Or, if I am worthy of your grace, then please grant me permission."

1.66.s:
ityuktavākyaḥ sa pitā ṣutraśokābhipīḍitaḥ .
pitā kṣaṇaṃ tato dhyātvā māmevaṃ vākyamuktavān . . 35
1.66.d:
इत्युक्तवाक्यः स पिता षुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः ।
पिता क्षणं ततो ध्यात्वा मामेवं वाक्यमुक्तवान् ॥ 35
1.66.m: Addressed with these words, his father, afflicted with grief for his son, / having reflected for a moment, then spoke these words to me:

1.66.s:
dhairyamāśrayatāṃ1 putra mā śoke ca manaḥ kṛthāḥ .
hanti śokārditaṃ vyādhiḥ śuṣkaṃ tṛṇamivānalaḥ . . 36
1.66.d:
धैर्यमाश्रयतां1 पुत्र मा शोके च मनः कृथाः ।
हन्ति शोकार्दितं व्याधिः शुष्कं तृणमिवानलः ॥ 36
1.66.m: "Resort to courage, my son; do not set your mind on grief. / Disease destroys one afflicted by sorrow, as fire destroys dry grass.

1.66.s:
devatārādhanaparo bhava putraka mā śucaḥ .
ityukte ca mayā prokto devamārādhayāmi kam . . 37
1.66.d:
देवताराधनपरो भव पुत्रक मा शुचः ।
इत्युक्ते च मया प्रोक्तो देवमाराधयामि कम् ॥ 37
1.66.m: Be devoted to worshipping the gods, dear son; do not grieve." / When this was said, he was asked by me: "Which deity should I worship?

1.66.s:
kamārādhya vimucye'haṃ tāta rogaiḥ samantataḥ .
ityevamukto bhagavānmāmuvāca pitā mama . . 38
1.66.d:
कमाराध्य विमुच्येऽहं तात रोगैः समन्ततः ।
इत्येवमुक्तो भगवान्मामुवाच पिता मम ॥ 38
1.66.m: Having worshipped whom may I be entirely freed from diseases, father?" / Thus addressed, my venerable father said to me:

1.66.s:
imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭaḥ padmayoniḥ sanātanaḥ .
yājñavalkyena ṛṣiṇā yogīśena mahātmanā2 . . 39
1.66.d:
इममर्थं पुरा पृष्टः पद्मयोनिः सनातनः ।
याज्ञवल्क्येन ऋषिणा योगीशेन महात्मना2 ॥ 39
1.66.m: "Regarding this matter, in ancient times the eternal Lotus-born one was asked / by the great-souled sage Yājñavalkya, the lord of yogins.

1.66.s:
yaduvāca mahātejāstasmai sa yadunandana .
tacchṛṇuṣva śucirbhūtvā ātmanaḥ śreyase suta . . 1.66.40
1.66.d:
यदुवाच महातेजास्तस्मै स यदुनन्दन ।
तच्छृणुष्व शुचिर्भूत्वा आत्मनः श्रेयसे सुत ॥ 1.66.40
1.66.m: What that one of great splendour said to him, O delighter of the Yadus, / listen to that, having become pure, for your own welfare, my son.

1.66.s:
surajyeṣṭhaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ padmayoniṃ prajāpatim .
yājñavalkyo mahātejāḥ paryapṛcchatpitāmaham . . 41
1.66.d:
सुरज्येष्ठं सुखासीनं पद्मयोनिं प्रजापतिम् ।
याज्ञवल्क्यो महातेजाः पर्यपृच्छत्पितामहम् ॥ 41
1.66.m: To the eldest of gods, seated comfortably, the Lotus-born Prajāpati, / Yājñavalkya of great splendour questioned the Grandfather:

1.66.s:
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi kiṃcidātmamanogatam .
samārādhya vibho devaṃ naro mucyeta vai bhavāt . . 42
1.66.d:
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि किंचिदात्ममनोगतम् ।
समाराध्य विभो देवं नरो मुच्येत वै भवात् ॥ 42
1.66.m: 'O venerable one, I wish to hear something that is in my mind: / having propitiated which god, O all-pervading one, might a man be liberated from worldly existence?

1.66.s:
gṛhastho brahmacārī vā vānaprastho'tha bhikṣukaḥ .
ya icchenmokṣamāsthātuṃ devatāṃ kāṃ yajeta saḥ . . 43
1.66.d:
गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी वा वानप्रस्थोऽथ भिक्षुकः ।
य इच्छेन्मोक्षमास्थातुं देवतां कां यजेत सः ॥ 43
1.66.m: Whether a householder, a student, a forest-dweller, or a mendicant, / he who wishes to attain liberation, what deity should he worship?

1.66.s:
kuto hyasya dhruvaḥ svargaḥ kuto naiḥ śreyasaṃ sukham .
svargataścaiva kiṃ kuryādyena na cyavate punaḥ . . 44
1.66.d:
कुतो ह्यस्य ध्रुवः स्वर्गः कुतो नैः श्रेयसं सुखम् ।
स्वर्गतश्चैव किं कुर्याद्येन न च्यवते पुनः ॥ 44
