1.66.m: Whence is his firm heaven, and whence the happiness of the highest good? / And having gone to heaven, what should one do so that he does not fall again?

1.66.s:
devātānāṃ tu ko devaḥ pitṝṇāṃ caiva kaḥ pitā .
tasmātparataraṃ yacca tanme brūhi pitāmaha . . 45
1.66.d:
देवातानां तु को देवः पितॄणां चैव कः पिता ।
तस्मात्परतरं यच्च तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥ 45
1.66.m: Who is the god of the gods, and who is the father of the ancestors? / And that which is higher than that, tell me that, O Grandfather!

1.66.s:
kena sṛṣṭamidaṃ viśvaṃ brahmansthāvarajaṅgamam .
pralayo ca kamabhyeti tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi . . 46
1.66.d:
केन सृष्टमिदं विश्वं ब्रह्मन्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
प्रलयो च कमभ्येति तन्मे त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 46
1.66.m: By whom was this universe created, O brāhmaṇa, both stationary and moving? / And to whom does it go at the dissolution? You ought to tell me that.'

1.66.s:
brahmovāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhavatā tuṣṭaścāsmi mahāmate .
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ puṇyottaramanuttamam . . 47
1.66.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि भवता तुष्टश्चास्मि महामते ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं पुण्योत्तरमनुत्तमम् ॥ 47
1.66.m: Brahmā said: / 'I have been well questioned by you, and I am pleased, O you of noble intellect! / Having bowed with the head to the god who is the highest holiness, beyond whom there is none,

1.66.s:
kathayiṣye dvijaśreṣṭha śṛṇuṣvaikamanādhunā .
ātmanaḥ śreyase vipra śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ . .48
1.66.d:
कथयिष्ये द्विजश्रेष्ठ शृणुष्वैकमनाधुना ।
आत्मनः श्रेयसे विप्र शुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः ॥48
1.66.m: I shall tell you, O best of the twice-born; listen now with a single mind / for your own highest good, O brāhmaṇa, having become pure and concentrated.

1.66.s:
udyanya eṣa kurute jagadvitimiraṃ karaiḥ .
nātaḥ parataro devaḥ kimanyatkathayāmi te . .4 9
anādi nidhano hyeṣaḥ puruṣaḥ śāśvato'vyayaḥ .
dīpayatyeva lokāṃstrīnravī raśmibhirulbaṇaiḥ . . 1.66.50
1.66.d:
उद्यन्य एष कुरुते जगद्वितिमिरं करैः ।
नातः परतरो देवः किमन्यत्कथयामि ते ॥4 9
अनादि निधनो ह्येषः पुरुषः शाश्वतोऽव्ययः ।
दीपयत्येव लोकांस्त्रीन्रवी रश्मिभिरुल्बणैः ॥ 1.66.50
1.66.m: He who, rising, makes the world free of darkness with his rays— / there is no god higher than him; what else shall I tell you? / For he is the beginningless and endless person, eternal and imperishable; / the Sun illuminates the three worlds with his fierce rays.

1.66.s:
sarvadevātmako hyeṣa tapasā cāṃśutāpanaḥ .
sarvasya jagato nāthaḥ karmasākṣī śubhāśubhe . . 51
1.66.d:
सर्वदेवात्मको ह्येष तपसा चांशुतापनः ।
सर्वस्य जगतो नाथः कर्मसाक्षी शुभाशुभे ॥ 51
1.66.m: For he is the self of all gods, and through austerity he scorches with his rays; / he is the lord of the entire world, the witness of actions, good and bad.

1.66.s:
kṣapayatyeṣa bhūtāni tathā visṛjate punaḥ .
eṣa bhāti tapatyeṣa vardhate ca gabhastibhiḥ . . 52
1.66.d:
क्षपयत्येष भूतानि तथा विसृजते पुनः ।
एष भाति तपत्येष वर्धते च गभस्तिभिः ॥ 52
1.66.m: He dissolves living beings, and likewise emits them again; / he shines, he scorches, and he thrives with his rays.

1.66.s:
eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca pūṣā1 prakṛtibhāvana .
na hyeṣa kṣayamāyāti nityamakṣayamaṇḍalaḥ . . 53
1.66.d:
एष धाता विधाता च पूषा1 प्रकृतिभावन ।
न ह्येष क्षयमायाति नित्यमक्षयमण्डलः ॥ 53
1.66.m: He is the creator and the ordainer, Pūṣan, the promoter of nature; / for he never comes to destruction, his orb being ever imperishable.

1.66.s:
pitṝṇāṃ hi pitā devatānāṃ ca devatā .
dhruvaṃ sthānaṃ smṛtaṃ hyeṣa ādhāro jagatastathā . . 54
1.66.d:
पितॄणां हि पिता देवतानां च देवता ।
ध्रुवं स्थानं स्मृतं ह्येष आधारो जगतस्तथा ॥ 54
1.66.m: He is indeed the father of the ancestors, and the deity of the deities; / for he is considered the firm abode, and likewise the support of the world.

1.66.s:
sarvakāle jagatkṛtsnamādityātsaṃprasūyate .
pralaye ca tamabhyeti ādityaṃ dīptatejasam . . 55
1.66.d:
सर्वकाले जगत्कृत्स्नमादित्यात्संप्रसूयते ।
प्रलये च तमभ्येति आदित्यं दीप्ततेजसम् ॥ 55
1.66.m: At all times the entire world is brought forth from the Sun, / and at the dissolution it goes into the Sun of blazing splendour.'

1.66.s:
yoginaścātra saṃlīnāstyaktvā gṛhakalevaram .
vāyubhūtā viśantyasmiṃstejorāśau divākare . . 56
1.66.d:
योगिनश्चात्र संलीनास्त्यक्त्वा गृहकलेवरम् ।
वायुभूता विशन्त्यस्मिंस्तेजोराशौ दिवाकरे ॥ 56
1.66.m: And yogins, having cast off their body, this house, merge here; / having become wind, they enter into this mass of splendour, the sun.

1.66.s:
tasya raśmisahasrāṇi śākhā iva vihaṃgamāḥ .
vasantyāśritya munayaḥ saṃsiddhā daivataiḥ saha . . 57
1.66.d:
तस्य रश्मिसहस्राणि शाखा इव विहंगमाः ।
वसन्त्याश्रित्य मुनयः संसिद्धा दैवतैः सह ॥ 57
1.66.m: Relying on his thousands of rays as birds [rely] on branches, / the perfected sages dwell together with the deities.

1.66.s:
janakādayo gṛhasthāstu rājāno yogadharmiṇaḥ .
vālakhilyādayaścaiva munayo brahmacāriṇaḥ . . 58
1.66.d:
जनकादयो गृहस्थास्तु राजानो योगधर्मिणः ।
वालखिल्यादयश्चैव मुनयो ब्रह्मचारिणः ॥ 58
1.66.m: Householder kings who practiced yoga, such as Janaka and others, / and celibate sages such as the Vālakhilyas,

1.66.s:
vyāsādayo vanasthāśca bhikṣuḥ pañcaśikhastathā .
sarve3 te yogamāsthāya praviṣṭāḥ sūryamaṇḍalam . . 59
1.66.d:
व्यासादयो वनस्थाश्च भिक्षुः पञ्चशिखस्तथा ।
सर्वे3 ते योगमास्थाय प्रविष्टाः सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥ 59
1.66.m: forest-dwellers such as Vyāsa, and likewise the mendicant Pañcaśikha— / all of them, resorting to yoga, entered the orb of the sun.

1.66.s:
śuko vyāsātmajaḥ śrīmānyogadharmamavāpya tu .
ādityakiraṇānpītvā na punarbhavamāntavān . . 1.66.60
1.66.d:
शुको व्यासात्मजः श्रीमान्योगधर्ममवाप्य तु ।
आदित्यकिरणान्पीत्वा न पुनर्भवमान्तवान् ॥ 1.66.60
1.66.m: Vyāsa’s illustrious son Śuka, having attained the practice of yoga, / drank the rays of the sun and did not undergo rebirth.

1.66.s:
śabdamātrāḥ śrutisukhā brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ .
pratyakṣo'yaṃ smṛto devaḥ sūryastimiranāśanaḥ . . 61
1.66.d:
शब्दमात्राः श्रुतिसुखा ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादयः ।
प्रत्यक्षोऽयं स्मृतो देवः सूर्यस्तिमिरनाशनः ॥ 61
1.66.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest are merely words pleasing to the ear; / this sun, the destroyer of darkness, is regarded as the god manifest to perception.

1.66.s:
tasmādanyavrate bhaktirna kāryā śubhamicchatā .
hṛṣṭena sādhyate yasmādadṛṣṭaṃ nityameva hi . .
tvayātaḥ satataṃ vipra arcanīyo divākaraḥ . . 62
1.66.d:
तस्मादन्यव्रते भक्तिर्न कार्या शुभमिच्छता ।
हृष्टेन साध्यते यस्माददृष्टं नित्यमेव हि ॥
त्वयातः सततं विप्र अर्चनीयो दिवाकरः ॥ 62
1.66.m: Therefore, one who desires good should not direct devotion to any other observance; / for from what is perceptible, that which is unseen is invariably accomplished. / Hence, O brāhmaṇa, the sun should be worshipped constantly by you.

1.66.s:
yājñavalkya uvāca
aho ya eṣa kathito bhavatā bhāskaro mama .
devatā sarvadevānāṃ naitanmithyā prajāyate . . 63
1.66.d:
याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच
अहो य एष कथितो भवता भास्करो मम ।
देवता सर्वदेवानां नैतन्मिथ्या प्रजायते ॥ 63
1.66.m: Yājñavalkya said: / Ah, this sun described to me by you / is the deity of all gods; this is not false.

1.66.s:
tasya devasya māhātmyaṃ śrutaṃ subahuśo mayā .
devarṣisiddhamanujaiḥ stutasyeha mahātmanaḥ . . 64
1.66.d:
तस्य देवस्य माहात्म्यं श्रुतं सुबहुशो मया ।
देवर्षिसिद्धमनुजैः स्तुतस्येह महात्मनः ॥ 64
1.66.m: I have heard very often of the greatness of that god, / of the great-souled one praised here by divine sages, siddhas, and mortals.

1.66.s:
kaḥ stauti daivatamajaṃ yasyaitatsacarācaram .
akṣayasyāprameyasya kiraṇodgamanādbhavet . . 65
1.66.d:
कः स्तौति दैवतमजं यस्यैतत्सचराचरम् ।
अक्षयस्याप्रमेयस्य किरणोद्गमनाद्भवेत् ॥ 65
1.66.m: Who can praise the unborn deity, by the rising of whose rays / this [entire world] with its moving and unmoving beings comes into existence—imperishable and immeasurable?

1.66.s:
dakṣiṇātkiraṇādyasya sambhūto bhagavānhariḥ .
vāmādbhavāṃstathā jātaḥ kiraṇātkila kañjaja . . 66
1.66.d:
दक्षिणात्किरणाद्यस्य सम्भूतो भगवान्हरिः ।
वामाद्भवांस्तथा जातः किरणात्किल कञ्जज ॥ 66
1.66.m: From whose right ray the Lord Hari was born, / and from whose left ray you were born, O lotus-born one;

1.66.s:
lālāṭādyasya rudrastu kā tulyā tena devatā .
tasya devasya kaḥ śaktaḥ pravaktuṃ guṇavistaram . . 67
1.66.d:
लालाटाद्यस्य रुद्रस्तु का तुल्या तेन देवता ।
तस्य देवस्य कः शक्तः प्रवक्तुं गुणविस्तरम् ॥ 67
1.66.m: and from whose forehead Rudra [arose]—what deity is equal to him? / Who is able to recount the full extent of that god's virtues?

1.66.s:
so'hamicchāmi devasya tasya sarvātmanaḥ prabho .
śrotumārādhanaṃ yena nistareyaṃ bhavārṇakam . . 68
1.66.d:
सोऽहमिच्छामि देवस्य तस्य सर्वात्मनः प्रभो ।
श्रोतुमाराधनं येन निस्तरेयं भवार्णकम् ॥ 68
1.66.m: As such, I desire to hear the worship of that god, the universal self, the Lord, / by which I may cross the ocean of mundane existence.

1.66.s:
kenopāyena mantrairvā rahasyaiḥ paricaryayā .
dānairvratopavāsairvā homairjapyairathāpi vā . . 69
1.66.d:
केनोपायेन मन्त्रैर्वा रहस्यैः परिचर्यया ।
दानैर्व्रतोपवासैर्वा होमैर्जप्यैरथापि वा ॥ 69
1.66.m: By what means—by mantras, secret rites, attendance, / gifts, votive observances and fasts, or homas and recitations—

1.66.s:
ārādhitaḥ samastānāṃ kleśānāṃ hānido raviḥ .
śakyaḥ samārādhayituṃ kathaṃ śaṃsa prajāpate . . 1.66.70
1.66.d:
आराधितः समस्तानां क्लेशानां हानिदो रविः ।
शक्यः समाराधयितुं कथं शंस प्रजापते ॥ 1.66.70
1.66.m: is the sun propitiated, who brings the destruction of all afflictions? / How is he to be worshipped? Tell me, O Prajāpati!

1.66.s:
dharmārthakāmasamprāptau puruṣāṇāṃ viceṣṭatām 1 .
janmanyavitathā saikā kriyā yārkaṃ samāśritā . . 71
1.66.d:
धर्मार्थकामसम्प्राप्तौ पुरुषाणां विचेष्टताम् 1 ।
जन्मन्यवितथा सैका क्रिया यार्कं समाश्रिता ॥ 71
1.66.m: Among men striving for the attainment of righteousness, wealth, and pleasure, / the one action that never fails across birth is that which is directed to the sun.

1.66.s:
durgasaṃsārakāṃtāramapāramabhidhāvatām .
ekaḥ sūryanamaskāro muktimārgasya deśakaḥ2 . . 72
1.66.d:
दुर्गसंसारकांतारमपारमभिधावताम् ।
एकः सूर्यनमस्कारो मुक्तिमार्गस्य देशकः2 ॥ 72
1.66.m: For those running through the boundless, impassable wilderness of saṃsāra, / a single salutation to the sun is the guide to the path of liberation.

1.66.s:
so'hamicchāmi taṃ devaṃ saptalokaparāyaṇam .
kālāyanamaśeṣasya1 jagato hadyavasthitam . . 73
1.66.d:
सोऽहमिच्छामि तं देवं सप्तलोकपरायणम् ।
कालायनमशेषस्य1 जगतो हद्यवस्थितम् ॥ 73
1.66.m: As such, I wish to worship that god, the resort of the seven worlds, / the abode of time, dwelling in the heart of the entire universe,

1.66.s:
ārādhayituṃ gopālaṃ graheśamamitaujasam .
śaṅkaraṃ jagato dīpaṃ smṛtamātrāghanāśanam . . 74
1.66.d:
आराधयितुं गोपालं ग्रहेशममितौजसम् ।
शङ्करं जगतो दीपं स्मृतमात्राघनाशनम् ॥ 74
1.66.m: the cowherd, the lord of planets, endowed with immeasurable splendour, / the beneficent one, the lamp of the world, whose mere remembrance destroys sins.

1.66.s:
tamanādyaṃ suraśreṣṭhaṃ prasādayitumicchataḥ .
upadeśapradānena prasādaṃ kartumarhasi . . 75
1.66.d:
तमनाद्यं सुरश्रेष्ठं प्रसादयितुमिच्छतः ।
उपदेशप्रदानेन प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ 75
1.66.m: To me, who desires to propitiate that beginningless supreme among gods, / you ought to grant your favour by imparting instruction.

1.66.s:
tasyaitadvacanaṃ śrutyā bhaktimudvahato ravau .
jagāma paritoṣaṃ sa padmayonirmahātapāḥ . .7 6
brahmovāca
yatpṛcchasi dvijaśreṣṭha sūryasyārādhanaṃ prati .
vratopavāsajapyādi tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu . . 77
1.66.d:
तस्यैतद्वचनं श्रुत्या भक्तिमुद्वहतो रवौ ।
जगाम परितोषं स पद्मयोनिर्महातपाः ॥7 6
ब्रह्मोवाच
यत्पृच्छसि द्विजश्रेष्ठ सूर्यस्याराधनं प्रति ।
व्रतोपवासजप्यादि तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ॥ 77
1.66.m: Hearing these words of his as he manifested devotion to the sun, / the lotus-born one of great austerities became delighted. / Brahmā said: / Regarding the worship of the sun about which you ask, O best of the twice-born, / consisting of votive observances, fasts, recitations, and the like—listen to it here with a single-pointed mind.

1.66.s:
anādi yatparaṃ brahma sarvaheyavivarjitam .
vyāpya yatsarvabhūteṣu sthitaṃ sadasataḥ param . . 78
1.66.d:
अनादि यत्परं ब्रह्म सर्वहेयविवर्जितम् ।
व्याप्य यत्सर्वभूतेषु स्थितं सदसतः परम् ॥ 78
1.66.m: The supreme Brahman, which is without beginning and free from all defects, / having pervaded all beings, abides beyond existence and non-existence.

1.66.s:
pradhānapuṃsoranayoryataḥ kṣobhaḥ pravartate .
nityayorvyāpinoścaiva jagadādau mahātmanoḥ . .79
1.66.d:
प्रधानपुंसोरनयोर्यतः क्षोभः प्रवर्तते ।
नित्ययोर्व्यापिनोश्चैव जगदादौ महात्मनोः ॥79
1.66.m: From whom the agitation of these two, primordial matter and the soul— / eternal, all-pervading, and great—arises at the beginning of the universe;

1.66.s:
tatkṣobhakatvād brahmāṃḍaṃ sṛṣṭerheturnirañjanaḥ .
aheturapi sarvātmā jāyate parameśvaraḥ . . 1.66.80
1.66.d:
तत्क्षोभकत्वाद् ब्रह्मांडं सृष्टेर्हेतुर्निरञ्जनः ।
अहेतुरपि सर्वात्मा जायते परमेश्वरः ॥ 1.66.80
1.66.m: By agitating them, the taintless, supreme Lord, / though himself causeless, becomes the self of all and the cause of the cosmic egg’s creation.

1.66.s:
pradhānapuruṣatvaṃ ca tathaiveśvaralīlayā .
samupaiti tataścaivaṃ brahmatvaṃ chandataḥ prabhuḥ . . 81
1.66.d:
प्रधानपुरुषत्वं च तथैवेश्वरलीलया ।
समुपैति ततश्चैवं ब्रह्मत्वं छन्दतः प्रभुः ॥ 81
1.66.m: And in the same way, through the Lord's play, the master assumes / the state of primordial matter and soul; and then, by his own will, the state of Brahmā.

1.66.s:
tataḥ sthitau pālayitā viṣṇutvaṃ jagataḥ kṣaye .
rudratvaṃ ca jagannāthaḥ svecchayā kurute raviḥ . . 82
1.66.d:
ततः स्थितौ पालयिता विष्णुत्वं जगतः क्षये ।
रुद्रत्वं च जगन्नाथः स्वेच्छया कुरुते रविः ॥ 82
1.66.m: Then, as the protector at the time of preservation, the Lord of the world, the sun, / by his own will assumes the state of Viṣṇu, and at the dissolution of the universe, the state of Rudra.

1.66.s:
tamekamakṣaraṃ dhāma sarvadevanamaskṛtam .
bhedābhedasvarūpaṃ taṃ praṇipatya divākaram . .
3varṇayiṣye'khilaṃ vipra tasyaivārādhanaṃ raveḥ . . 83
1.66.d:
तमेकमक्षरं धाम सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम् ।
भेदाभेदस्वरूपं तं प्रणिपत्य दिवाकरम् ॥
3वर्णयिष्येऽखिलं विप्र तस्यैवाराधनं रवेः ॥ 83
1.66.m: Having bowed to that sun, the one imperishable realm, venerated by all the gods, / whose essential nature is difference and non-difference, / I will describe completely the worship of that very sun, O brāhmaṇa.

1.66.s:
guhyaṃ cāpi tathā tasya bhāskarasya śṛṇuṣva vai .
tuṣṭena hi purā mahyaṃ kathitaṃ bhāskareṇa tu . . 84
brahmayājñavalkyasamvādavarṇanam
1.66.d:
गुह्यं चापि तथा तस्य भास्करस्य शृणुष्व वै ।
तुष्टेन हि पुरा मह्यं कथितं भास्करेण तु ॥ 84
ब्रह्मयाज्ञवल्क्यसम्वादवर्णनम्
1.66.m:
And listen also to the secret of that sun; / for it was formerly told to me by the pleased sun.
Description of the Dialogue between Brahmā and Yājñavalkya

1.67.s:
brahmovāca
prabhāte saṃstuto devo mūrtihetormayā purā .
yajantaṃ cāparaṃ devaṃ bhaktinamraṃ mahāmatiḥ . . 1
1.67.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
प्रभाते संस्तुतो देवो मूर्तिहेतोर्मया पुरा ।
यजन्तं चापरं देवं भक्तिनम्रं महामतिः ॥ 1
1.67.m: Brahmā said: / Formerly, in the morning, the god was praised by me for the sake of [assuming] a form, / and as I worshipped him as the supreme deity, bowing with devotion, he of great intellect,

1.67.s:
pratyakṣatvamatho gatvā rahasyaṃ proktavānmama .
ahaṃ ca kṛtavānpraśnaṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyakṣato ravim . . 2
1.67.d:
प्रत्यक्षत्वमथो गत्वा रहस्यं प्रोक्तवान्मम ।
अहं च कृतवान्प्रश्नं दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यक्षतो रविम् ॥ 2
1.67.m: having become visible, declared the secret to me. / And having beheld the sun visibly, I asked a question:

1.67.s:
vedeṣu1 ca purāṇeṣu sāṅgopāṅgeṣu gīyase .
tvamajaḥ śāśvato dhātā mahābhūtamanuttamam2 . . 3
1.67.d:
वेदेषु1 च पुराणेषु साङ्गोपाङ्गेषु गीयसे ।
त्वमजः शाश्वतो धाता महाभूतमनुत्तमम्2 ॥ 3
1.67.m: "You are sung in the Vedas and in the Purāṇas with their ancillary branches / as unborn, eternal, the creator, and the unexcelled great element.

1.67.s:
pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhūtabhavyaṃ tvayi sarvamidaṃ jagat .
catvāro hyāśramā deva sarve gārhasthyamūlakāḥ . . 4
1.67.d:
प्रतिष्ठितं भूतभव्यं त्वयि सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
चत्वारो ह्याश्रमा देव सर्वे गार्हस्थ्यमूलकाः ॥ 4
1.67.m: All this world, past and future, is established in you. / Indeed, O Lord, all four stages of life are rooted in the householder's life;

1.67.s:
yajante tvāmaharaharnānāmūrtisamāśritāḥ .
pitā mātā hi sarvasya daivataṃ tvaṃ hiṃ śāśvatam . . 5
1.67.d:
यजन्ते त्वामहरहर्नानामूर्तिसमाश्रिताः ।
पिता माता हि सर्वस्य दैवतं त्वं हिं शाश्वतम् ॥ 5
1.67.m: resorting to diverse forms, they sacrifice to you day after day. / For you are the father, the mother of all, and the eternal deity.

1.67.s:
yajase caiva kaṃ devameva cāpi na vidmahe .
kathyatāṃ mama deveśa paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me . . 6
1.67.d:
यजसे चैव कं देवमेव चापि न विद्महे ।
कथ्यतां मम देवेश परं कौतूहलं हि मे ॥ 6
1.67.m: And yet to which deity do you sacrifice? This we do not know. / Tell me, O Lord of gods, for great indeed is my curiosity."

1.67.s:
itthaṃ mayokto bhagavānidaṃ vacanamabravīt .
avācyametadvaktavyamātmaguhyaṃ sanātanam . . 7
1.67.d:
इत्थं मयोक्तो भगवानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
अवाच्यमेतद्वक्तव्यमात्मगुह्यं सनातनम् ॥ 7
1.67.m: Addressed thus by me, the Blessed One spoke these words: / "This secret of the Self, eternal and ineffable, must be spoken.

1.67.s:
tava bhaktimato brahmanvakṣyāmīha yathātatham .
yataḥ sūkṣmamavijñeyamavyaktamacalaṃ dhruvam . . 8
1.67.d:
तव भक्तिमतो ब्रह्मन्वक्ष्यामीह यथातथम् ।
यतः सूक्ष्ममविज्ञेयमव्यक्तमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥ 8
1.67.m: To you who possess devotion, O Brahman, I will declare it truthfully. / That which is subtle, unknowable, unmanifest, immovable, and constant,

1.67.s:
indriyairindriyārthaiśca sarvabhūtaiśca varjitam .
sa hyantarātmā bhūtānāṃ kṣetrajñaśceti kathyate . . 9
1.67.d:
इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थैश्च सर्वभूतैश्च वर्जितम् ।
स ह्यन्तरात्मा भूतानां क्षेत्रज्ञश्चेति कथ्यते ॥ 9
1.67.m: free from sense organs, sense objects, and all beings— / that is indeed the inner Self of beings, and it is called the knower of the field.

1.67.s:
triguṇavyatirikto'sau puruṣaśceti kathyate .
hiraṇyagarbho bhagavānsaiva4 buddhiriti smṛtaḥ . . 1.67.10
1.67.d:
त्रिगुणव्यतिरिक्तोऽसौ पुरुषश्चेति कथ्यते ।
हिरण्यगर्भो भगवान्सैव4 बुद्धिरिति स्मृतः ॥ 1.67.10
1.67.m: Beyond the three guṇas, it is called the Puruṣa; / it is the Blessed One, Hiraṇyagarbha, and is recognized as the intellect.

1.67.s:
mahāniti ca yogeṣu pradhānaśceti kathyate .
sāṃkhye5 ca paṭhyate śāstre nāmabhirbahubhiḥ sadā . . 11
1.67.d:
महानिति च योगेषु प्रधानश्चेति कथ्यते ।
सांख्ये5 च पठ्यते शास्त्रे नामभिर्बहुभिः सदा ॥ 11
1.67.m: It is called the Mahat in yogic teachings, and Pradhāna; / and in the Sāṃkhya treatise it is constantly designated by many names.

1.67.s:
viśvago viśvabhūtaśca viśvātmā viśvasambhavaḥ1 .
dhṛtaṃ caivātmakaṃ yena idaṃ trailokyamātmanā . . 12
1.67.d:
विश्वगो विश्वभूतश्च विश्वात्मा विश्वसम्भवः1 ।
धृतं चैवात्मकं येन इदं त्रैलोक्यमात्मना ॥ 12
1.67.m: It is omnipresent, all-becoming, the self of the universe, and the origin of the universe, / and by it this triad of worlds is upheld in its own nature.

1.67.s:
aśarīraḥ śarīreṣu lipyate na ca karmabhiḥ .
mamāntarātmā tava ca ye cānye dehasaṃjñakāḥ . . 13
1.67.d:
अशरीरः शरीरेषु लिप्यते न च कर्मभिः ।
ममान्तरात्मा तव च ये चान्ये देहसंज्ञकाः ॥ 13
1.67.m: Bodiless among bodies, it is not stained by actions; / it is the inner Self of me, of you, and of whatever else is designated as an embodied being."

1.67.s:
sarveṣāṃ sākṣibhūto'sau2 na karoti na lipyate .
saguṇo nirguṇo viṣṇurjñānagamyo hyasau smṛtaḥ . . 14
1.67.d:
सर्वेषां साक्षिभूतोऽसौ2 न करोति न लिप्यते ।
सगुणो निर्गुणो विष्णुर्ज्ञानगम्यो ह्यसौ स्मृतः ॥ 14
1.67.m:
He is the witness of all; he does not act, nor is he defiled.
With qualities and without qualities, Viṣṇu is indeed remembered as accessible through knowledge.

1.67.s:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādo'sau sarvato'kṣiśiromukhaḥ .
sarvataḥ śrutiyukto'sau sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati . . 15
1.67.d:
सर्वतः पाणिपादोऽसौ सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखः ।
सर्वतः श्रुतियुक्तोऽसौ सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ 15
1.67.m:
His hands and feet are everywhere; his eyes, heads, and faces are on all sides;
Possessed of ears everywhere, he stands encompassing all.

1.67.s:
viśvamūrdhā4 viśvabhujo viśvapādākṣināsikaḥ .
ekaścarati kṣetreṣu svairacārī yathāsukham . . 16
1.67.d:
विश्वमूर्धा4 विश्वभुजो विश्वपादाक्षिनासिकः ।
एकश्चरति क्षेत्रेषु स्वैरचारी यथासुखम् ॥ 16
1.67.m:
Having universal heads, universal arms, universal feet, eyes, and noses,
He wanders alone in the fields, moving at will as he pleases.

1.67.s:
kṣetrāṇyasya śarīrāṇi bījaṃ cāpi śubhāśubham .
tāni vetti sa yogātmā ataḥ kṣetrajña ucyate . .
avyaktake pure śete tenā'sau puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 17
1.67.d:
क्षेत्राण्यस्य शरीराणि बीजं चापि शुभाशुभम् ।
तानि वेत्ति स योगात्मा अतः क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते ॥
अव्यक्तके पुरे शेते तेनाऽसौ पुरुषः स्मृतः ॥ 17

1.67.s:
viśvaṃ bahuvidhaṃ jñeyaṃ sa ca sarvatra vidyate .
tasmātsa bahurūpatvādviśvarūpa iti smṛtaḥ . . 18
1.67.d:
विश्वं बहुविधं ज्ञेयं स च सर्वत्र विद्यते ।
तस्मात्स बहुरूपत्वाद्विश्वरूप इति स्मृतः ॥ 18
1.67.m:
The universe is to be known as manifold, and he is present everywhere;
Therefore, because of having manifold forms, he is remembered as universal-formed (viśvarūpa).

1.67.s:
mahāpuruṣaśabdaṃ hi bibhartyeṣa sanātanaḥ .
sa tu vai vikriyāpannaḥ sṛjatyātmānamātmanā . . 19
1.67.d:
महापुरुषशब्दं हि बिभर्त्येष सनातनः ।
स तु वै विक्रियापन्नः सृजत्यात्मानमात्मना ॥ 19
1.67.m:
Indeed, this eternal one bears the title of Great Spirit (mahāpuruṣa);
And undergoing transformation, he creates himself by himself.

1.67.s:
ākāśātpatitaṃ toyaṃ yāti svādvantaraṃ yathā .
bhūme rasaviśeṣeṇa tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ . . 1.67.20
1.67.d:
आकाशात्पतितं तोयं याति स्वाद्वन्तरं यथा ।
भूमे रसविशेषेण तथा गुणवशात्तु सः ॥ 1.67.20
1.67.m:
Just as water fallen from the sky takes on a different taste
Through the particular essence of the earth, so does he through the influence of the qualities (guṇas).

1.67.s:
eka eva yathā vāyurdehe tiṣṭhati pañcadhā .
ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca tathā tasya na saṃśayaḥ . . 21
1.67.d:
एक एव यथा वायुर्देहे तिष्ठति पञ्चधा ।
एकत्वं च पृथक्त्वं च तथा तस्य न संशयः ॥ 21
1.67.m:
Just as the wind, being one, abides in the body in five ways,
So there is unity and multiplicity in him, without doubt.

1.67.s:
sthānāntaraviśeṣeṇa yathāgnirlabhate parām .
saṃjñāṃ dāvāgrikādyeṣu tathā devo hyasau smṛtaḥ . . 22
1.67.d:
स्थानान्तरविशेषेण यथाग्निर्लभते पराम् ।
संज्ञां दावाग्रिकाद्येषु तथा देवो ह्यसौ स्मृतः ॥ 22
1.67.m:
Just as fire, according to the distinction of different locations,
Obtains a distinct designation, such as forest fire and the like, so indeed is this god remembered.

1.67.s:
yathā dīpasahasrāṇi dīpa ekaḥ prasūyate .
tathā rūpasahasrāṇi sa evaikaḥ prasūyate . . 23
1.67.d:
यथा दीपसहस्राणि दीप एकः प्रसूयते ।
तथा रूपसहस्राणि स एवैकः प्रसूयते ॥ 23
1.67.m:
Just as a single lamp begets thousands of lamps,
So he alone, being one, begets thousands of forms.

1.67.s:
sa yadā budhyatetmānaṃ tadā bhavati kevalaḥ .
ekatvaṃ pralaye cāsya bahutvaṃ syātpravartane . . 24
1.67.d:
स यदा बुध्यतेत्मानं तदा भवति केवलः ।
एकत्वं प्रलये चास्य बहुत्वं स्यात्प्रवर्तने ॥ 24
1.67.m:
When he knows himself, then he becomes solitary;
His is unity at dissolution, and multiplicity at creation.

1.67.s:
nityaṃ hi nāsti jagati bhūtaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam .
ṛte1 tamekamīśānaṃ puruṣaṃ bījasaṃjñitam . . 25
1.67.d:
नित्यं हि नास्ति जगति भूतं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
ऋते1 तमेकमीशानं पुरुषं बीजसंज्ञितम् ॥ 25
1.67.m:
For there is no permanent being in the world, whether immobile or mobile,
Except that one Lord, the spirit (puruṣa) designated as the seed.

1.67.s:
akṣayaścāprameyadhra savargabhra sa ucyate .
tasmādavyaktamutpannaṃ triguṇaṃ sarvakāraṇam . . 26
1.67.d:
अक्षयश्चाप्रमेयध्र सवर्गभ्र स उच्यते ।
तस्मादव्यक्तमुत्पन्नं त्रिगुणं सर्वकारणम् ॥ 26
1.67.m:
He is said to be imperishable, immeasurable, and […];
From him the unmanifest was produced, possessing the three qualities, the cause of all.

1.67.s:
avyaktāvyaktabhāvasthā yā sā prakṛtirucyate .
tāṃ yoniṃ brahmaṇo viddhi yo'sau sadasadātmakaḥ . . 27
1.67.d:
अव्यक्ताव्यक्तभावस्था या सा प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।
तां योनिं ब्रह्मणो विद्धि योऽसौ सदसदात्मकः ॥ 27
1.67.m:
She who abides in the state of the manifest and unmanifest is called nature (prakṛti);
Know her to be the womb of Brahman, which consists of being and non-being.

1.67.s:
nāsti tasmātparo hyanyaḥ sa pitā sa prajāpatiḥ .
ātmā mama sa vijñeyastatastaṃ pūjayāmyaham . . 28
1.67.d:
नास्ति तस्मात्परो ह्यन्यः स पिता स प्रजापतिः ।
आत्मा मम स विज्ञेयस्ततस्तं पूजयाम्यहम् ॥ 28
1.67.m:
There is indeed no other higher than he; he is the father, he is Prajāpati;
He is to be known as my own Self; therefore I worship him.

1.67.s:
svargatāścāpi ye kecittaṃ namasyanti dehinaḥ .
te tatprasādādgacchanti tenādiṣṭāḥ parāṃ gatim . . 29
1.67.d:
स्वर्गताश्चापि ये केचित्तं नमस्यन्ति देहिनः ।
ते तत्प्रसादाद्गच्छन्ति तेनादिष्टाः परां गतिम् ॥ 29
1.67.m:
And whatever embodied beings, having attained heaven, bow to him,
They, directed by him, go to the supreme state through his grace.

1.67.s:
taṃ devāścāsurāścaiva nānāmatasamāśritāḥ3 .
bhaktyā sampūjayantyādyaṃ gatiṃ caiṣāṃ dadāti saḥ . . 1.67.30
1.67.d:
तं देवाश्चासुराश्चैव नानामतसमाश्रिताः3 ।
भक्त्या सम्पूजयन्त्याद्यं गतिं चैषां ददाति सः ॥ 1.67.30
1.67.m:
The gods and the asuras, resorting to various doctrines,
Worship the primeval one with devotion, and he grants them their destination.

1.67.s:
sa hi sarvagataścaiva nirguṇaścāpi kathyate .
evaṃ jñātvā tamātmānaṃ pūjayāmi sanātanam . .
bhāskaraṃ devadeveśaṃ sarvabhūteśamacyutam . . 31
1.67.d:
स हि सर्वगतश्चैव निर्गुणश्चापि कथ्यते ।
एवं ज्ञात्वा तमात्मानं पूजयामि सनातनम् ॥
भास्करं देवदेवेशं सर्वभूतेशमच्युतम् ॥ 31

1.67.s:
brahmovāca
ityuktavānpurā pṛṣṭo mayā devo divākaraḥ .
pūjaya tvaṃ mahātmānaṃ tapantaṃ vipulaṃ tapaḥ . . 32
siddhārthasaptamīvratavarṇanam
1.67.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्युक्तवान्पुरा पृष्टो मया देवो दिवाकरः ।
पूजय त्वं महात्मानं तपन्तं विपुलं तपः ॥ 32
सिद्धार्थसप्तमीव्रतवर्णनम्
1.67.m:
Brahmā said:
Having been questioned by me formerly, the god Divākara spoke thus:
'Worship the Great Self who practices vast ascetic heat.'
Description of the Siddhārthasaptamī Vrata

1.68.s:
brahmovāca
vacmi te paramaṃ devaṃ sarvadevaiśca pūjitam .
ārādhayanti yaṃ devaṃ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ . . 1
1.68.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वच्मि ते परमं देवं सर्वदेवैश्च पूजितम् ।
आराधयन्ति यं देवं ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥ 1
1.68.m:
Brahmā said:
I tell you of the supreme god worshipped by all the gods,
The god whom Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara adore.

1.68.s:
padmākṛtiṃ sadā brahmā nalinairguggulena tu .
vyomarūpaṃ sadā devaṃ mahādevorcate ravim . . 2
1.68.d:
पद्माकृतिं सदा ब्रह्मा नलिनैर्गुग्गुलेन तु ।
व्योमरूपं सदा देवं महादेवोर्चते रविम् ॥ 2
1.68.m:
Brahmā always [worships] the lotus-shaped [god] with lotuses and guggulu;
Mahādeva always worships the Sun, the god whose form is space,

1.68.s:
jātipuṣpairdvijaśreṣṭha dhūpena vijayena tu .
vṛṣaṇaṃ sihlakaṃ vipra śrīkhaṇḍamagarustathā . . 3
1.68.d:
जातिपुष्पैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठ धूपेन विजयेन तु ।
वृषणं सिह्लकं विप्र श्रीखण्डमगरुस्तथा ॥ 3
1.68.m:
With jasmine flowers, O best of the twice-born, and with the incense called Vijaya;
O vipra, [it contains] vṛṣaṇa, olibanum, sandalwood, and agallochum,

1.68.s:
karpūraṃ ca tathā mustā śarkarā satvacā dvija .
ityeṣa vijayo dhūpaḥ svayaṃ devena nirmitaḥ . . 4
1.68.d:
कर्पूरं च तथा मुस्ता शर्करा सत्वचा द्विज ।
इत्येष विजयो धूपः स्वयं देवेन निर्मितः ॥ 4
1.68.m:
As well as camphor, nutgrass, sugar, and cinnamon, O twice-born;
This is the Vijaya incense, fashioned by the god himself.

1.68.s:
keśavaścakrarūpaṃ tu sadā sampūjayedravim .
nīlotpaladalaśyāmo nīlotpalakadambakaiḥ . . 5
1.68.d:
केशवश्चक्ररूपं तु सदा सम्पूजयेद्रविम् ।
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामो नीलोत्पलकदम्बकैः ॥ 5
1.68.m:
Keśava, dark as a blue lotus petal, always worships the Sun
In the form of a discus with heaps of blue lotuses,

1.68.s:
dhūpenāgurusaṃjñena bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
mayā sa pṛṣṭo deveśastasyaivārādhanāya vai . . 6
1.68.d:
धूपेनागुरुसंज्ञेन भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
मया स पृष्टो देवेशस्तस्यैवाराधनाय वै ॥ 6
1.68.m:
With the incense named aguru, endowed with devotion and faith.
That lord of gods was asked by me regarding his worship:

1.68.s:
kāni puṣpāṇi ceṣṭāni sadā bhāskarapūjane .
tena coktāni puṣpāṇi svayaṃ tāni nibodha me . . 7
1.68.d:
कानि पुष्पाणि चेष्टानि सदा भास्करपूजने ।
तेन चोक्तानि पुष्पाणि स्वयं तानि निबोध मे ॥ 7
1.68.m:
'Which flowers are beloved always in the worship of Bhāskara?'
And the flowers spoken of by him—learn them from me yourself.

1.68.s:
mallikāyāstu kusumairbhogavāñjāyate naraḥ .
saubhāgyaṃ puṇḍarīkaiśca bhajatyeva ca śāśvatam . . 8
1.68.d:
मल्लिकायास्तु कुसुमैर्भोगवाञ्जायते नरः ।
सौभाग्यं पुण्डरीकैश्च भजत्येव च शाश्वतम् ॥ 8
1.68.m:
Through the blossoms of the mallikā, a man becomes one who enjoys pleasures;
And through white lotuses, he enjoys lasting good fortune.

1.68.s:
1gandhakuṭajakaiḥ puṣpaiḥ paramaiśvaryamaśnute .
bhavatyakṣayamatyantaṃ nityamarcayato ravim . . 9
1.68.d:
1गन्धकुटजकैः पुष्पैः परमैश्वर्यमश्नुते ।
भवत्यक्षयमत्यन्तं नित्यमर्चयतो रविम् ॥ 9
1.68.m:
Through fragrant kuṭaja blossoms, he attains supreme sovereignty;
For one who continually worships the Sun, it becomes exceedingly imperishable.

1.68.s:
mandārapuṣpaiḥ pūjā tu sarvakuṣṭhavināśinī2 .
bilvapatraiśca kusumairmahatīṃ śriyamaśnute . . 1.68.10
1.68.d:
मन्दारपुष्पैः पूजा तु सर्वकुष्ठविनाशिनी2 ।
बिल्वपत्रैश्च कुसुमैर्महतीं श्रियमश्नुते ॥ 1.68.10
1.68.m:
Worship with mandāra flowers destroys all leprosy,
And with bilva leaves and blossoms, he attains great prosperity.

1.68.s:
arkasrajā bhavatyarthaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ .
pradadyādūpiṇīṃ kanyāmarcito bakulasrajā . . 11
1.68.d:
अर्कस्रजा भवत्यर्थं सर्वकामफलप्रदः ।
प्रदद्यादूपिणीं कन्यामर्चितो बकुलस्रजा ॥ 11
1.68.m:
With a garland of arka [flowers], he bestows wealth and grants the fruits of all desires;
Worshipped with a garland of bakula, he will grant a beautiful maiden.

1.68.s:
kiṃśukairarcito devo na pīḍayati bhāskaraḥ .
pūjito'gastyakusumairānukūlyaṃ prayacchati . . 12
1.68.d:
किंशुकैरर्चितो देवो न पीडयति भास्करः ।
पूजितोऽगस्त्यकुसुमैरानुकूल्यं प्रयच्छति ॥ 12
1.68.m:
Worshipped with kiṃśukas, the god Bhāskara does not afflict [a person];
Worshipped with agastya flowers, he grants favour.

1.68.s:
karavīraistu viprendra sūryasyānucaro bhavet .
tathā 1mudgarapuṣpaiśca samabhyarcya divākaram . . 13
1.68.d:
करवीरैस्तु विप्रेन्द्र सूर्यस्यानुचरो भवेत् ।
तथा 1मुद्गरपुष्पैश्च समभ्यर्च्य दिवाकरम् ॥ 13
1.68.m:
Through karavīras, O chief of vipras, one becomes an attendant of Sūrya;
Likewise, having thoroughly worshipped Divākara with mudgara flowers,

1.68.s:
haṃsayuktena yānena raveḥ sālokyatāṃ vrajet .
śatapuṣpasahasraistu pūṣasālokyatāṃ vrajet . .
bakapuṣpairdvijaśreṣṭha yāti bhānusalokatām . . 14
1.68.d:
हंसयुक्तेन यानेन रवेः सालोक्यतां व्रजेत् ।
शतपुष्पसहस्रैस्तु पूषसालोक्यतां व्रजेत् ॥
बकपुष्पैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठ याति भानुसलोकताम् ॥ 14

1.68.s:
catuḥsamena gandhena samabhyarcya divākaram .
pañcabhūtālayasthānamāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ . . 15
1.68.d:
चतुःसमेन गन्धेन समभ्यर्च्य दिवाकरम् ।
पञ्चभूतालयस्थानमाप्नुयान्नात्र संशयः ॥ 15
1.68.m:
Having worshipped Divākara with the fourfold perfume (catuḥsama),
One attains the abode that is the residence of the five elements; of this there is no doubt.

1.68.s:
devāgāraṃ tu sammārjya bhaktyā yastu pralepayet .
sa rogānmucyate kṣipraṃ dravyalābhaṃ ca vindati . . 16
1.68.d:
देवागारं तु सम्मार्ज्य भक्त्या यस्तु प्रलेपयेत् ।
स रोगान्मुच्यते क्षिप्रं द्रव्यलाभं च विन्दति ॥ 16
1.68.m:
He who sweeps the temple of the god and smears it with devotion
Is quickly freed from diseases and gains wealth.

1.68.s:
tasya cāyatanaṃ bhaktyā gairikeṇopalepayet .
prāpnuyānmahatīṃ lakṣmīṃ rogaiścāpi pramucyate . . 17
1.68.d:
तस्य चायतनं भक्त्या गैरिकेणोपलेपयेत् ।
प्राप्नुयान्महतीं लक्ष्मीं रोगैश्चापि प्रमुच्यते ॥ 17
1.68.m:
And he who smears his temple with red chalk (gairika) with devotion
Obtains great fortune and is also released from diseases.

1.68.s:
aṣṭādaśeha kuṣṭhāni ye cānye vyādhayo nṛṇām .
pralayaṃ yānti te sarve mṛdā yadyupalepayet . . 18
1.68.d:
अष्टादशेह कुष्ठानि ये चान्ये व्याधयो नृणाम् ।
प्रलयं यान्ति ते सर्वे मृदा यद्युपलेपयेत् ॥ 18
1.68.m:
The eighteen types of leprosy here and whatever other illnesses afflict men,
All of them go to destruction if one smears it with clay.

1.68.s:
vilepanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ raktacandanamuttamam .
puṣpāṇāṃ karavīrāṇi praśastāni pracakṣate . . 19
1.68.d:
विलेपनानां सर्वेषां रक्तचन्दनमुत्तमम् ।
पुष्पाणां करवीराणि प्रशस्तानि प्रचक्षते ॥ 19
1.68.m:
Of all ointments, red sandalwood is the best;
Among flowers, karavīras are declared to be commendable.

1.68.s:
nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcidbhāsvatastuṣṭikārakam .
kiṃ tasya na bhavelloke yastvebhiḥ svarcayedravim . . 1.68.20
1.68.d:
नातः परतरं किंचिद्भास्वतस्तुष्टिकारकम् ।
किं तस्य न भवेल्लोके यस्त्वेभिः स्वर्चयेद्रविम् ॥ 1.68.20
1.68.m:
There is nothing higher than this that causes satisfaction to the radiant one;
What would not come to pass in the world for one who truly worships the Sun with these?

1.68.s:
karavīraiḥ pūjayedyo bhāskaraṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ .
sarvakāmasamṛddho'sau sūryakāmamavāpnuyāt . . 21
1.68.d:
करवीरैः पूजयेद्यो भास्करं श्रद्धयान्वितः ।
सर्वकामसमृद्धोऽसौ सूर्यकाममवाप्नुयात् ॥ 21
1.68.m:
He who, endowed with faith, worships Bhāskara with karavīras,
Abundant in all desires, obtains the desire of Sūrya.

1.68.s:
vilepyāyatanaṃ3 yastu kuryānmaṇḍalakaṃ śubham .
sa sūryalokamāsādya modate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ . . 22
1.68.d:
विलेप्यायतनं3 यस्तु कुर्यान्मण्डलकं शुभम् ।
स सूर्यलोकमासाद्य मोदते शाश्वतीः समाः ॥ 22
1.68.m:
He who, having smeared the temple, makes an auspicious maṇḍala
Reaches the world of the Sun and rejoices for eternal years.

1.68.s:
ekenāsya bhavedartho dvābhyāmārogyamaśnute .
tribhiḥ santatyavicchinnā caturbhirbhārgavīṃ4 labhet . . 23
1.68.d:
एकेनास्य भवेदर्थो द्वाभ्यामारोग्यमश्नुते ।
त्रिभिः सन्तत्यविच्छिन्ना चतुर्भिर्भार्गवीं4 लभेत् ॥ 23
1.68.m:
With one, he gains wealth; with two, he obtains health;
With three, unbroken lineage; with four, he obtains Lakṣmī.

1.68.s:
pañcabhirvipulaṃ dhānyaṃ ṣaḍbhirāyurbalaṃ yaśaḥ .
saptamaṇḍalakārī syānmaṃḍalādhipatirnara . . 24
1.68.d:
पञ्चभिर्विपुलं धान्यं षड्भिरायुर्बलं यशः ।
सप्तमण्डलकारी स्यान्मंडलाधिपतिर्नर ॥ 24
1.68.m: With five, abundant grain; with six, longevity, strength, and renown; / one who makes seven maṇḍalas becomes the ruler of a domain.

1.68.s:
āyurdhanasutairyuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate .
ghṛtapradīpadānena cakṣuṣmāñjāyate naraḥ . . 25
1.68.d:
आयुर्धनसुतैर्युक्तः सूर्यलोके महीयते ।
घृतप्रदीपदानेन चक्षुष्माञ्जायते नरः ॥ 25
1.68.m: Endowed with life, wealth, and sons, he is exalted in the world of the sun. / By offering a lamp of ghee, a man becomes endowed with sight.

1.68.s:
kaṭutailapradānena sa śatrūñjayate naraḥ .
tilatailapradānena sūryaloke mahīyate . . 26
1.68.d:
कटुतैलप्रदानेन स शत्रूञ्जयते नरः ।
तिलतैलप्रदानेन सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 26
1.68.m: By offering pungent mustard oil, that man conquers his enemies; / by offering sesame oil, he is exalted in the world of the sun.

1.68.s:
madhūkatailadānena saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ vrajet .
saṃpūjya vidhivaddevaṃ puṣpadhūpādibhirbudhaḥ . . 27
1.68.d:
मधूकतैलदानेन सौभाग्यं परमं व्रजेत् ।
संपूज्य विधिवद्देवं पुष्पधूपादिभिर्बुधः ॥ 27
1.68.m: By offering madhūka oil, he attains supreme good fortune. / Having worshipped the god according to rule with flowers, incense, and the like, the wise man

1.68.s:
yathāśaktyā tataḥ paścānnaivedyaṃ bhaktito nyaset .
puṣpāṇāṃ pravarā jātī dhūpānāṃ vijayaḥ paraḥ . . 28
1.68.d:
यथाशक्त्या ततः पश्चान्नैवेद्यं भक्तितो न्यसेत् ।
पुष्पाणां प्रवरा जाती धूपानां विजयः परः ॥ 28
1.68.m: should then faithfully present a food offering according to his ability. / Among flowers, jasmine is foremost; among incenses, vijaya is supreme;

1.68.s:
gandhānāṃ kuṅkumaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ lepānāṃ raktacandanam .
dīpadāne ghṛtaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naivedye modakaḥ paraḥ . . 29
1.68.d:
गन्धानां कुङ्कुमं श्रेष्ठं लेपानां रक्तचन्दनम् ।
दीपदाने घृतं श्रेष्ठं नैवेद्ये मोदकः परः ॥ 29
1.68.m: among perfumes, saffron is best; among unguents, red sandalwood; / in offering lamps, ghee is best; among food offerings, the modaka sweet is supreme.

1.68.s:
etaistuṣyati deveśaḥ sānnidhyaṃ cādhigacchati .
evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivatkṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam . . 1.68.30
1.68.d:
एतैस्तुष्यति देवेशः सान्निध्यं चाधिगच्छति ।
एवं संपूज्य विधिवत्कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम् ॥ 1.68.30
1.68.m: With these the lord of gods is pleased and grants his presence. / Having worshipped thus according to rule and having performed circumambulation,

1.68.s:
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ devadevaṃ divākaram .
sukhāsīnastataḥ paśyedraverabhimukhe sthitaḥ . . 31
1.68.d:
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं देवदेवं दिवाकरम् ।
सुखासीनस्ततः पश्येद्रवेरभिमुखे स्थितः ॥ 31
1.68.m: bowing with his head to the god, the god of gods, the Day-Maker, / seated comfortably, facing the sun, he should look [upon him].

1.68.s:
ekaṃ siddhārthakaṃ kṛtvā haste pānīyasaṃyutam .
kāmaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā taṃ vāñchitaṃ naraḥ . . 32
1.68.d:
एकं सिद्धार्थकं कृत्वा हस्ते पानीयसंयुतम् ।
कामं यथेष्टं हृदये कृत्वा तं वाञ्छितं नरः ॥ 32
1.68.m: Taking one white mustard seed in his hand, accompanied by water, / placing whatever desire he wishes in his heart, a man

1.68.s:
pibetsatoyaṃ taṃ vipra aspṛṣṭaṃ daśanaiḥ sakṛt .
dvitīyāyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ dvau gṛhītvā tu suvrata . . 33
1.68.d:
पिबेत्सतोयं तं विप्र अस्पृष्टं दशनैः सकृत् ।
द्वितीयायां तु सप्तम्यां द्वौ गृहीत्वा तु सुव्रत ॥ 33
1.68.m: should swallow it with the water at once, unchewed by his teeth, O brāhmaṇa. / But on the second saptamī, taking two, O you of noble vows,

1.68.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ grahītavyāstrayo'pi ca .
jñeyāścaturthyāṃ catvāraḥ pañcamyāṃ pañca eva hi . . 34
1.68.d:
तृतीयायां तु सप्तम्यां ग्रहीतव्यास्त्रयोऽपि च ।
ज्ञेयाश्चतुर्थ्यां चत्वारः पञ्चम्यां पञ्च एव हि ॥ 34
1.68.m: on the third saptamī, three should be taken; / on the fourth, four are to be known, and on the fifth, exactly five.

1.68.s:
ṣaṭ pibeccāpi ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ .
saptamyāṃ saptamāyāṃ tu sapta caiva pibennaraḥ . . 35
1.68.d:
षट् पिबेच्चापि षष्ठ्यां तु इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ।
सप्तम्यां सप्तमायां तु सप्त चैव पिबेन्नरः ॥ 35
1.68.m: On the sixth, he should swallow six; such is this Vedic tradition. / On the seventh saptamī, a man should swallow seven.

1.68.s:
ādau prabhṛti vijñeyo mantro'yamabhimantraṇe .
siddhārthakastvaṃ hi loke sarvatra śrūyase yathā . .
tathā māmapi siddhārthamarthataḥ kurutāṃ raviḥ . . 36
1.68.d:
आदौ प्रभृति विज्ञेयो मन्त्रोऽयमभिमन्त्रणे ।
सिद्धार्थकस्त्वं हि लोके सर्वत्र श्रूयसे यथा ॥
तथा मामपि सिद्धार्थमर्थतः कुरुतां रविः ॥ 36
1.68.m: From the very beginning, this mantra is to be known for consecration: / 'Just as you are renowned everywhere in the world as the white mustard seed (siddhārthaka), / so may the sun make me one whose aims are accomplished (siddhārtha) in truth!'

1.68.s:
tato havirupaspṛśya japaṃ kuryādyathepsitam .
hutāśanaṃ ca juhuyādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā . . 37
1.68.d:
ततो हविरुपस्पृश्य जपं कुर्याद्यथेप्सितम् ।
हुताशनं च जुहुयाद्विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥ 37
1.68.m: Then, having touched sacrificial food, he should perform recitation as desired, / and he should make oblations in the fire according to the rite prescribed by rule.

1.68.s:
evameva parāḥ kāryā saptamyaḥ sapta sarvadā .
ekātprabhṛti kāryā sā sarvadodakasaptamī . . 38
1.68.d:
एवमेव पराः कार्या सप्तम्यः सप्त सर्वदा ।
एकात्प्रभृति कार्या सा सर्वदोदकसप्तमी ॥ 38
1.68.m: In this very manner, the subsequent seven saptamīs are always to be observed; / beginning from one, that water-saptamī is always to be performed.

1.68.s:
ekaṃ toyena sahitaṃ dvau cāpi ghṛtasaṃyutau .
trīṃstathā madhunā sārdhaṃ dadhnā catura eva ca . . 39
1.68.d:
एकं तोयेन सहितं द्वौ चापि घृतसंयुतौ ।
त्रींस्तथा मधुना सार्धं दध्ना चतुर एव च ॥ 39
1.68.m: One accompanied by water, two accompanied by ghee, / three with honey, and four with curds,

1.68.s:
yuktānnapayasā pañca ṣaṭ ca gomayasaṃyutān .
pañcagavyena vai sapta pibetsiddhārthakāndvija . . 1.68.40
1.68.d:
युक्तान्नपयसा पञ्च षट् च गोमयसंयुतान् ।
पञ्चगव्येन वै सप्त पिबेत्सिद्धार्थकान्द्विज ॥ 1.68.40
1.68.m: five accompanied by boiled milk, six mixed with cow dung, / and seven with pañcagavya—a twice-born man should swallow the white mustard seeds.

1.68.s:
anena vidhinā yastu kuryātsarṣapasaptamīm .
bahuputro bahudhanaḥ siddhārthaścāpi sarvadā . . 41
1.68.d:
अनेन विधिना यस्तु कुर्यात्सर्षपसप्तमीम् ।
बहुपुत्रो बहुधनः सिद्धार्थश्चापि सर्वदा ॥ 41
1.68.m: Whoever performs the mustard-seed saptamī according to this rule / has many sons, much wealth, and his aims are always accomplished.

1.68.s:
iha loke naro vipra pretyayāti vibhāvasum .
tasmātsampūjayeddevaṃ vidhinānena bhāskaram . . 42
1.68.d:
इह लोके नरो विप्र प्रेत्ययाति विभावसुम् ।
तस्मात्सम्पूजयेद्देवं विधिनानेन भास्करम् ॥ 42
1.68.m: In this world [he is prosperous], O brāhmaṇa, and having departed, he goes to the sun. / Therefore, one should worship the god, the Day-Maker, according to this rule.

1.68.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
siddhārthasaptamīvratavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 68 .
svapnadarśanavarṇanam
1.68.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
सिद्धार्थसप्तमीव्रतवर्णनं नामाष्टषष्टितमोऽध्यायः । 68 ।
स्वप्नदर्शनवर्णनम्
1.68.m:
Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Siddhārthasaptamī Votive Observance', in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the venerable Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Vision of Dreams

1.69.s:
brahmovāca
saptamyāmuṣito vipraḥ svapnadarśanamucyate .
svapne dṛṣṭe ca saptamyāṃ puruṣo niyatavrataḥ . . 1
1.69.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सप्तम्यामुषितो विप्रः स्वप्नदर्शनमुच्यते ।
स्वप्ने दृष्टे च सप्तम्यां पुरुषो नियतव्रतः ॥ 1
1.69.m: Brahmā said: / The vision of dreams is now told for the brāhmaṇa who fasts on the saptamī. / When a dream is seen on the saptamī by a man firm in his vow,

1.69.s:
samāpya vidhivatsarvaṃ japahomādikaṃ kramāt .
pūjayitvā dineśaṃ tu yathāvibhavamātmanaḥ . . 2
1.69.d:
समाप्य विधिवत्सर्वं जपहोमादिकं क्रमात् ।
पूजयित्वा दिनेशं तु यथाविभवमात्मनः ॥ 2
1.69.m: having completed everything—recitation, oblation, and so on—in order according to rule, / and having worshipped the Lord of Day according to his own means,

1.69.s:
tataḥ śayīta śayane devadevaṃ vicintayan .
samprasupto yadā paśyedudayantaṃ divākaram . . 3
1.69.d:
ततः शयीत शयने देवदेवं विचिन्तयन् ।
सम्प्रसुप्तो यदा पश्येदुदयन्तं दिवाकरम् ॥ 3
1.69.m: he should then lie down upon a bed, meditating upon the god of gods. / When, fully asleep, he sees the rising Day-Maker,

1.69.s:
śakradhvajaṃ tathā candraṃ tasya sarvāḥ samṛddhayaḥ .
dṛśyaṃ janaṃ tathā śaktiṃ1 sragvigoveṇunisvanāḥ . . 4
1.69.d:
शक्रध्वजं तथा चन्द्रं तस्य सर्वाः समृद्धयः ।
दृश्यं जनं तथा शक्तिं1 स्रग्विगोवेणुनिस्वनाः ॥ 4
1.69.m: Indra's banner, or the moon, all kinds of prosperity belong to him. / Seeing people, a lance, a person wearing a garland, a cow, sounds of a flute,

1.69.s:
śvetābjacāmarādarśakanakāsisutodbhavam .
rudhirasya srutiṃ sekaṃ pānaṃ caiśvaryakārakam . . 5
1.69.d:
श्वेताब्जचामरादर्शकनकासिसुतोद्भवम् ।
रुधिरस्य स्रुतिं सेकं पानं चैश्वर्यकारकम् ॥ 5
1.69.m: a white lotus, a chowrie, a mirror, gold, a sword, or the birth of a son; / the flowing, sprinkling, and drinking of blood brings sovereignty.

1.69.s:
śvetāyāḥ pañcapūtāyā darśanaṃ vṛddhikārakam .
prajāpaterghṛtāktasya darśanaṃ putradaṃ smṛtam . . 6
1.69.d:
श्वेतायाः पञ्चपूताया दर्शनं वृद्धिकारकम् ।
प्रजापतेर्घृताक्तस्य दर्शनं पुत्रदं स्मृतम् ॥ 6
1.69.m: The sight of a white woman purified by the five [cow products] brings growth; / the sight of Prajāpati anointed with ghee is traditionally taught to grant sons.

1.69.s:
śastavṛkṣābhirohaśca kṣipramaiśvaryakārakaḥ .
dohanaṃ mahiṣīsiṃhīgodhenūnāṃ svake mukhe . . 7
1.69.d:
शस्तवृक्षाभिरोहश्च क्षिप्रमैश्वर्यकारकः ।
दोहनं महिषीसिंहीगोधेनूनां स्वके मुखे ॥ 7
1.69.m: Climbing an auspicious tree swiftly brings sovereignty. / Milking buffalo cows, lionesses, and milch cows into one's own mouth;

1.69.s:
dhanuṣāṃ ca śarāṇāṃ ca nābhau ca drutanirgatiḥ .
abhihanyātsvayaṃ khādetsiṃhāngā bhujagāṃstathā . . 8
1.69.d:
धनुषां च शराणां च नाभौ च द्रुतनिर्गतिः ।
अभिहन्यात्स्वयं खादेत्सिंहान्गा भुजगांस्तथा ॥ 8
1.69.m: the swift emergence of bows and arrows from one's navel; / that he himself slays and eats lions, cows, and serpents;

1.69.s:
svāṃgaśīrṣaṃ2 hutavahe tasya śrīragrataḥ sthitā .
rājate haimane pātre yo bhuṃkte pāyasaṃ dvijaḥ . . 9
1.69.d:
स्वांगशीर्षं2 हुतवहे तस्य श्रीरग्रतः स्थिता ।
राजते हैमने पात्रे यो भुंक्ते पायसं द्विजः ॥ 9
1.69.m: [placing] the head of his own body into the fire—prosperity stands before him. / If a twice-born man eats milk-rice from a silver or golden vessel,

1.69.s:
padmapatre yathā viprastasya jantorbalaṃ bhavet .
dyūte vāde'tha vā yuddhe vijayo hi sukhāvahaḥ . . 1.69.10
1.69.d:
पद्मपत्रे यथा विप्रस्तस्य जन्तोर्बलं भवेत् ।
द्यूते वादेऽथ वा युद्धे विजयो हि सुखावहः ॥ 1.69.10
1.69.m: or, O brāhmaṇa, on a lotus leaf, strength belongs to that being; / in gambling, debate, or battle, victory indeed brings happiness.

1.69.s:
agnestu grasanaṃ vipra āgreyaṃ vṛddhikārakam .
gātrasya jvalanaṃ vipra śirovedhaśca bhūtaye . . 11
1.69.d:
अग्नेस्तु ग्रसनं विप्र आग्रेयं वृद्धिकारकम् ।
गात्रस्य ज्वलनं विप्र शिरोवेधश्च भूतये ॥ 11
1.69.m: Swallowing fire, O brāhmaṇa, or that relating to Agni, brings growth. / The blazing of one's body, O brāhmaṇa, and the piercing of the head lead to prosperity.

1.69.s:
mālyāmbarāṇāṃ4 yuktānāṃ śastānāṃ śuklapakṣiṇām .
sadā lābhaṃ praśaṃsanti tathā viṣṭhānulepanam . . 12
1.69.d:
माल्याम्बराणां4 युक्तानां शस्तानां शुक्लपक्षिणाम् ।
सदा लाभं प्रशंसन्ति तथा विष्ठानुलेपनम् ॥ 12
1.69.m: They always praise obtaining garlands and garments, auspicious white birds, / and likewise being anointed with feces.

1.69.s:
svāṅgasya kartane kṣepe rathayāne prajāgamaḥ .
nānāśirobāhutā ca hastānāṃ kurute śriyam . . 13
1.69.d:
स्वाङ्गस्य कर्तने क्षेपे रथयाने प्रजागमः ।
नानाशिरोबाहुता च हस्तानां कुरुते श्रियम् ॥ 13
1.69.m: The cutting and casting away of one's own limbs, or riding in a chariot, brings offspring; / having multiple heads, arms, and hands brings fortune.

1.69.s:
agamyāgamanaṃ caiva śokamadhyayanaṃ tathā .
devadvijajanācāryaguruvṛddhatapasvinaḥ . . 14
1.69.d:
अगम्यागमनं चैव शोकमध्ययनं तथा ।
देवद्विजजनाचार्यगुरुवृद्धतपस्विनः ॥ 14
1.69.m: Approaching an unapproachable woman, sorrow, and study; / whatever gods, twice-born people, teachers, elders, and ascetics

1.69.s:
yadyadvadanti tatsarvaṃ satyameva hi nirdiśet .
praśastadarśanaṃ caiva abhiṣeko nṛpaśriyāḥ . . 15
1.69.d:
यद्यद्वदन्ति तत्सर्वं सत्यमेव हि निर्दिशेत् ।
प्रशस्तदर्शनं चैव अभिषेको नृपश्रियाः ॥ 15
1.69.m: speak, all that indeed should be declared as true. / Seeing what is auspicious and anointment with royal splendour:

1.69.s:
syādrājyaṃ śiraśchedena bahudhā sphuṭitena tu .
ruditaṃ harṣasamprāptyai rājyaṃ nigaḍabandhane . . 16
1.69.d:
स्याद्राज्यं शिरश्छेदेन बहुधा स्फुटितेन तु ।
रुदितं हर्षसम्प्राप्त्यै राज्यं निगडबन्धने ॥ 16
1.69.m: kingship results from the severing of one's head, or from its bursting in many ways; / weeping leads to the attainment of joy; kingship results from being bound in fetters.

1.69.s:
turaṅgaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ padmaṃ rājānāṃ śvetakuñjaram .
mahadaiśvaryamāpnoti yobhīkaścādhirohati . . 17
1.69.d:
तुरङ्गं वृषभं पद्मं राजानां श्वेतकुञ्जरम् ।
महदैश्वर्यमाप्नोति योभीकश्चाधिरोहति ॥ 17
1.69.m: A horse, a bull, a lotus, a king, a white elephant— / whoever mounts these fearlessly attains great sovereignty.

1.69.s:
grasamāno grahāṃstārā mahīṃ ca parivartayan .
unmūlayanparvatāṃśca rājyalābhamavāpnuyāt . . 18
1.69.d:
ग्रसमानो ग्रहांस्तारा महीं च परिवर्तयन् ।
उन्मूलयन्पर्वतांश्च राज्यलाभमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 18
1.69.m: Swallowing planets and stars, turning the earth upside down, / and uprooting mountains, one obtains kingship.

1.69.s:
dehānniṣkrāntirantrāṇāṃ tairvā vṛkṣasya veṣṭanam .
pātaḥ samudrasaritāmaiśvaryāṇi sukhāni ca . . 19
1.69.d:
देहान्निष्क्रान्तिरन्त्राणां तैर्वा वृक्षस्य वेष्टनम् ।
पातः समुद्रसरितामैश्वर्याणि सुखानि च ॥ 19
1.69.m: The departure of entrails from the body, or wrapping a tree with them; / falling into oceans and rivers brings sovereignty and pleasures.

1.69.s:
udadhiṃ saritaṃ vāpi tīrtvā pāraṃ prayāti ca .
adriṃ laṅghayateścāpi bhavantyarthajayāyuṣaḥ . . 1.69.20
1.69.d:
उदधिं सरितं वापि तीर्त्वा पारं प्रयाति च ।
अद्रिं लङ्घयतेश्चापि भवन्त्यर्थजयायुषः ॥ 1.69.20
1.69.m: Crossing an ocean or a river and reaching the other side, / and also leaping over a mountain brings wealth, victory, and long life.

1.69.s:
ujjvalā strī viśedaṅkamāśīrvādaparāḥ striyaḥ .
bhavatyarthāgamaḥ śīghraṃ kṛmibhiryadi bhakṣyate . . 21
1.69.d:
उज्ज्वला स्त्री विशेदङ्कमाशीर्वादपराः स्त्रियः ।
भवत्यर्थागमः शीघ्रं कृमिभिर्यदि भक्ष्यते ॥ 21
1.69.m: If a radiant woman enters his lap, or women bestow blessings; / if he is eaten by worms, acquisition of wealth swiftly occurs.

1.69.s:
svapne svapna iti jñātaṃ dṛṣṭaprakathanaṃ tathā .
maṅgalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śubhaṃ darśanameva ca . . 2 2
saṃyogaścaiva maṅgalyairārogyadhanakārakaḥ .
aiśvaryarājyalābhāya yasminsvapna udāhṛtaḥ . . 23
1.69.d:
स्वप्ने स्वप्न इति ज्ञातं दृष्टप्रकथनं तथा ।
मङ्गलानां च सर्वेषां शुभं दर्शनमेव च ॥ 2 2
संयोगश्चैव मङ्गल्यैरारोग्यधनकारकः ।
ऐश्वर्यराज्यलाभाय यस्मिन्स्वप्न उदाहृतः ॥ 23
1.69.m: Recognising a dream as a dream in sleep, and narrating what was seen; / the auspicious sight of all auspicious things / and contact with auspicious objects brings health and wealth; / [such is] the dream declared for the attainment of sovereignty and kingship.

1.69.s:
tairdṛṣṭai rogiṇo rogānmucyante nātra saṃśayaḥ .
na svapnaṃ śobhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā svapyātprātaśca kīrtayet . .
rājabhojakaviprebhyaḥ śucibhyaśca śucirnaraḥ . . 24
1.69.d:
तैर्दृष्टै रोगिणो रोगान्मुच्यन्ते नात्र संशयः ।
न स्वप्नं शोभनं दृष्ट्वा स्वप्यात्प्रातश्च कीर्तयेत् ॥
राजभोजकविप्रेभ्यः शुचिभ्यश्च शुचिर्नरः ॥ 24
1.69.m: When these are seen, sick persons are freed from illness, of this there is no doubt. / Having seen an auspicious dream, one should not sleep [again], and in the morning, a pure man / should recite it to king, Bhojakas, and pure brāhmaṇas.

1.69.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
svapnadarśanavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonasaptatimo'dhyāyaḥ . 69 .
sarṣapasaptamīvarṇanam
1.69.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
स्वप्नदर्शनवर्णनं नामैकोनसप्ततिमोऽध्यायः । 69 ।
सर्षपसप्तमीवर्णनम्
1.69.m:
Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, named ‘Description of Dream Visions,’ in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan, in the Mahāpurāṇa the glorious Bhaviṣya, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of Sarṣapasaptamī.

1.70.s:
brahmovāca
tato madhyāhnasamaye snātaḥ prayatamānasaḥ .
tathaiva devānvidhivatpūjayitvā yathāsukham1 . . 1
1.70.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो मध्याह्नसमये स्नातः प्रयतमानसः ।
तथैव देवान्विधिवत्पूजयित्वा यथासुखम्1 ॥ 1
1.70.m: Brahmā said: / Then at midday, having bathed with a restrained mind, / and having likewise properly worshipped the gods as convenient,

1.70.s:
samyakkṛtajapo maunī naro hutahutāśanaḥ .
niṣkramya devāyatanādbhojakānbhojayettataḥ 1 . . 2
1.70.d:
सम्यक्कृतजपो मौनी नरो हुतहुताशनः ।
निष्क्रम्य देवायतनाद्भोजकान्भोजयेत्ततः 1 ॥ 2
1.70.m: a man, having properly muttered his prayers, keeping silence, having offered oblations into the sacrificial fire, / should step out of the temple and then feed the Bhojakas,

1.70.s:
tathā purāṇaviduṣa itihāsavido dvijān .
tathā vedavidaścaiva divyānbhaumāṃśca suvrata . . 3
1.70.d:
तथा पुराणविदुष इतिहासविदो द्विजान् ।
तथा वेदविदश्चैव दिव्यान्भौमांश्च सुव्रत ॥ 3
1.70.m: as well as twice-born who know the Purāṇas and who know the Itihāsas, / and likewise those who know the Vedas, both celestial and earthly, O you of noble vows.

1.70.s:
raktāni vastrāṇi tathā ca gāvaḥ sugandhamālyādi haviṣyamannam .
payasvinī cāpyatha bhojakāya deyā tathānyatpriyamātmano yat . . 4
1.70.d:
रक्तानि वस्त्राणि तथा च गावः सुगन्धमाल्यादि हविष्यमन्नम् ।
पयस्विनी चाप्यथ भोजकाय देया तथान्यत्प्रियमात्मनो यत् ॥ 4
1.70.m: Red garments, cows, fragrant garlands, and the like, sacrificial food, / and a milch cow are also to be given to the Bhojaka, as well as whatever else is dear to oneself.

1.70.s:
bhavedalābho yadi bhojakānāṃ viprāstadārhanti jayopajīvinaḥ .
ye mantravidbrāhmaṇapāṭhakāśca ye ye'pi sāmādhyayaneṣu yuktāḥ . . 5
1.70.d:
भवेदलाभो यदि भोजकानां विप्रास्तदार्हन्ति जयोपजीविनः ।
ये मन्त्रविद्ब्राह्मणपाठकाश्च ये येऽपि सामाध्ययनेषु युक्ताः ॥ 5
1.70.m: If Bhojakas are not available, then brāhmaṇas living by their wits are worthy, / or those who know mantras and recite the Brāhmaṇas, or whoever are devoted to the study of the Sāmaveda.

1.70.s:
prathamaṃ bhojakā bhojyāḥ purāṇaviduṣaiḥ2 saha .
teṣāmṛte mantravidastathā vedavido dvijāḥ . . 6
1.70.d:
प्रथमं भोजका भोज्याः पुराणविदुषैः2 सह ।
तेषामृते मन्त्रविदस्तथा वेदविदो द्विजाः ॥ 6
1.70.m: First the Bhojakas are to be fed along with the knowers of the Purāṇas; / failing them, the mantra-knowing and Veda-knowing twice-born.

1.70.s:
kṛtvaivaṃ saptamī sapta naro bhaktyā samanvitaḥ .
śraddadhāno'nasūyaśca anantaṃ prāpnuyātsukham 3 . . 7
1.70.d:
कृत्वैवं सप्तमी सप्त नरो भक्त्या समन्वितः ।
श्रद्दधानोऽनसूयश्च अनन्तं प्राप्नुयात्सुखम् 3 ॥ 7
1.70.m: Having observed seven saptamīs in this manner, endowed with devotion, / faithful and free from malice, a man attains endless happiness.

1.70.s:
daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ kṛtānāṃ yatphalaṃ labhet .
tatphalaṃ saptamī2 sapta kṛtvā prāpnoti mānavaḥ . . 8
1.70.d:
दशानामश्वमेधानां कृतानां यत्फलं लभेत् ।
तत्फलं सप्तमी2 सप्त कृत्वा प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥ 8
1.70.m: The fruit that one obtains by performing ten horse-sacrifices, / that fruit a man obtains by observing seven saptamīs.

1.70.s:
duṣprāpaṃ nāsti talloke anayā yanna labhyate .
na ca rogostyasau loke anayā yo na śāmyati . . 9
1.70.d:
दुष्प्रापं नास्ति तल्लोके अनया यन्न लभ्यते ।
न च रोगोस्त्यसौ लोके अनया यो न शाम्यति ॥ 9
1.70.m: There is nothing difficult to attain in that world which is not obtained through this; / nor is there any disease in this world that is not alleviated by it.

1.70.s:
kuṣṭhāni cāpi sarvāṇi durucchedyānyapi dhruvam .
apayānti yathā nāgā garuḍasya bhayārditāḥ . . 1.70.10
1.70.d:
कुष्ठानि चापि सर्वाणि दुरुच्छेद्यान्यपि ध्रुवम् ।
अपयान्ति यथा नागा गरुडस्य भयार्दिताः ॥ 1.70.10
1.70.m: Even all forms of leprosy, though utterly difficult to eradicate, surely / depart like serpents afflicted with fear of Garuḍa.

1.70.s:
vrataniyamatapobhiḥ saptamīḥ saptaevaṃ vidhivadiha hi kṛtvā mānavo dharmaśīlaḥ .
śrutadhanasutabhāgyārogyapuṇyairupeto vrajati tadanulokaṃ śāśvataṃ tigmaraśmeḥ . . 11
1.70.d:
व्रतनियमतपोभिः सप्तमीः सप्तएवं विधिवदिह हि कृत्वा मानवो धर्मशीलः ।
श्रुतधनसुतभाग्यारोग्यपुण्यैरुपेतो व्रजति तदनुलोकं शाश्वतं तिग्मरश्मेः ॥ 11
1.70.m: Having thus duly observed seven saptamīs here with observances, restraints, and austerities, a righteous man, / endowed with sacred learning, wealth, sons, good fortune, health, and merit, goes thereafter to the eternal world of the Hot-Rayed One.

1.70.s:
imaṃ vidhiṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śrutvā kṛtvā ca mānavaḥ .
sahasraraśmiṃ sa viśeṣānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā . . 12
1.70.d:
इमं विधिं द्विजश्रेष्ठ श्रुत्वा कृत्वा च मानवः ।
सहस्ररश्मिं स विशेषान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 12
1.70.m: Having heard this ritual and performed it, O best of twice-born, / a man certainly enters the Thousand-Rayed One; no doubt should be entertained here.

1.70.s:
surairvā munibhirvāpi purāṇajñairidaṃ śrutam .
sarve te paramātmānaṃ pūjayanti divākaram . . 13
1.70.d:
सुरैर्वा मुनिभिर्वापि पुराणज्ञैरिदं श्रुतम् ।
सर्वे ते परमात्मानं पूजयन्ति दिवाकरम् ॥ 13
1.70.m: Whether heard by gods, sages, or knowers of the Purāṇas, / all of them worship the Sun, the Supreme Self.

1.70.s:
idamākhyānamārṣeyaṃ yanmayābhihitaṃ tava .
sūryabhaktāya dātavyaṃ netarāya 1 kadācana . . 14
1.70.d:
इदमाख्यानमार्षेयं यन्मयाभिहितं तव ।
सूर्यभक्ताय दातव्यं नेतराय 1 कदाचन ॥ 14
1.70.m: This narrative revealed by the seers, which I have spoken to you, / should be imparted to a devotee of Sūrya, never to anyone else.

1.70.s:
yaścaitacchrāvayennityaṃ yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnaraḥ .
sa sahasrārciṣaṃ devaṃ praviśennātra saṃśayaḥ . . 15
1.70.d:
यश्चैतच्छ्रावयेन्नित्यं यश्चैतच्छृणुयान्नरः ।
स सहस्रार्चिषं देवं प्रविशेन्नात्र संशयः ॥ 15
1.70.m: And the person who recites this regularly, or who hears it, / enters the God of a Thousand Rays; there is no doubt in this.

1.70.s:
mucyedārtastathā rogācchrutvemāmāditaḥ kathām .
jijñāsurlabhate kāmānbhaktaḥ sūryagatiṃ labhet . . 16
1.70.d:
मुच्येदार्तस्तथा रोगाच्छ्रुत्वेमामादितः कथाम् ।
जिज्ञासुर्लभते कामान्भक्तः सूर्यगतिं लभेत् ॥ 16
1.70.m: An afflicted person is freed from disease upon hearing this story from the beginning; / one seeking knowledge obtains his desires, and a devotee attains the state of Sūrya.

1.70.s:
kṣemeṇa gacchate'dhvānaṃ yastvidaṃ paṭhatedhvani .
yo yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ sa taṃ prāpnoti ca dhruvam . . 17
1.70.d:
क्षेमेण गच्छतेऽध्वानं यस्त्विदं पठतेध्वनि ।
यो यं प्रार्थयते कामं स तं प्राप्नोति च ध्रुवम् ॥ 17
1.70.m: He who recites this on a journey travels the road in safety; / and whatever desire one requests, that one surely attains.

1.70.s:
ekāntabhāvopagata ekānte susamāhitaḥ .
prāpyaitatparamaṃ guhyaṃ bhūtvā sūryavrato naraḥ . . 18
1.70.d:
एकान्तभावोपगत एकान्ते सुसमाहितः ।
प्राप्यैतत्परमं गुह्यं भूत्वा सूर्यव्रतो नरः ॥ 18
1.70.m: Having entered a solitary place, well-composed in solitude, / having received this supreme secret and become devoted to the observance of Sūrya, a man

1.70.s:
prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ .
lagnagarbhā pramucyeta garbhiṇī janayetsutam . . 19
1.70.d:
प्राप्नोति परमं स्थानं भास्करस्य महात्मनः ।
लग्नगर्भा प्रमुच्येत गर्भिणी जनयेत्सुतम् ॥ 19
1.70.m: attains the supreme abode of the magnanimous Bhāskara. / A pregnant woman whose foetus is retained is delivered safely and gives birth to a son;

1.70.s:
vandhyā prasavamāpnoti putrapautrasamanvitam .
evametanmamākhyātaṃ bhāskareṇāmitaujasā . .
mayāpi tava mākhyātaṃ bhaktyā bhānoridaṃ dvija . . 1.70.20
1.70.d:
वन्ध्या प्रसवमाप्नोति पुत्रपौत्रसमन्वितम् ।
एवमेतन्ममाख्यातं भास्करेणामितौजसा ॥
मयापि तव माख्यातं भक्त्या भानोरिदं द्विज ॥ 1.70.20
1.70.m: a barren woman attains childbirth endowed with sons and grandsons. / Thus was this declared to me by Bhāskara of boundless splendour, / and this has been told to you by me out of devotion to Bhānu, O twice-born.

1.70.s:
pūjanīyastvayā bhānuḥ sarvapāpopaśāntaye .
sa hi dhātā4 vidhātā ca sarvasya jagato guruḥ . . 21
1.70.d:
पूजनीयस्त्वया भानुः सर्वपापोपशान्तये ।
स हि धाता4 विधाता च सर्वस्य जगतो गुरुः ॥ 21
1.70.m: Bhānu should be worshipped by you for the appeasement of all sins; / for he is the creator, the ordainer, and the guru of the entire world.

1.70.s:
udyanyaḥ kurute nityaṃ jagadvitimiraṃ karaiḥ .
dvādaśātmā sa deveśaḥ prīyatāṃ te'diteḥ sutaḥ . . 22
1.70.d:
उद्यन्यः कुरुते नित्यं जगद्वितिमिरं करैः ।
द्वादशात्मा स देवेशः प्रीयतां तेऽदितेः सुतः ॥ 22
1.70.m: Rising daily, he makes the universe free of darkness with his rays; / may that lord of gods, twelvefold in nature, the son of Aditi, be pleased with you.

1.70.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
ādityamāhātmye sarṣapasaptamīvarṇanaṃ nāma saptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 70 .
brahmaproktasūryanāmavarṇanam
1.70.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
आदित्यमाहात्म्ये सर्षपसप्तमीवर्णनं नाम सप्ततितमोऽध्यायः । 70 ।
ब्रह्मप्रोक्तसूर्यनामवर्णनम्
1.70.m:
Thus ends the seventieth chapter, named ‘Description of Sarṣapasaptamī,’ in the praise of Āditya, in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan, in the Mahāpurāṇa the glorious Bhaviṣya, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Names of Sūrya Spoken by Brahmā.

1.71.s:
brahmovāca
nāmabhiḥ saṃstuto devo yairarkaḥ parituṣyati .
tāni te kīrtayāmyeṣa yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ . . 1
1.71.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नामभिः संस्तुतो देवो यैरर्कः परितुष्यति ।
तानि ते कीर्तयाम्येष यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥ 1
1.71.m: Brahmā said: / The names by which the god Arka is praised and becomes thoroughly pleased, / these I shall declare to you duly and in order.

1.71.s:
namaḥ sūryāya nityāya ravaye kāryabhānave .
bhāskarāya mataṅgāya mārtaṇḍāya vivasvate . . 2
1.71.d:
नमः सूर्याय नित्याय रवये कार्यभानवे ।
भास्कराय मतङ्गाय मार्तण्डाय विवस्वते ॥ 2
1.71.m: Homage to Sūrya, the eternal, to Ravi, the creator of effects, / to Bhāskara, Mataṅga, Mārtaṇḍa, and Vivasvat.

1.71.s:
ādityāyādidevāya namaste raśmimāline .
divākarāya dīptāya agnaye mihirāya ca . . 3
1.71.d:
आदित्यायादिदेवाय नमस्ते रश्मिमालिने ।
दिवाकराय दीप्ताय अग्नये मिहिराय च ॥ 3
1.71.m: To Āditya, the primordial god, homage to you, the garlanded with rays, / to Divākara, the radiant, to Agni, and to Mihira.

1.71.s:
prabhākarāya mitrāya namaste'ditisambhava .
namo gopataye nityaṃ1 diśāṃ ca pataye namaḥ . .4
1.71.d:
प्रभाकराय मित्राय नमस्तेऽदितिसम्भव ।
नमो गोपतये नित्यं1 दिशां च पतये नमः ॥4
1.71.m: To Prabhākara, to Mitra, homage to you, born of Aditi; / perpetual homage to the lord of rays, and homage to the lord of the directions.

1.71.s:
namo dhātre vidhātre ca aryamṇe varuṇāya ca .
pūṣṇe bhagāya mitrāya parjanyāyāṃśave namaḥ . . 5
1.71.d:
नमो धात्रे विधात्रे च अर्यम्णे वरुणाय च ।
पूष्णे भगाय मित्राय पर्जन्यायांशवे नमः ॥ 5
1.71.m: Homage to the creator and ordainer, to Aryaman and Varuṇa, / to Pūṣan, Bhaga, Mitra, Parjanya, and Aṃśu, homage.

1.71.s:
namo hitakṛte nityaṃ dharmāya tapanāya ca .
haraye2 haritāśvāya viśvasya pataye namaḥ . . 6
1.71.d:
नमो हितकृते नित्यं धर्माय तपनाय च ।
हरये2 हरिताश्वाय विश्वस्य पतये नमः ॥ 6
1.71.m: Homage to the doer of good always, to Dharma, and to the Scorcher, / to Hari, to the one with green horses, homage to the lord of the universe.

1.71.s:
viṣṇave brahmaṇe nityaṃ tryambakāya tathātmane .
namaste saptalokeśa namaste saptasaptaye . . 7
1.71.d:
विष्णवे ब्रह्मणे नित्यं त्र्यम्बकाय तथात्मने ।
नमस्ते सप्तलोकेश नमस्ते सप्तसप्तये ॥ 7
1.71.m: To Viṣṇu, to Brahmā constantly, likewise to Tryambaka and the Self; / homage to you, lord of the seven worlds, homage to you who have seven steeds.

1.71.s:
ekasmai hi namastubhyamekacakrarathāya ca .
jyotiṣāṃ pataye nityaṃ sarvaprāṇabhṛte namaḥ . . 8
1.71.d:
एकस्मै हि नमस्तुभ्यमेकचक्ररथाय च ।
ज्योतिषां पतये नित्यं सर्वप्राणभृते नमः ॥ 8
1.71.m: Homage indeed to you who are one, and who have a one-wheeled chariot; / perpetual homage to the lord of lights, to the supporter of all living beings.

1.71.s:
hitāya sarvabhūtānāṃ śivāyārtiharāya ca .
namaḥ padmaprabodhāya namo vedādimūrtaye . . 9
1.71.d:
हिताय सर्वभूतानां शिवायार्तिहराय च ।
नमः पद्मप्रबोधाय नमो वेदादिमूर्तये ॥ 9
1.71.m: To the benefactor of all beings, to Śiva, and to the remover of afflictions; / homage to the awakener of the lotus, homage to the embodiment of the beginning of the Vedas.

1.71.s:
kādhijāya4 namastubhyaṃ namastārāsutāya ca .
bhīmajāya namastubhyaṃ pāvakāya ca vai namaḥ . . 1.71.10
1.71.d:
काधिजाय4 नमस्तुभ्यं नमस्तारासुताय च ।
भीमजाय नमस्तुभ्यं पावकाय च वै नमः ॥ 1.71.10
1.71.m: Homage to you born from the earth, homage to the son of Tārā; / homage to you born of Bhīma, and homage indeed to the Purifier.

1.71.s:
dhiṣaṇāya5 namonityaṃ namaḥ kṛṣṇāya nityadā .
namo'stvaditiputrāya namo lakṣyāya nityaśaḥ . . 11
1.71.d:
धिषणाय5 नमोनित्यं नमः कृष्णाय नित्यदा ।
नमोऽस्त्वदितिपुत्राय नमो लक्ष्याय नित्यशः ॥ 11
1.71.m: Perpetual homage to Dhiṣaṇa, homage always to Kṛṣṇa; / homage to the son of Aditi, homage always to the goal.

1.71.s:
etānyādityanāmāni mayā proktāni vai purā .
ārādhanāya devasya sarvakāmena suvrata . . 12
1.71.d:
एतान्यादित्यनामानि मया प्रोक्तानि वै पुरा ।
आराधनाय देवस्य सर्वकामेन सुव्रत ॥ 12
1.71.m: These names of Āditya were indeed spoken by me in ancient times / for worshipping the god, with all desires fulfilled, O you of noble vows.

1.71.s:
sāyaṃ prātaḥ śucirbhūtvā yaḥ paṭhetsusamāhitaḥ .
sa prāpnotyakhilānkāmānyathāhaṃ prāptavānpurā . . 13
1.71.d:
सायं प्रातः शुचिर्भूत्वा यः पठेत्सुसमाहितः ।
स प्राप्नोत्यखिलान्कामान्यथाहं प्राप्तवान्पुरा ॥ 13
1.71.m: He who, having become pure, recites them morning and evening with a concentrated mind, / obtains all desires, just as I obtained [them] in ancient times.

1.71.s:
prasādāttasya devasya bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ .
śrīkāmaḥ śriyamāpnoti dharmārthī dharmamāpnuyāt . . 14
1.71.d:
प्रसादात्तस्य देवस्य भास्करस्य महात्मनः ।
श्रीकामः श्रियमाप्नोति धर्मार्थी धर्ममाप्नुयात् ॥ 14
1.71.m: By the grace of that god, the magnanimous Bhāskara, / one who desires fortune attains fortune, and one who seeks righteousness attains righteousness.

1.71.s:
āturo mucyate rogādbaddho mucyeta bandhanāt .
rājyārthī rājyamāpnoti kāmārthī kāmamāpnuyāt . . 15
1.71.d:
आतुरो मुच्यते रोगाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् ।
राज्यार्थी राज्यमाप्नोति कामार्थी काममाप्नुयात् ॥ 15
1.71.m: The afflicted is freed from disease, the bound is freed from bondage; / one who seeks a kingdom attains a kingdom, and one who seeks desire attains desire.

1.71.s:
etajjapyaṃ rahasyaṃ ca saṃdhyopāsanameva ca .
etena japamātreṇa naraḥ pāpātpramucyate . . 16
1.71.d:
एतज्जप्यं रहस्यं च संध्योपासनमेव च ।
एतेन जपमात्रेण नरः पापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 16
1.71.m: This is to be muttered, it is a secret, and it is the twilight adoration itself; / by the mere recitation of this, a man is freed from sin.

1.71.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
brahmaproktasūryanāmavarṇanaṃ nāmaikasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 71 .
durvāsāśāpavisarjanavarṇanam
1.71.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
ब्रह्मप्रोक्तसूर्यनामवर्णनं नामैकसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः । 71 ।
दुर्वासाशापविसर्जनवर्णनम्
1.71.m:
Thus ends the seventy-first chapter, entitled "Description of the Names of the Sun Spoken by Brahmā," in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the Śatārdhasāhasrī Saṃhitā of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Utterance of the Curse by Durvāsas

1.72.s:
sumanturuvāca
itthaṃ brahmavaco yogī śrutvā rājandivākaram .
vyomarūpaṃ samārādhya gataḥ sūryasalokatām . . 1
1.72.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इत्थं ब्रह्मवचो योगी श्रुत्वा राजन्दिवाकरम् ।
व्योमरूपं समाराध्य गतः सूर्यसलोकताम् ॥ 1
1.72.m: Sumantu said: / Having thus heard the words of Brahmā, O king, that yogin worshipped the Maker of Day, / whose form is the sky, and attained the realm of the Sun.

1.72.s:
tathā tvamapi rājendra pūjayitvā vibhāvasum .
gamiṣyasi paraṃ sthānaṃ devānāmapi durlabham . . 2
1.72.d:
तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र पूजयित्वा विभावसुम् ।
गमिष्यसि परं स्थानं देवानामपि दुर्लभम् ॥ 2
1.72.m: So you too, O best of kings, having worshipped the Radiator of Light, / will go to the supreme abode, hard even for the gods to attain.

1.72.s:
śatānīka uvāca
ādyaṃ sthānaṃ raveḥ kutra jambūdvīpe mahāmune .
yatra pūjāṃ vidhānoktāṃ pratigṛhṇātyasau raviḥ . . 3
1.72.d:
शतानीक उवाच
आद्यं स्थानं रवेः कुत्र जम्बूद्वीपे महामुने ।
यत्र पूजां विधानोक्तां प्रतिगृह्णात्यसौ रविः ॥ 3
1.72.m: Śatānīka said: / Where is the first seat of the Sun in Jambūdvīpa, O great sage, / where that Sun receives worship prescribed by the rules?

1.72.s:
sumanturuvāca
sthānāni trīṇi devasya dvīpe'sminbhāskarasya1 tu .
pūrvamindravanaṃ nāma tathā muṇḍīramucyate . . 4
1.72.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
स्थानानि त्रीणि देवस्य द्वीपेऽस्मिन्भास्करस्य1 तु ।
पूर्वमिन्द्रवनं नाम तथा मुण्डीरमुच्यते ॥ 4
1.72.m: Sumantu said: / There are three seats of the divine Sun on this continent: / the first is called Indravana, and likewise Muṇḍīra is mentioned;

1.72.s:
kālapriyaṃ3 tṛtīyaṃ tu triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .
tathānyadapi te vacmi yatpurā brahmaṇoditam . . 5
1.72.d:
कालप्रियं3 तृतीयं तु त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ।
तथान्यदपि ते वच्मि यत्पुरा ब्रह्मणोदितम् ॥ 5
1.72.m: the third is Kālapriya, renowned in the three worlds. / And I shall tell you of yet another, which was spoken of old by Brahmā.

1.72.s:
candrabhāgātaṭe nāmnā puraṃ yatsāmbasaṃjñitam4 .
dvīpesmiñchāśvataṃ sthānaṃ yatra sūryasya nityatā . . 6
1.72.d:
चन्द्रभागातटे नाम्ना पुरं यत्साम्बसंज्ञितम्4 ।
द्वीपेस्मिञ्छाश्वतं स्थानं यत्र सूर्यस्य नित्यता ॥ 6
1.72.m: On the bank of the Candrabhāgā is the city known by the name of Sāmba; / on this continent it is the eternal seat where the Sun is ever present.

1.72.s:
prītyā sāmbasya tatrarko janasyānugrahāya ca .
tatra dvādaśabhāgena mitro maitreṇa cakṣuṣā . . 7
1.72.d:
प्रीत्या साम्बस्य तत्रर्को जनस्यानुग्रहाय च ।
तत्र द्वादशभागेन मित्रो मैत्रेण चक्षुषा ॥ 7
1.72.m: Out of affection for Sāmba, and to bestow grace upon the people, the Sun is there. / There, as Mitra, with his twelfth part, with a friendly eye,

1.72.s:
avalokañjagatsarvaṃ śreyo'rthaṃ tiṣṭhate sadā .
prayuktāṃ vidhivatpūjāṃ gṛhṇāti bhagavānsvayam . . 8
1.72.d:
अवलोकञ्जगत्सर्वं श्रेयोऽर्थं तिष्ठते सदा ।
प्रयुक्तां विधिवत्पूजां गृह्णाति भगवान्स्वयम् ॥ 8
1.72.m: he remains forever, looking upon the entire world for its welfare; / the Lord himself accepts the worship performed according to rule.

1.72.s:
śatānīka uvāca
ko'yaṃ sāmbaḥ sutaḥ kasya kasya prīto divākara .
yasya cāyaṃ sahasrāṃśurvaradaḥ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ7 . . 9
1.72.d:
शतानीक उवाच
कोऽयं साम्बः सुतः कस्य कस्य प्रीतो दिवाकर ।
यस्य चायं सहस्रांशुर्वरदः पुण्यकर्मणः7 ॥ 9
1.72.m: Śatānīka said: / Who is this Sāmba? Whose son is he? With whom was the Maker of Day pleased, / and to which man of meritorious deeds was the Thousand-Rayed one a giver of boons?

1.72.s:
sumanturuvāca
ya ete dvādaśādityā virājante mahābalāḥ .
teṣāṃ yo viṣṇusaṃjñastu sarvalokeṣu viśrutaḥ . . 1.72.10
1.72.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
य एते द्वादशादित्या विराजन्ते महाबलाः ।
तेषां यो विष्णुसंज्ञस्तु सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतः ॥ 1.72.10
1.72.m: Sumantu said: / These twelve Ādityas who shine forth, endowed with great strength— / among them, the one known as Viṣṇu, celebrated in all the worlds,

1.72.s:
ihāsau vāsudevatvamavāpa bhagavānvibhuḥ .
tasmātsāmbaḥ suto jajñe jāmbavatyāṃ mahābalaḥ . . 11
1.72.d:
इहासौ वासुदेवत्वमवाप भगवान्विभुः ।
तस्मात्साम्बः सुतो जज्ञे जाम्बवत्यां महाबलः ॥ 11
1.72.m: the all-pervading Lord attained here the state of Vāsudeva. / From him, a son endowed with great strength, Sāmba, was born to Jāmbavatī.

1.72.s:
sa tu pitrā bhṛśaṃ śaptaḥ kuṣṭharogamavāptavān .
tenāyaṃ sthāpitaḥ sūryaḥ svānāmnā ca puraṃ kṛtam . . 12
1.72.d:
स तु पित्रा भृशं शप्तः कुष्ठरोगमवाप्तवान् ।
तेनायं स्थापितः सूर्यः स्वानाम्ना च पुरं कृतम् ॥ 12
1.72.m: He, severely cursed by his father, contracted the disease of leprosy. / By him this Sun was installed, and a city was founded in his own name.

1.72.s:
śatānīka uvāca
śastaḥ kasminnimitte'sau pitrā caivātmasambhavaḥ8 .
nālpaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ vipra yenāsau śaptavānsutam . . 13
1.72.d:
शतानीक उवाच
शस्तः कस्मिन्निमित्तेऽसौ पित्रा चैवात्मसम्भवः8 ।
नाल्पं हि कारणं विप्र येनासौ शप्तवान्सुतम् ॥ 13
1.72.m: Śatānīka said: / For what reason was he, his own son, cursed by his father? / Indeed, no small cause must it have been for which he cursed his son, O brahmin.

1.72.s:
sumanturuvāca
śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājaṃstasya yacchāpakāraṇam .
durvāsā nāma bhagavānrudrasyāṃśasamudbhavaḥ . . 14
1.72.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
शृणुष्वावहितो राजंस्तस्य यच्छापकारणम् ।
दुर्वासा नाम भगवान्रुद्रस्यांशसमुद्भवः ॥ 14
1.72.m: Sumantu said: / Listen attentively, O king, to the reason for his curse. / The venerable one named Durvāsas, born from a portion of Rudra,

1.72.s:
aṭamānaḥ sa bhagavāṃstrīllokānpracacāra ha .
atha prāpto dvāravatīṃ madhusaṃjñocitāṃ purā . . 15
1.72.d:
अटमानः स भगवांस्त्रील्लोकान्प्रचचार ह ।
अथ प्राप्तो द्वारवतीं मधुसंज्ञोचितां पुरा ॥ 15
1.72.m: that venerable one wandered about, roaming through the three worlds. / Then he arrived at Dvāravatī, formerly fittingly called Madhu.

1.72.s:
tamāgatamṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā sāmbo rūpeṇa garvitaḥ .
piṅgākṣaṃ1 kṣudhitaṃ rūkṣaṃ virūpaṃ sukṛśaṃ tathā . . 16
1.72.d:
तमागतमृषिं दृष्ट्वा साम्बो रूपेण गर्वितः ।
पिङ्गाक्षं1 क्षुधितं रूक्षं विरूपं सुकृशं तथा ॥ 16
1.72.m: Seeing that sage who had arrived—tawny-eyed, hungry, rough, / deformed, and extremely emaciated—Sāmba, arrogant on account of his beauty,

1.72.s:
anukārāspadaṃ cakre darśane gamane tathā .
dṛṣṭvā tasya mukhaṃ sāmbo vakra cakre tathātmanaḥ . . 17
1.72.d:
अनुकारास्पदं चक्रे दर्शने गमने तथा ।
दृष्ट्वा तस्य मुखं साम्बो वक्र चक्रे तथात्मनः ॥ 17
1.72.m: made him an object of mockery in his look and his gait. / Seeing his face, Sāmba made his own crooked,

1.72.s:
mukhaṃ kurukulaśreṣṭha garvito yauvanena tu .
atha kruddho mahātejā durvāsā ṛṣisattamaḥ . . 18
1.72.d:
मुखं कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ गर्वितो यौवनेन तु ।
अथ क्रुद्धो महातेजा दुर्वासा ऋषिसत्तमः ॥ 18
1.72.m: contorting his face, O best of the Kuru lineage, proud in his youth. / Then the supreme sage Durvāsas, of great splendour, became enraged,

1.72.s:
sāmbaṃ covāca bhagavānvidhunvanmukhamātmanaḥ .
yasmādvirūpaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā svātmarūpeṇa garvitaḥ . . 19
1.72.d:
साम्बं चोवाच भगवान्विधुन्वन्मुखमात्मनः ।
यस्माद्विरूपं मां दृष्ट्वा स्वात्मरूपेण गर्वितः ॥ 19
1.72.m: and the venerable one, shaking his face, said to Sāmba: / "Because you, seeing me deformed, proud of your own beauty,

1.72.s:
gamane darśane mahyamanukāraṃ samācaraḥ .
tasmāttu kuṣṭharogitvamacirāttvaṃ gamiṣyasi . . 1.72.20
1.72.d:
गमने दर्शने मह्यमनुकारं समाचरः ।
तस्मात्तु कुष्ठरोगित्वमचिरात्त्वं गमिष्यसि ॥ 1.72.20
1.72.m: have mocked my gait and my look, / therefore you shall shortly fall into the condition of a leper."

1.72.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
sāmbāya durvāsasā śāpavisarjanaṃ nāma dvisattatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 72 .
sāmbakṛtasūryārādhanavarṇanam
1.72.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
साम्बाय दुर्वाससा शापविसर्जनं नाम द्विसत्ततितमोऽध्यायः । 72 ।
साम्बकृतसूर्याराधनवर्णनम्
1.72.m:
Thus ends the seventy-second chapter, entitled "The Utterance of the Curse upon Sāmba by Durvāsas," in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the Śatārdhasāhasrī Saṃhitā of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Worship of the Sun Performed by Sāmba

1.73.s:
sumanturuvāca
etasminneva kāle tu nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ .
brahmaṇo mānasaḥ putrastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ . . 1
1.73.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु नारदो भगवानृषिः ।
ब्रह्मणो मानसः पुत्रस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः ॥ 1
1.73.m: Sumantu said: / At that very time, the venerable sage Nārada, / the mind-born son of Brahmā, renowned in the three worlds,

1.73.s:
sarvalokacaraḥ so'tha aṭamānaḥ samantataḥ .
vāsudevaṃ sa vai draṣṭuṃ nityaṃ dvāravatīṃ purīm . . 2
1.73.d:
सर्वलोकचरः सोऽथ अटमानः समन्ततः ।
वासुदेवं स वै द्रष्टुं नित्यं द्वारवतीं पुरीम् ॥ 2
1.73.m: who moves through all the worlds, wandering everywhere, / in order to see Vāsudeva, constantly to the city of Dvāravatī,

1.73.s:
āyāti ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ krodhano munisattamaḥ .
athāgacchati tasmiṃstu sarve yadukumārakāḥ . . 3
1.73.d:
आयाति ऋषिभिः सार्धं क्रोधनो मुनिसत्तमः ।
अथागच्छति तस्मिंस्तु सर्वे यदुकुमारकाः ॥ 3
1.73.m: that irascible, best of sages would come along with other sages. / When he arrived, all the princes of the Yadu clan,

1.73.s:
pradyumnaprabhṛtayo ye prahvāścāvanatāḥ sthitāḥ .
abhivādyārghyapādyābhyāṃ pūjāṃ cakruḥ samantataḥ . . 4
1.73.d:
प्रद्युम्नप्रभृतयो ये प्रह्वाश्चावनताः स्थिताः ।
अभिवाद्यार्घ्यपाद्याभ्यां पूजां चक्रुः समन्ततः ॥ 4
1.73.m: Pradyumna and the rest, stood bowing low and humbly inclined; / having greeted him with guest-water and foot-water, they paid him homage all around.

1.73.s:
sāmbastvavaśyabhāvitvāttasya śāpasya kāraṇam .
avajñāṃ kurūte nityaṃ nāradasya mahātmanaḥ . . 5
1.73.d:
साम्बस्त्ववश्यभावित्वात्तस्य शापस्य कारणम् ।
अवज्ञां कुरूते नित्यं नारदस्य महात्मनः ॥ 5
1.73.m: Sāmba, however, on account of the inevitability of the cause of his curse, / constantly showed disrespect toward the great-souled Nārada.

1.73.s:
rataḥ krīḍāsu vai nityaṃ rūpayauvanagarvitaḥ .
avinītaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa nāradaḥ . . 6
1.73.d:
रतः क्रीडासु वै नित्यं रूपयौवनगर्वितः ।
अविनीतं तु तं दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास नारदः ॥ 6
1.73.m: Always indulging in sports, he was arrogant because of his beauty and youth. / Seeing him ill-mannered, Nārada reflected:

1.73.s:
asyāhamavinītasya kariṣye vinayaṃ śubham .
evaṃ sañcintayityā tu vāsudevamathābravīt .. . 7
1.73.d:
अस्याहमविनीतस्य करिष्ये विनयं शुभम् ।
एवं सञ्चिन्तयित्या तु वासुदेवमथाब्रवीत् ॥ । 7
1.73.m: "I shall bring about proper discipline for this ill-mannered boy." / Having reflected thus, he then spoke to Vāsudeva:

1.73.s:
imāḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasryaḥ striyo yādavasattama .
sarvāsāṃ hi sadā sāmbe bhāvo deva samāśritaḥ . . 8
1.73.d:
इमाः षोडशसाहस्र्यः स्त्रियो यादवसत्तम ।
सर्वासां हि सदा साम्बे भावो देव समाश्रितः ॥ 8
1.73.m: "These sixteen thousand women, O best of the Yādavas— / the affection of all of them, O lord, is constantly fixed on Sāmba.

1.73.s:
rūpeṇāpratimaḥ sāmbo lokesminsacarācare .
sadā hīcchanti 1tāstasya darśanaṃ cāpi hi striyaḥ . . 9
1.73.d:
रूपेणाप्रतिमः साम्बो लोकेस्मिन्सचराचरे ।
सदा हीच्छन्ति 1तास्तस्य दर्शनं चापि हि स्त्रियः ॥ 9
1.73.m: Sāmba is peerless in beauty in this world with its moving and unmoving beings; / and indeed those women constantly desire the sight of him."

1.73.s:
śrutvaivaṃ nāradādvākyaṃ cintayāmāsa keśavaḥ .
yadetannāradenoktamanyadatra tu kiṃ bhavet . . 1.73.10
1.73.d:
श्रुत्वैवं नारदाद्वाक्यं चिन्तयामास केशवः ।
यदेतन्नारदेनोक्तमन्यदत्र तु किं भवेत् ॥ 1.73.10
1.73.m: Having heard this statement from Nārada, Keśava reflected: / "What has Nārada said here? What else could this be?

1.73.s:
vacanaṃ śrūyate loke cāpalyaṃ strīṣu vidyate .
ślokau cemau purā gītau cittajñairyoṣitāṃ dvijaiḥ . . 11
1.73.d:
वचनं श्रूयते लोके चापल्यं स्त्रीषु विद्यते ।
श्लोकौ चेमौ पुरा गीतौ चित्तज्ञैर्योषितां द्विजैः ॥ 11
1.73.m: A saying is heard in the world: fickleness is found in women. / And these two verses were sung of old by twice-born sages who knew the hearts of women:

1.73.s:
pauṃścalyāccalacittatvānnaiḥsnehyācca svabhāvataḥ .
rakṣitāḥ sarvato hyetā vikurvanti hi bhartṛṣu . . 12
1.73.d:
पौंश्चल्याच्चलचित्तत्वान्नैःस्नेह्याच्च स्वभावतः ।
रक्षिताः सर्वतो ह्येता विकुर्वन्ति हि भर्तृषु ॥ 12
1.73.m: 'Through unchastity, through fickle-mindedness, and through natural cold-heartedness, / even when guarded on all sides, they prove faithless to their husbands.

1.73.s:
naitā rūpaṃ parīkṣante nāsāṃ vayasi niścayaḥ .
surūpaṃ vā virūpaṃ vā pumānityeva bhuñjate . . 13
1.73.d:
नैता रूपं परीक्षन्ते नासां वयसि निश्चयः ।
सुरूपं वा विरूपं वा पुमानित्येव भुञ्जते ॥ 13
1.73.m: They do not inspect beauty, nor do they care about age; / handsome or ugly, they enjoy him simply because he is a man.'"

1.73.s:
manasā cintayanneva kṛṣṇo nāradamabravīt .
na hyahaṃ śraddadhāmyetadyadetadbhāṣitaṃ tvayā . . 14
1.73.d:
मनसा चिन्तयन्नेव कृष्णो नारदमब्रवीत् ।
न ह्यहं श्रद्दधाम्येतद्यदेतद्भाषितं त्वया ॥ 14
1.73.m: Reflecting thus in his mind, Kṛṣṇa said to Nārada: / "I do not believe this that has been spoken by you."

1.73.s:
bruvāṇamevaṃ devaṃ tu nārado vākyamabravīt1 .
tathāhaṃ tatkariṣyāmi yathā śraddhāsyate bhavān . . 15
1.73.d:
ब्रुवाणमेवं देवं तु नारदो वाक्यमब्रवीत्1 ।
तथाहं तत्करिष्यामि यथा श्रद्धास्यते भवान् ॥ 15
1.73.m: To the Lord as he spoke thus, Nārada said these words: / "I shall act in such a way that you will believe it."

1.73.s:
evamuktvā yayau svargaṃ nāradastu yathāgataḥ .
tataḥ katipayāhobhirdvārakāṃ punarabhyagāt . . 16
1.73.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ स्वर्गं नारदस्तु यथागतः ।
ततः कतिपयाहोभिर्द्वारकां पुनरभ्यगात् ॥ 16
1.73.m: Having spoken thus, Nārada went to heaven just as he had come. / Then, after a few days, he came again to Dvārakā.

1.73.s:
tasminnahani devo'pi sahāntaḥpurikairjanaiḥ .
anubhūya jalakrīḍāṃ pānamāsevate rahaḥ . . 17
1.73.d:
तस्मिन्नहनि देवोऽपि सहान्तःपुरिकैर्जनैः ।
अनुभूय जलक्रीडां पानमासेवते रहः ॥ 17
1.73.m: On that day, the Lord too, having enjoyed water-sports / along with the women of the inner apartments, was partaking of drink in private,

1.73.s:
3ramyaraivatakodyāne nānādrumavibhūṣite .
sarvartukusumairnityaṃ vāsite sarvakānane . . 18
1.73.d:
3रम्यरैवतकोद्याने नानाद्रुमविभूषिते ।
सर्वर्तुकुसुमैर्नित्यं वासिते सर्वकानने ॥ 18
1.73.m: in the delightful pleasure-garden of Raivataka, adorned with various trees, / constantly perfumed throughout all its groves with flowers of every season,

1.73.s:
nānājalajaphullābhirdīrghikābhiralaṅkṛte .
haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭe cakravākopaśobhite . . 19
1.73.d:
नानाजलजफुल्लाभिर्दीर्घिकाभिरलङ्कृते ।
हंससारससंघुष्टे चक्रवाकोपशोभिते ॥ 19
1.73.m: adorned with oblong ponds filled with blooming aquatic flowers of many kinds, / resounding with swans and cranes, beautified with cakravāka birds.

1.73.s:
tasminsa ramate devaḥ strībhiḥ parivṛtastadā .
hāranūpurakeyūraraśanādyairvibhūṣaṇaiḥ . . 1.73.20
1.73.d:
तस्मिन्स रमते देवः स्त्रीभिः परिवृतस्तदा ।
